args.doc: Selector from which the info is to be retrieved. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: attribute
args.doc: Requested attribute name.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the state

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Attribute Names
keywords.doc:
Returns all HTML attribute names of an element as a list.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Optionally asserts that the attribute names match the expected values. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

Available assertions:

  • == , != and contains / *= can work with multiple values
  • validate and evaluate only accept one single expected value

Other operators are not allowed.

Example:

Get Attribute Names    [name="readonly_input"]    ==    type    name    value    readonly    # Has exactly these attribute names.
Get Attribute Names    [name="readonly_input"]    contains    disabled    # Contains at least this attribute name.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns all HTML attribute names of an element as a list.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector from which the info is to be retrieved. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the state

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get BoundingBox
keywords.doc:
Gets elements size and location as an object {x: float, y: float, width: float, height: float}.

Alternatively you can select a single attribute of the bounding box by setting the key argument.

If an element is hidden and has no bounding box, the keyword will fail. Depending on the method used to make an element invisible, an element might still have a bounding box which can be retrieved. To allow also hidden elements without a bounding box, set allow_hidden to True, which results in a return value of None in case of no bounding box.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Optionally asserts that the value matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

Example use:

${bounding_box}=    Get BoundingBox    id=element                 # unfiltered
Log                 ${bounding_box}                                 # {'x': 559.09375, 'y': 75.5, 'width': 188.796875, 'height': 18}
${x}=               Get BoundingBox    id=element    x            # filtered
Log                 X: ${x}                                         # X: 559.09375
# Assertions:
Get BoundingBox     id=element         width         >    180
Get BoundingBox     id=element         ALL           validate    value['x'] > value['y']*2

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Gets elements size and location as an object ``{x: float, y: float, width: float, height: float}``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector from which the bounding box shall be retrieved. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: key
args.doc: Optionally filters the returned values. If keys is set to ALL (default) it will return the BoundingBox as Dictionary, otherwise it will just return the single value selected by the key. Note: If a single value is retrieved, an assertion does not need a validate combined with a cast of value.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the assertion

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

args.name: allow_hidden
args.doc: (named only) If True, hidden elements are not causing a failure and will return None. Otherwise a hidden element will fail. Defaults to False.

keywords.name: Get Browser Catalog
keywords.doc:
Returns all browsers, open contexts in them and open pages in these contexts.

See Browser, Context and Page for more information about these concepts.

The data is parsed into a python list containing data representing the open Objects.

keywords.name: Get Browser Ids
keywords.doc:
Returns a list of ids from open browsers. See Browser, Context and Page for more information about Browser and related concepts.

browser Defaults to ALL

  • ALL / ANY Returns all ids as a list.
  • ACTIVE / CURRENT Returns the id of the currently active browser as list.

The ACTIVE browser is a synonym for the CURRENT Browser.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns a list of ids from open browsers. See `Browser, Context and Page` for more information about Browser and related concepts.

args.name: browser
args.doc: The browser to get the ids from. ALL for all open browsers or ACTIVE for the currently active browser.

keywords.name: Get Checkbox State
keywords.doc:
Returns the state of the checkbox found by selector.

Optionally asserts that the state matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

  • CHECKED => True
  • UNCHECKED => False

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Example:

Get Checkbox State    [name=can_send_email]    ==    checked

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns the state of the checkbox found by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector which shall be examined. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: == and != and equivalent are allowed on boolean values. Other operators are not accepted.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Boolean value of expected state. Strings are interpreted as booleans. All strings are ${True} except the following: FALSE, NO, OFF, 0, UNCHECKED, NONE, ${EMPTY} (case-insensitive). Defaults to UNCHECKED.

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Classes
keywords.doc:
Returns all classes of an element as a list.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Optionally asserts that the value matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

Available assertions:

  • == , != and contains / *= can work with multiple values
  • validate and evaluate only accept one single expected value

Other operators are not allowed.

Example:

Get Classes    id=draggable    ==    react-draggable    box    # Element has exactly these class names.
Get Classes    id=draggable    validate    "react-draggable-dragged" not in value    # Element does not contain react-draggable-dragged class.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns all classes of an element as a list.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector from which the info is to be retrieved. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected values for the state

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Client Size
keywords.doc:
Gets elements or pages client size (clientHeight, clientWidth) as object {width: float, height: float}.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Optionally asserts that the value matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

See Get BoundingBox or Get Scroll Size for examples.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Gets elements or pages client size (``clientHeight``, ``clientWidth``) as object {width: float, height: float}.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Optional selector from which the client size shall be retrieved. If no selector is given the client size of the page itself is used (document.scrollingElement). See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: key
args.doc: Optionally filters the returned values. If keys is set to ALL (default) it will return the client size as dictionary, otherwise it will just return the single value selected by the key.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the assertion

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Console Log
keywords.doc:
Returns the console log of the active page.

If assertions are used and fail, this keyword will fail immediately without retrying.

The returned data is a list of log messages.

A log message is a dictionary with the following structure:

[{
  "type": str,
  "text": str,
  "location": {
    "url": str,
    "lineNumber": int,
    "columnNumber": int
  },
  "time": str
}]

Example:

[{
  'type': 'log',
  'text': 'Stuff loaded...',
  'location': {
    'url': 'https://example.com/js/chunk-769742de.6a462276.js',
    'lineNumber': 60,
    'columnNumber': 63771
  },
  'time': '2023-02-05T17:42:52.064Z'
}]

Keys:

Key Description
type One of the following values: log, debug, info, error, warning, dir, dirxml, table, trace, clear, startGroup, startGroupCollapsed, endGroup, assert, profile, profileEnd, count, timeEnd
text The text of the console message.
location.url The URL of the resource that generated this message.
location.lineNumber The line number in the resource that generated this message (0-based).
location.columnNumber The column number in the resource that generated this message (0-based).
time The timestamp of the log message as ISO 8601 string.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns the console log of the active page.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: Optional assertion operator. See Assertions for more information.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Optional expected value. See Assertions for more information.

args.name: message
args.doc: Optional custom message to use on failure. See Assertions for more information.

args.name: full
args.doc: If true, returns the full console log. If false, returns only new entries that were added since last time.

args.name: last
args.doc: If set, returns only the last n entries. Can be an integer for the number of entries or a time period in Robot Framework time format.

keywords.name: Get Context Ids
keywords.doc:
Returns a list of context ids based on the browser selection. See Browser, Context and Page for more information about Context and related concepts.

ALL and ANY are synonyms. ACTIVE and CURRENT are also synonyms.

The ACTIVE context of the ACTIVE Browser is the Current Context.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns a list of context ids based on the browser selection. See `Browser, Context and Page` for more information about Context and related concepts.

args.name: context
args.doc: The context to get the ids from. ALL will return all ids from selected browser(s), ACTIVE for the one active context of each selected browser.

args.name: browser
args.doc: The browser id or selection to get the context ids from. ALL Context ids from all open browsers shall be fetched. ACTIVE Only context ids from the active browser shall be fetched. If a browser id is given and no browser with that id is open, the keyword fails.

keywords.name: Get Cookie
keywords.doc:
Returns information about the cookie named cookie as a Robot Framework dot dictionary or a string.

If return_type is dictionary or dict, then the keyword returns a Robot Framework dot dictionary. The dictionary contains all key value pairs of the cookie. If return_type is string or str, then the keyword returns the cookie as a string in format: name1=value1. The return value contains only the name and value keys of the cookie.

If no cookie is found with the given name, the keyword fails. When several cookies have the same name, for example on different domains, paths or partitions, the keyword returns one of them, and which one is not specified. Use Get Cookies to get all of them, with urls to keep only the cookies that apply to given URLs.

The cookie dictionary contains details about the cookie. Keys available in the dictionary are documented in the table below.

Value Explanation
name The name of the cookie.
value Value of the cookie.
domain Specifies which hosts are allowed to receive the cookie.
path Indicates a URL path that must exist in the requested URL, for example /.
expires Lifetime of a cookie. Returned as a datetime object or None if no valid time is received.
httpOnly When true, the cookie is not accessible via JavaScript.
secure When true, the cookie is only used with HTTPS connections.
sameSite Attribute that lets servers require that a cookie shouldn't be sent with cross-origin requests.
partitionKey Top level site of a partitioned cookie. The key exists only for partitioned cookies.

See playwright documentation for details about each attribute.

Example:

${cookie}=        Get Cookie              Foobar
Should Be Equal   ${cookie.value}           Tidii
Should Be Equal   ${cookie.expires.year}     ${2020}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns information about the cookie named ``cookie`` as a Robot Framework dot dictionary or a string.

args.name: cookie
args.doc: Name of the cookie to be retrieved.

args.name: return_type
args.doc: Type of the return value. Can be either dictionary or string. Defaults to dictionary.

keywords.name: Get Cookies
keywords.doc:
Returns cookies from the currently active browser context.

If return_type is dictionary or dict, then the keyword returns a list of Robot Framework dot dictionaries. Each dictionary contains all key value pairs of the cookie. See the Get Cookie keyword documentation for details about the dictionary keys and values.

If return_type is string or str, then the keyword returns the cookies as a string in format: name1=value1; name2=value2; name3=value3. The return value contains only name and value keys of the cookies. If no cookies are found, an empty list is returned.

Example:

${cookies} =    Get Cookies    urls=https://api.example.com/v1
${cookies} =    Get Cookies    string    urls=${list_of_urls}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns cookies from the currently active browser context.

args.name: return_type
args.doc: Type of the return value. Can be either dictionary or string. Defaults to dictionary.

args.name: urls
args.doc: A URL or a list of URLs. When given, only the cookies that apply to at least one of the URLs are returned: the domain and the path of the cookie must match the URL, and a secure cookie is returned only for an HTTPS or a local URL. Defaults to None, which returns all cookies of the context. An empty string or an empty list applies no filter and also returns all cookies.

keywords.name: Get Credential
keywords.doc:
Returns the credential matching the given id and/or rpId.

At least one of id_ and rpId must be given, otherwise the keyword fails. If both are given, the credential must match both of them. When more than one credential matches, the first match is returned. When no credential matches, the keyword fails.

The returned credential is a dictionary with the following keys:

Key Description
id Base64url-encoded credential id.
rpId Relying party id (typically the site's effective domain).
userHandle Base64url-encoded user handle.
privateKey Base64url-encoded PKCS#8 (DER) private key as a Secret.
publicKey Base64url-encoded SPKI (DER) public key as a Secret.

The privateKey and publicKey are wrapped in the Secret type, so that their values are not shown in the Robot Framework log. The values themselves are available in the value attribute. Note that the node side of the library might write the whole credential, including the private key, as plain text to the playwright-log.txt file. See PlaywrightLogTypes for how to control that file.

See Install Credential for more information about how to use this keyword.

Example:

${credential} =    Get Credential    id_=${CREDENTIAL_ID}
Should Be Equal    ${credential["id"]}    ${CREDENTIAL_ID}
Should Be Equal    ${credential["rpId"]}    ${DOMAIN_NAME}
Should Be Equal    ${credential["userHandle"]}    userhandleCreatedByTheApp
Should Be Equal    ${credential["privateKey"].value}    privateKeyCreatedByTheApp
Should Be Equal    ${credential["publicKey"].value}    publicKeyCreatedByTheApp
keywords.shortdoc: Returns the credential matching the given id and/or rpId.

args.name: id_
args.doc: Base64url-encoded credential id.

args.name: rpId
args.doc: Relying party id (typically the site's effective domain).

keywords.name: Get Device
keywords.doc:
Returns a single device descriptor whose name matches name exactly.

The keyword fails if there is no device with that name. The matching is case sensitive.

Allows a concise syntax to set website testing values to exact matches of specific mobile devices.

Use the returned descriptor by passing it to New Context. After creating a context with a device descriptor, make sure that your active page is in that context before using it. Usage:

${device}=          Get Device       iPhone X
New Context         &{device}
New Page
Get Viewport Size   # returns { "width": 375, "height": 812 }

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns a single device descriptor whose name matches ``name`` exactly.

args.name: name
args.doc: Name of the requested device. See Playwright's deviceDescriptorsSource.json for a formatted list.

keywords.name: Get Devices
keywords.doc:
Returns a dictionary of all Playwright device descriptors.

The keys are the device names and the values are the device descriptors themselves.

See Playwright's deviceDescriptorsSource.json for a formatted list.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns a dictionary of all Playwright device descriptors.

keywords.name: Get Download State
keywords.doc:
Gets the state of a download.

Returns a dictionary of type DownloadInfo with the following keys:

{
  saveAs: str
  suggestedFilename: str
  state: str
  downloadID: Optional[str]
}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Gets the state of a download.

args.name: download
args.doc: DownloadInfo dictionary returned from Promise To Wait For Download or download id as string.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected state of the download. Be aware that the returned value is a dictionary

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Element
keywords.doc:
Returns a selector string that points to the element found by selector.

The returned string is the selector Playwright resolved for the element. It is an ordinary selector, so it can be used as the first clause of another selector, chained with >>. Because it is a selector and not a captured DOM node, it is resolved again from the page on every use.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Example:

${element} =    Get Element    \#username_field
${option_value} =    Get Property    ${element} >> optionOne    value    # Locator is resolved from the page.
${option_value} =    Get Property    ${element} >> optionTwo    value    # Locator is resolved again from the page.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns a selector string that points to the element found by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector from which the element shall be retrieved. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

keywords.name: Get Element By
keywords.doc:
Allows locating elements by their features.

Selection strategies can be several Playwright strategies like AltText or Label. See Playwright Locators for more information.

This keywords implements the following Playwright functions:

  • page.getByAltText
  • page.getByLabel
  • page.getByPlaceholder
  • page.getByTestId
  • page.getByText
  • page.getByTitle

page.getByRole is supported by Get Element By Role keyword.

If an element shall be fetched from an iframe, a selector prefix must be set using Set Selector Prefix keyword including >>> as ending.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Allows locating elements by their features.

args.name: selection_strategy
args.doc: SelectionStrategy to be used. Refers to Playwrights page.getBy*** functions. See https://playwright.dev/docs/locators

args.name: text
args.doc: Text to locate the element for.

args.name: exact
args.doc: Whether to find an exact match: case-sensitive and whole-string. Defaults to false. Ignored when locating by a regular expression. Note that exact match still trims whitespace. This has no effect if RegExp is used or if TestID is used as strategy.

args.name: all_elements
args.doc: If True, returns all matched elements as a list.

keywords.name: Get Element By Role
keywords.doc:
Returns a selector string for the element matched by role, or a list of selector strings if all_elements is set to True.

The returned value is used like the one from Get Element: as the first clause of another selector, chained with >>.

Allows locating elements by their ARIA role, ARIA attributes and accessible name.

Consider the following DOM structure.

<h3>Sign up</h3>
<label>
  <input type="checkbox" /> Subscribe
</label>
<br/>
<button>Submit</button>

You can locate each element by its implicit role:

${heading}    Get Element By Role    heading    name=Sign up
${checkbox}   Get Element By Role    checkbox    name=Subscribe
${button}     Get Element By Role    button    name=/submit/i

If an element shall be fetched from an iframe, a selector prefix must be set using Set Selector Prefix keyword including >>> as ending.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns a selector string for the element matched by ``role``, or a list of selector strings if ``all_elements`` is set to ``True``.

args.name: role
args.doc: Role from which shall be retrieved.

args.name: all_elements
args.doc: If True, returns all matched elements as a list.

args.name: checked
args.doc: An attribute that is usually set by aria-checked or native <input type=checkbox> controls.

args.name: disabled
args.doc: An attribute that is usually set by aria-disabled or disabled.

args.name: exact
args.doc: Whether name is matched exactly: case-sensitive and whole-string. Defaults to false. Ignored when name is a regular expression. Note that exact match still trims whitespace.

args.name: expanded
args.doc: An attribute that is usually set by aria-expanded.

args.name: include_hidden
args.doc: Option that controls whether hidden elements are matched. By default, only non-hidden elements, as defined by ARIA, are matched by role selector.

args.name: level
args.doc: A number attribute that is usually present for roles heading, list item, row, treeitem, with default values for <h1>-<h6> elements.

args.name: name
args.doc: Option to match the accessible name. By default, matching is case-insensitive and searches for a substring, use exact to control this behavior.

args.name: pressed
args.doc: An attribute that is usually set by aria-pressed.

args.name: selected
args.doc: An attribute that is usually set by aria-selected.

keywords.name: Get Element Count
keywords.doc:
Returns the count of elements found with selector.

Optionally asserts that the count matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

Example:

Get Element Count    label    >    1

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns the count of elements found with ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector which shall be counted. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the assertion

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Element States
keywords.doc:
Get the active states from the element found by selector.

This Keyword returns a list of states that are valid for the selected element.

Optionally asserts that the state matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default, assertion is not done.

This keyword internally works with Python IntFlag. Flags can be processed using bitwise operators like & (bitwise AND) and | (bitwise OR). When using the assertion operators then, evaluate or validate the value contains the states as ElementState.

Example:

Get Element States    h1    validate    value & visible   # Fails in case of an invisible element
Get Element States    h1    then    value & (visible | hidden)  # Returns either ['visible'] or ['hidden']
Get Element States    h1    then    bool(value & visible)  # Returns ${True} if element is visible

The most typical use case would be to verify if an element contains a specific state or multiple states.

Example:

Get Element States    id=checked_elem      *=    checked
Get Element States    id=checked_elem      not contains    checked
Get Element States    id=invisible_elem    contains    hidden    attached
Get Element States    id=disabled_elem     contains    visible    disabled    readonly

Elements do return the positive and negative values if applicable. As example, a checkbox does return either checked or unchecked while a text input element has none of those two states. Options of select elements have also either selected or deselected.

If an element is not attached to the DOM, so that it can not be found within 250ms, it is marked as detached as the only state.

stable state is not returned, because it would cause too high delay in that keyword.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Get the active states from the element found by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector of the corresponding object. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected states

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

args.name: return_names
args.doc: If set to False the keyword does return an IntFlag object (ElementState) instead of a list. ElementState may contain multiple states at the same time. Defaults to True.

keywords.name: Get Elements
keywords.doc:
Returns a list of selector strings, one for each element matched by selector.

Each string can be used as the first clause of another selector, chained with >>, exactly like the value returned by Get Element.

Keyword does not use strict mode and returns an empty list if the selector does not match any element.

Example:

${elements} =    Get Elements    //select
${elem} =    Get From List    ${elements}    0
${option_value} =    Get Property    ${elem} >> option    value

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns a list of selector strings, one for each element matched by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector from which the elements shall be retrieved. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

keywords.name: Get Page Errors
keywords.doc:
Returns the page errors of the active page.

If assertions are used and fail, this keyword will fail immediately without retrying.

The returned data is a list of error messages.

An error message is a dictionary with the following structure:

{
  "name": str,
  "message": str,
  "stack": str,
  "time": str
}

Example:

[{
  'name': 'ReferenceError',
  'message': 'YT is not defined',
  'stack': 'ReferenceError: YT is not defined\n    at HTMLIFrameElement.onload (https://example.com/:20:2245)',
  'time': '2023-02-05T20:08:48.912Z'
}]

Keys:

Key Description
name The name/type of the error.
message The human readable error message.
stack The stack trace of the error, if given.
time The timestamp of the error as ISO 8601 string.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns the page errors of the active page.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: Optional assertion operator. See Assertions for more information.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Optional expected value. See Assertions for more information.

args.name: message
args.doc: Optional custom message to use on failure. See Assertions for more information.

args.name: full
args.doc: If true, returns all page errors. If false, returns only new errors that were added since last time.

args.name: last
args.doc: If set, returns only the last n entries. Can be an integer for the number of entries or a time period in Robot Framework time format.

keywords.name: Get Page Ids
keywords.doc:
Returns a list of page ids based on the context and browser selection. See Browser, Context and Page for more information about Page and related concepts.

ALL and ANY are synonyms. ACTIVE and CURRENT are also synonyms.

Example:

Test Case
    New Page    https://www.imbus.de
    New Page    https://www.reaktor.com
    ${current_page}=   Get Page IDs    ACTIVE    ACTIVE    ACTIVE
    Log                Current page ID is: ${current_page}[0]
    ${all_pages}=      Get Page IDs    CURRENT   CURRENT   ALL
    Log Many           These are all Page IDs    @{all_pages}

Example to count open pages of a specific context:

Test Case
   New Browser    firefox
   ${context}=    New Context
   New Page    https://www.imbus.de
   New Page    https://www.op.fi
   New Context
   New Page    https://www.robocon.io
   ${page_count}=    Get Page IDs    ALL    ${context}    ALL    then    len(value)
   Should Be Equal As Integers    ${page_count}    2

The ACTIVE page of the ACTIVE context of the ACTIVE Browser is the Current Page.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns a list of page ids based on the context and browser selection. See `Browser, Context and Page` for more information about Page and related concepts.

args.name: page
args.doc: The page to get the ids from. ALL Returns all page ids as a list. ACTIVE Returns the id of the active page as a list.

args.name: context
args.doc: The context id or selection to get the page ids from. ALL Page ids from all contexts shall be fetched. ACTIVE Only page ids from the active context shall be fetched.

args.name: browser
args.doc: The browser id or selection to get the page ids from. ALL Page ids from all open browsers shall be fetched. ACTIVE Only page ids from the active browser shall be fetched.

keywords.name: Get Page Source
keywords.doc:
Gets the page's HTML source as a string.

Optionally does a string assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

If the HTML of a single element is needed, use Get Property instead. Example:

${html1} =    Get Property    ${selector}    innerHTML
${html2} =    Get Property    ${selector}    outerHTML

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Gets the page's HTML source as a string.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the state

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Property
keywords.doc:
Returns the property of the element found by selector.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Optionally asserts that the property value matches the expected value. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

If assertion_operator is set and the property is not found, value is None and the keyword does not fail. If no assertion_operator is set and the property is not found, the keyword fails. See Get Attribute for examples.

Example:

Get Property    h1    innerText    ==    Login Page
${property} =    Get Property    h1    innerText

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns the ``property`` of the element found by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector from which the info is to be retrieved. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: property
args.doc: Requested property name.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the state

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Scroll Position
keywords.doc:
Gets elements or pages current scroll position as object {top: float, left: float, bottom: float, right: float}.

It describes the rectangle which is visible of the scrollable content of that element. All values are measured from position {top: 0, left: 0}.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Optionally asserts that the value matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

See Get BoundingBox or Get Scroll Size for examples.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Gets elements or pages current scroll position as object ``{top: float, left: float, bottom: float, right: float}``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Optional selector from which the scroll position shall be retrieved. If no selector is given the scroll position of the page itself is used (document.scrollingElement). See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: key
args.doc: Optionally filters the returned values. If keys is set to ALL (default) it will return the scroll position as dictionary, otherwise it will just return the single value selected by the key.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the assertion

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Scroll Size
keywords.doc:
Gets elements or pages scrollable size as object {width: float, height: float}.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Optionally asserts that the state matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

See Get BoundingBox for more similar examples.

Example use:

${height}=         Get Scroll Size    height                          # filtered page by height
Log                Height: ${height}                                  # Height: 58425
${scroll_size}=    Get Scroll Size    id=keyword-shortcuts-container  # unfiltered element
Log                ${scroll_size}                                     # {'width': 253, 'height': 3036}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Gets elements or pages scrollable size as object ``{width: float, height: float}``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Optional selector from which the scroll size shall be retrieved. If no selector is given the scroll size of the page itself is used. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: key
args.doc: Optionally filters the returned values. If keys is set to ALL (default) it will return the scroll size as dictionary, otherwise it will just return the single value selected by the key.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the assertion

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Select Options
keywords.doc:
Returns attributes of options of a select element as a list of dictionaries.

Each returned dictionary has the keys "index", "value", "label" and "selected".

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Optionally asserts that these match the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

Example:

Get Select Options     //select[2]    validate  [v["label"] for v in value] == ["Email", "Mobile"]
Get Select Options   select#names     validate  any(v["label"] == "Mikko" for v in value)

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns attributes of options of a ``select`` element as a list of dictionaries.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector from which the info is to be retrieved. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the state

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Selected Options
keywords.doc:
Returns the specified attribute of selected options of the select element.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Optionally asserts that these match the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

  • == , != and contains / *= can work with multiple values
  • validate and evaluate only accept one single expected value

Other operators are not allowed.

Example:

Select Options By      label                    //select[2]    Email      Mobile
${selected_list} =       Get Selected Options   //select[2]                                         # getter
Get Selected Options   //select[2]              label          ==         Mobile             Mail   #assertion content
Select Options By      label                    select#names   2          4
Get Selected Options   select#names             index          ==         2                  4      #assertion index
Get Selected Options   select#names             label          *=         Mikko                     #assertion contain
Get Selected Options   select#names             label          validate   len(value) == 3           #assertion length

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns the specified attribute of selected options of the ``select`` element.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector from which the info is to be retrieved. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: option_attribute
args.doc: Which attribute shall be returned/verified. Defaults to label.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the state

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Style
keywords.doc:
Gets the computed style properties of the element selected by selector.

A pseudo element is a CSS functionality to add styles, for example ::before or ::after.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Optionally asserts that the style matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

When key is ALL, a dictionary is returned and only the sequence assertion operators ==, !=, contains / *=, validate and evaluate / then are allowed. Assertion formatters are not applied in that case.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Gets the computed style properties of the element selected by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector from which the style shall be retrieved. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: key
args.doc: Key of the requested CSS property. Retrieves "ALL" styles as dictionary by default. All css settings can be used as keys even if they are not all returned in the dictionary.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the assertion

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

args.name: pseudo_element
args.doc: Pseudo element to match. Defaults to None.

keywords.name: Get Table Cell Element
keywords.doc:
Returns a selector string for the cell at the same column and row index as the selected elements.

The returned value is used like the one from Get Element.

column and row can also consume index numbers instead of selectors. Indexes are starting from 0 and -1 is specific for the last element.

Selectors for column and row are directly appended to the table selector like this: f"{table} >> {column}" and f"{table} >> {row}".

GitHub Slack Real Name
mkorpela @mkorpela Mikko Korpela
aaltat @aaltat Tatu Aalto
xylix @Kerkko Pelttari Kerkko Pelttari
Snooz82 @René René Rohner

Example:

${table}=    Set Variable    [id="Get Table Cell Element"] >> div.kw-docs table >> nth=1
${e}=    Get Table Cell Element    ${table}    "Real Name"    "aaltat"   # Returns element with text Tatu Aalto
Get Text    ${e}    ==    Tatu Aalto
${e}=    Get Table Cell Element    ${table}    "Slack"    "Mikko Korpela"   # Returns element with text @mkorpela
Get Text    ${e}    ==    @mkorpela
${e}=    Get Table Cell Element    ${table}    "mkorpela"    "Kerkko Pelttari"   # column does not need to be in row 0
Get Text    ${e}    ==    @mkorpela
${e}=    Get Table Cell Element    ${table}    2    -1   # Index is also directly possible
Get Text    ${e}    ==    René Rohner

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns a selector string for the cell at the same column and row index as the selected elements.

args.name: table
args.doc: selector must select the <table> element that contains both selected elements

args.name: column
args.doc: selector can select any <th> or <td> element or one of their descendants.

args.name: row
args.doc: selector can select any <tr> element or one of their descendants like <td> elements.

keywords.name: Get Table Cell Index
keywords.doc:
Returns the index (0 based) of a table cell within its row.

Example:

${table}=    Set Variable    id=Get Table Cell Element >> div.kw-docs table   #Table of keyword Get Table Cell Element
${idx}=    Get Table Cell Index    ${table} >> "Real Name"
Should Be Equal    ${idx}    ${2}
Get Table Cell Index    ${table} >> "@aaltat"    ==    1

Optionally asserts that the index matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns the index (0 based) of a table cell within its row.

args.name: selector
args.doc: can select any <th> or <td> element or one of their descendants. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the assertion

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Table Row Index
keywords.doc:
Returns the index (0 based) of a table row.

Example:

${table}=    Set Variable    id=Get Table Cell Element >> div.kw-docs table   #Table of keyword Get Table Cell Element
${idx}=    Get Table Row Index    ${table} >> "@René"
Should Be Equal    ${idx}    ${4}
Get Table Row Index    ${table} >> "@aaltat"    ==    2

Optionally asserts that the index matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns the index (0 based) of a table row.

args.name: selector
args.doc: can select any <tr>, <th> or <td> element or one of their descendants. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the assertion

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Text
keywords.doc:
Returns text attribute of the element found by selector.

Keyword can also return the value property text of input or textarea elements. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode. The text_type argument determines how text is returned. The allInnerTexts and allTextContents will return a list of strings, while other types return a single string.

Optionally asserts that the text matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default, assertion is not done.

Example:

${text} =    Get Text    id=important                                # Returns element text without assertion.
${text} =    Get Text    id=important    ==    Important text        # Returns element text with assertion.
${text} =    Get Text    //input         ==    root                  # Returns input element text with assertion.
${text} =    Get Text    id=important    text_type=innerHTML         # Returns element inner HTML.
${text} =    Get Text    id=important    text_type=allInnerTexts     # Returns element inner text as list of strings.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns text attribute of the element found by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector from which the text is to be retrieved. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the state

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

args.name: text_type
args.doc: How text is returned. Possible values are allInnerTexts, allTextContents, innerText, inputValue, and innerHTML. Defaults to None, which returns the value of input and textarea elements and the inner text of all other elements.

keywords.name: Get Title
keywords.doc:
Returns the title of the current page.

Optionally asserts that title matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns the title of the current page.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the state

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Url
keywords.doc:
Returns the current URL.

Optionally asserts that it matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns the current URL.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the state

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.

keywords.name: Get Viewport Size
keywords.doc:
Returns the current viewport dimensions.

Optionally asserts that the state matches the specified assertion. See Assertions for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.

If the page does not have a viewport size, for example because the context was created without one, None is returned and no assertion is done.

Example:

Get Viewport Size    ALL    ==    {'width':1280, 'height':720}
Get Viewport Size    width    >=    1200

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns the current viewport dimensions.

args.name: key
args.doc: Optionally filters the returned values. If keys is set to ALL (default) it will return the viewport size as dictionary, otherwise it will just return the single value selected by the key. Note: If a single value is retrieved, an assertion does not need a validate combined with a cast of value.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: See Assertions for further details. Defaults to None.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value for the assertion

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message for assertion.
args.repr: message: str | tuple | dict | None = None

keywords.name: Go Back
keywords.doc:
Navigates to the previous page in history.

If the wait times out, the page's load report is logged: whether its navigation committed, how far the document got and which requests were still open.

Example:

Go To    ${DEEP_LINK}
Go Back    timeout=30s    wait_until=domcontentloaded
Get Url    ==    ${START_URL}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Navigates to the previous page in history.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Time to wait for the navigation. If not defined, the library default timeout is used.

args.name: wait_until
args.doc: When to consider the navigation succeeded, defaults to load. See PageLoadStates for the events: domcontentloaded, load, networkidle or commit.

keywords.name: Go Forward
keywords.doc:
Navigates to the next page in history.

If the wait times out, the page's load report is logged: whether its navigation committed, how far the document got and which requests were still open.

Example:

Go Forward    wait_until=networkidle

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Navigates to the next page in history.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Time to wait for the navigation. If not defined, the library default timeout is used.

args.name: wait_until
args.doc: When to consider the navigation succeeded, defaults to load. See PageLoadStates for the events: domcontentloaded, load, networkidle or commit.

keywords.name: Go To
keywords.doc:
Navigates to the given url.

Returns the HTTP status code of the navigation request as an integer, or 0 if no response was received.

If the wait times out, the page's load report is logged: whether its navigation committed, how far the document got and which requests were still open.

Example:

Go To    ${LANDING_PAGE}    referer=https://partner.example.com/campaign
Get Text    id=referer    ==    https://partner.example.com/campaign

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Navigates to the given ``url``.

args.name: url
args.doc: URL to be navigated to.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Time to wait for the page to load. If not defined, the library default timeout is used.

args.name: wait_until
args.doc: When to consider the operation succeeded, defaults to load. The event can be either: domcontentloaded - consider the operation to be finished when the DOMContentLoaded event is fired. load - consider the operation to be finished when the load event is fired. networkidle - consider the operation to be finished when there are no network connections for at least 500 ms. commit - consider the operation to be finished when the network response is received and the document started loading.

args.name: referer
args.doc: Value of the Referer header sent with this one navigation request. Has no effect when the context or page already sets Referer with extraHTTPHeaders in New Context or with Set Extra HTTP Headers; that value is sent then.

keywords.name: Grant Permissions
keywords.doc:
Grants permissions to the current context.

Example:

New Context
Grant Permissions    geolocation

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Grants permissions to the current context.

args.name: permissions
args.doc: Permissions to grant, given as separate arguments. See Permission for the available values, for example geolocation, notifications, camera or microphone.

args.name: origin
args.doc: The origin to grant the permissions to, e.g. "https://example.com". If not given, the permissions are granted for all origins.

keywords.name: Handle Future Dialogs
keywords.doc:
Handle next dialog on page with action.

The dialog can be an alert, beforeunload, confirm or prompt dialog. This keyword must be called before the action, for example a click, which triggers the dialog.

The handler is registered on the current page and stays in effect for all following dialogs on that page. Calling this keyword again on the same page replaces the handler, so the latest call decides how dialogs are handled.

If a handler is not set, dialogs are dismissed by default.

The handler runs when the dialog appears, not while this keyword executes, so a failure to accept or dismiss the dialog can not be raised as a keyword failure. Such a failure is reported in the playwright-log.txt file only, which is linked into the Robot Framework log when a keyword fails.

Example:

Handle Future Dialogs    action=accept
Click                    \#alerts

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Handle next dialog on page with ``action``.

args.name: action
args.doc: How to handle the alert. Can be accept or dismiss.

args.name: prompt_input
args.doc: The value to enter into the prompt. Only valid if the action argument equals accept. Defaults to an empty string.

keywords.name: Highlight Elements
keywords.doc:
Adds a highlight to elements matched by the selector. Provides a style adjustment.

Returns the number of highlighted elements. Keyword does not fail, if the selector matched zero elements in the page. Keyword does not scroll elements to viewport and highlighted element might be outside the viewport. Use Scroll To Element keyword to scroll element in viewport.

Keyword does not fail if selector resolves to multiple elements.

Highlights which are created with duration=0 stay in the page until they are removed. Calling this keyword with an empty selector, for example Highlight Elements ${EMPTY}, removes all such highlights that were made with Playwright's native highlighting, in other words with mode=playwright or mode=both. Highlights drawn in border mode can not be removed that way.

Example:

Highlight Elements    input#login_button    duration=200ms
${count} =    Highlight Elements    input#login_button    duration=200ms    width=4px    style=solid    color=\#FF00FF
Should Be Equal    ${count}    ${5}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Adds a highlight to elements matched by the ``selector``. Provides a style adjustment.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selectors which shall be highlighted. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: duration
args.doc: Sets for how long the selector shall be highlighted. Defaults to 5s => 5 seconds. If set to 0 seconds, the highlighting is not deleted.

args.name: width
args.doc: Sets the width of the highlight border. Defaults to 2px.

args.name: style
args.doc: Sets the style of the border. Defaults to dotted.

args.name: color
args.doc: Sets the color of the border. Valid colors i.e. are: red, blue, yellow, pink, black

args.name: mode
args.doc: Sets the mode of the highlight. Valid modes are: border (classic mode), playwright (Playwright's native one) and both. Defaults to border. If playwright is used, width, style and color are ignored and only one highlighting can happen at the same time.

keywords.name: Hover
keywords.doc:
Moves the virtual mouse and scrolls to the element found by selector.

This method hovers over an element matching selector by performing the following steps:

  • Find an element matching selector. If there is none, wait until a matching element is attached to the DOM.
  • Wait for actionability checks on the matched element, unless the force option is set. If the element is detached during the checks, the whole action is retried.
  • Scroll the element into view if needed.
  • Use Mouse Move to hover over the center of the element, or the specified position.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Example:

Hover    h1
Hover    h1    10   20    Alt

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Moves the virtual mouse and scrolls to the element found by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector element to hover. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: position_x
args.doc: A point to hover relative to the top-left corner of element bounding box. If not specified, hovers over some visible point of the element. Only positive values within the bounding-box are allowed. Both values must be given, otherwise the position is ignored.

args.name: position_y
args.doc: A point to hover relative to the top-left corner of element bounding box. If not specified, hovers over some visible point of the element. Only positive values within the bounding-box are allowed. Both values must be given, otherwise the position is ignored.

args.name: force
args.doc: Set to True to skip Playwright's Actionability checks. Defaults to False.

args.name: modifiers
args.doc: Modifier keys to press. Ensures that only these modifiers are pressed during the hover, and then restores current modifiers back. If not specified, currently pressed modifiers are used. Valid modifier keys are Alt, Control, ControlOrMeta, Meta and Shift.

keywords.name: Http
keywords.doc:
Sends an HTTP request with the browser's fetch from the active page.

The request is a request of the page itself: a relative url is resolved against the URL of the page, the browser's CORS rules apply, the browser sends the cookies of the context by the credentials rule, and Wait For Request and Wait For Response see it. The browser does not let a page set some headers, such as Cookie, Host or Origin, and drops them without an error.

Use Send API Request instead for a request outside the page, which shares the cookies of the context but not the page's rules, such as CORS.

The named-only arguments are the options of the browser's fetch. An argument that is not given keeps the browser's default.

Give at most one of body, form and multipart. An empty form or multipart dictionary is sent too: as an empty URL-encoded body or a multipart body without parts, as the browser does. The body and the files given as buffer can be at most 4 MiB together; a file given as path does not count.

GET and HEAD requests are sent without a body: a text, JSON, form or multipart body is left out, and a bytes body fails, so that binary data is not dropped unnoticed.

The keyword fails when fetch fails: on a network error, a request CORS blocks, redirect=error on a redirect or a wrong integrity. A response with an error status, such as 404, does not fail it.

Returns an HttpResponse with the status, the headers the page can read, the type of the response, the raw body as bytes and the views text and json. The response is logged without its body, and the body at TRACE level.

Assigned with &{response} =, bytes holds base64 text. Assign with ${response} = to get the raw bytes.

${response} =      HTTP    /api/endpoint
Should Be Equal    ${response.status}            ${200}
Should Be Equal    ${response.json.some_field}   some value

VAR    &{fields} =    username=demo    password=mode
${response} =      HTTP    /login    POST    form=${fields}

VAR    &{file} =    path=${CURDIR}/avatar.png
VAR    &{fields} =    description=Profile picture    file=${file}
${response} =      HTTP    /api/avatar    POST    multipart=${fields}    timeout=30s

${response} =      HTTP    /logo.png
Create Binary File    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/logo.png    ${response.bytes}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Sends an HTTP request with the browser's ``fetch`` from the active page.

args.name: url
args.doc: The request URL, e.g. /api/foo.

args.name: method
args.doc: The HTTP method. Defaults to GET.

args.name: body
args.doc: The request body: text, a Robot Framework Secret, bytes, or a dictionary, a list, a number or a boolean, which is sent as JSON (see JsonSerializable) with the Content-Type application/json. When a text body can be parsed as JSON, the Content-Type is also set to application/json. Other text is sent as text/plain; charset=utf-8, and bytes without a Content-Type, as the browser does, so that a cross-origin request needs no CORS preflight for it. A Content-Type in headers, in any case, always wins.
args.repr: body: JsonSerializable | bytes | Secret | None = None

args.name: headers
args.doc: HttpHeaders (a dictionary) of the request.

args.name: form
args.doc: FormFields (a dictionary), sent URL-encoded as application/x-www-form-urlencoded, the way the browser encodes a URLSearchParams body.

args.name: multipart
args.doc: MultipartFields (a dictionary of text fields and files), sent as multipart/form-data the way the browser encodes a FormData body, in the order given. Do not set a Content-Type in headers: the browser then leaves out the boundary of the parts, and the server cannot read the body.

args.name: credentials
args.doc: Whether cookies and HTTP authentication are sent, see FetchCredentials. The browser's default sends them only to the page's own origin.

args.name: redirect
args.doc: How a redirect is handled, see FetchRedirect.

args.name: mode
args.doc: Which cross-origin requests are allowed, see FetchMode.

args.name: cache
args.doc: How the browser's HTTP cache is used, see FetchCache.

args.name: referrer
args.doc: The URL sent as Referer. It must be on the page's origin, otherwise the browser uses the page URL. about:client is the page URL, an empty string sends none.

args.name: referrerPolicy
args.doc: How much of the referrer is sent, see ReferrerPolicy.

args.name: integrity
args.doc: The expected hash of the response body as a subresource integrity value, e.g. sha256-.... The keyword fails when the body does not match.

args.name: keepalive
args.doc: When True, the request outlives the page, for example when it is closed. The body can be at most 64 KiB.

args.name: priority
args.doc: The priority relative to the page's other requests, see FetchPriority.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: How long to wait for the whole response, body included. Defaults to the library timeout; 0 waits without a limit.

keywords.name: Install Credential
keywords.doc:
Installs the virtual WebAuthn authenticator into the context.

Overrides navigator.credentials.create() and navigator.credentials.get() in all current and future pages of the context. Call this before the page first touches navigator.credentials.

Until the authenticator is installed, no interception is in place and the page sees the platform's native (or absent) WebAuthn behavior. Create Credential installs the authenticator as well, so this keyword is mainly needed when the credentials are created by the application itself. There must be an open context, otherwise the keyword fails.

Example:

New Context
Install Credential
New Page    ${SUT_URL}
# Do something on the page that causes the page to call navigator.credentials.create()
${credential_id} =    Get Credential Id   # This is a user keyword that returns the credential id from somewhere. Talk to your application team to find out how to get the credential id.
${credential} =    Get Credential    id_=${credential_id}    # This will return the credential that was created by the application and installed into the context.
New Context
Create Credential
...    rpId=${DOMAIN_NAME}
...    id_=${credential["id"]}
...    privateKey=${credential["privateKey"]}
...    publicKey=${credential["publicKey"]}
...    userHandle=${credential["userHandle"]}
New Page    ${SUT_URL}
# User should be able to interact with the page using the installed credential.
keywords.shortdoc: Installs the virtual WebAuthn authenticator into the context.

keywords.name: Keyboard Input
keywords.doc:
Input text into page with virtual keyboard.

Attention: Argument type int for 'delay' in milliseconds has been changed to timedelta in Browser 14.0.0. Use Robot Framework time format with units instead.

Note: To press a special key, like Control or ArrowDown, use Keyboard Key. Modifier keys DO NOT affect these actions. For testing modifier effects use single key presses with Keyboard Key press

Example:

Keyboard Input    insertText    0123456789

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Input text into page with virtual keyboard.

args.name: action
args.doc: insertText: Dispatches only input event, does not emit the keydown, keyup or keypress events. type: Sends a keydown, keypress/input, and keyup event for each character in the text.

args.name: input
args.doc: The input string to be typed. No special keys possible.

args.name: delay
args.doc: Time to wait between key presses in Robot Framework's time format. Defaults to 0 ms.

keywords.name: Keyboard Key
keywords.doc:
Press a keyboard key on the virtual keyboard or set a key up or down.

Useful keys for down and up for example are: Shift, Control, Alt, Meta, ShiftLeft

Example execution:

Keyboard Key    press    S
Keyboard Key    press    S        delay=500 ms
Keyboard Key    down     Shift
Keyboard Key    press    ArrowLeft
Keyboard Key    press    Delete
Keyboard Key    up       Shift

Note: Capital letters don't need to be written by the help of Shift. You can type them in directly.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Press a keyboard key on the virtual keyboard or set a key up or down.

args.name: action
args.doc: Determines whether the key should be released (up), held down (down) or pressed once (press). down and up are useful for combinations, i.e. with Shift.

args.name: key
args.doc: The key to be pressed. Examples of valid keys are: F1 - F12, Digit0 - Digit9, KeyA - KeyZ, Backquote, Minus, Equal, Backslash, Backspace, Tab, Delete, Escape, ArrowDown, End, Enter, Home, Insert, PageDown, PageUp, ArrowRight, ArrowUp , etc.

args.name: delay
args.doc: Time the key is held down between keydown and keyup, in Robot Framework's time format. Only valid with action press, other actions raise an error. Defaults to 0 s. Example: 50 ms

keywords.name: Launch Browser Server
keywords.doc:
Launches a new playwright Browser server with specified options.

Returns a websocket endpoint (wsEndpoint) string that can be used to connect to the server.

Check New Browser for the other argument docs.

The launched browser server can be used to connect to it with Connect To Browser keyword. This keyword can also be used from command line with rfbrowser launch-browser-server command.

See Playwright documentation for more information.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Launches a new playwright Browser server with specified options.

args.name: firefoxUserPrefs
args.repr: firefoxUserPrefs: dict[str, str | int | float | bool] | None = None

args.name: port
args.doc: Port to use for the browser server. Defaults to 0, which results in a random free port being assigned.

args.name: wsPath
args.doc: Path at which to serve the browser server. For security, this defaults to an unguessable string.

keywords.name: LocalStorage Clear
keywords.doc:
Remove all saved data from the local storage.

Example:

LocalStorage Set Item    Foo    bar
LocalStorage Clear
${item} =    LocalStorage Get Item    Foo
Should Be Equal    ${item}    ${None}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Remove all saved data from the local storage.

args.name: frame_selector
args.doc: If this selector points to an element inside an iframe, the LocalStorage of that frame is used. Example: iframe[name="test"] >>> body

keywords.name: LocalStorage Get Item
keywords.doc:
Get saved data from the local storage.

See Assertions for further details about the assertion arguments. They default to None.

If the key does not exist in the storage, ${None} is returned.

Example:

LocalStorage Get Item    Key    ==    Value    My error
${value} =    LocalStorage Get Item    Key

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Get saved data from the local storage.

args.name: key
args.doc: Named key of the item in the storage.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: Assertion operator to use. See Assertions for more information.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value to compare with.

args.name: message
args.doc: Custom error message to use.

args.name: frame_selector
args.doc: If this selector points to an element inside an iframe, the LocalStorage of that frame is used. Example: iframe[name="test"] >>> body

keywords.name: LocalStorage Remove Item
keywords.doc:
Remove saved data with key from the local storage.

Example:

LocalStorage Set Item       Foo    bar
LocalStorage Remove Item    Foo
${item} =    LocalStorage Get Item    Foo
Should Be Equal    ${item}    ${None}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Remove saved data with key from the local storage.

args.name: key
args.doc: The name of the item which shall be deleted.

args.name: frame_selector
args.doc: If this selector points to an element inside an iframe, the LocalStorage of that frame is used. Example: iframe[name="test"] >>> body

keywords.name: LocalStorage Set Item
keywords.doc:
Save data to the local storage.

Example:

LocalStorage Set Item    Key    Value

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Save data to the local storage.

args.name: key
args.doc: The name of the key under which it should be saved.

args.name: value
args.doc: The value which shall be saved as a string.

args.name: frame_selector
args.doc: If this selector points to an element inside an iframe, the LocalStorage of that frame is used. Example: iframe[name="test"] >>> body

keywords.name: Merge Coverage Reports
keywords.doc:
Combines multiple raw coverage reports into a single report.

Returns the path to the output_folder.

The input_folder argument is the base folder where the coverage reports are located. The keyword will look into each subfolder and if the subfolder contains a "raw" folder, it will use the data from the "raw" folder for the combined report.

The output_folder argument is the folder where the combined report is saved. If the folder does not exist, it is created. If the folder exists, its content is deleted before the report is created.

The output_folder and input_folder must be full paths to the folders.

The config_file argument is optional and can be used to provide a path to a monocart-coverage-reports options file. If the file is defined but does not exist, the keyword fails. For more details see: https://www.npmjs.com/package/monocart-coverage-reports#config-file

The name argument is optional and can be used to provide a name for the combined report. If it is not defined, the report is named "Browser library Merged Coverage Report".

The reports argument is optional and can be used to provide a list of reporters to create. Default is v8.

The keyword combines only the raw reports. To get raw reports, the Start Coverage keyword must be called with the raw=True argument. If no raw reports are found from the input_folder, the keyword fails. The keyword should be used when there is a need to combine multiple reports into a single report. For example, when tests are run in multiple pages. The example below demonstrates how to use the keyword.

Example:

New Page
Start Coverage
Go To    ${LOGIN_URL}
Test Feature X In The Page
Stop Coverage
New Page
Start Coverage
Go To    ${LOGIN_URL}
Test Feature Y In The Page
Stop Coverage
Merge Coverage Reports    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/browser/coverage    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/browser/combined-coverage
keywords.shortdoc: Combines multiple raw coverage reports into a single report.

args.name: input_folder
args.doc: Path to the base folder where the raw coverage reports are located.

args.name: output_folder
args.doc: Path to the folder where the combined report is stored.

args.name: config_file
args.doc: Optional path to options file

args.name: name
args.doc: Optional name for the combined report.

args.name: reports
args.doc: Optional list of reporters to create. Default is v8.

keywords.name: Mock Responses
keywords.doc:
Adds a route rule that answers every request matching matcher with a mock response.

The request never reaches the server.

Give at most one of body, json and path; none is an empty body, for example with status=204. Unless headers has a Content-Type, which always wins, the Content-Type is text/plain; charset=utf-8 for a text body, application/octet-stream for a bytes body, application/json for json, guessed from the file extension for path (application/octet-stream if unknown, and with charset=utf-8 for a text/ type, so give a file in another encoding its Content-Type in headers), and none without a body, which WebKit reports as application/octet-stream.

Returns the rule id, to give to Remove Route Rule.

A rule ends when its context or page closes, when it is removed with Remove Route Rule or Remove All Route Rules, or when it has used up its times. It does not end with the test or suite.

A request that a service worker answers never reaches a route rule; open the context with serviceWorkers=block in New Context to route those requests too. Each answered request is logged only in playwright-log.txt. When several rules match a request, the newest one wins, and a Page rule wins over a Context rule.

The keyword never logs the body or header values, but a string value still shows in the keyword's arguments in the Robot Framework log; give a token as Secret to keep it out. With enable_playwright_debug in the library import, the values are visible as plain text in the Playwright debug log.

A cross-origin mock response needs no CORS headers. If it sets its own Access-Control-Allow-Origin, the browser checks it, so * together with credentials fails.

Example, mock the orders and then fail the next request once:

Mock Responses    **/api/orders    json=${orders}
Mock Responses    **/api/orders    status=500    times=1
Click    id=reload-orders    # gets 500
Click    id=reload-orders    # gets ${orders}

See route rules for more.
keywords.shortdoc: Adds a route rule that answers every request matching ``matcher`` with a mock response.

args.name: matcher
args.doc: Request URL matcher: a glob pattern, a JavaScript RegExp enclosed in /, or a JavaScript arrow function that receives the request URL and returns a boolean, such as url => url.searchParams.get('id') === '7'. Globs and RegExps match as in Wait For Response, see its matcher examples; unlike there, the function gets the URL, not the request. An invalid RegExp fails.

args.name: status
args.doc: The response status, from 100 to 599. There is no reason phrase argument: the browser shows the standard phrase, or Unknown for a code such as 299.

args.name: body
args.doc: The response body as text or a Robot Framework Secret, sent as UTF-8, or as bytes, sent unchanged. A dictionary, a list, a number or a boolean is sent as JSON, as with json. body= is an empty body. To answer with a captured body, give its bytes, for example body=${response.bytes} from Wait For Response.
args.repr: body: JsonSerializable | bytes | Secret | None = None

args.name: json
args.doc: A JsonSerializable value, such as a dictionary, list or number, sent as compact JSON. A string is sent as a JSON string, so JSON text goes in body with a Content-Type header. None means not given: for a JSON null body use body=null with a Content-Type header.

args.name: path
args.doc: A file whose bytes are the body; binary files work. A relative path resolves against the working directory.

args.name: headers
args.doc: HttpHeaders (a dictionary), all headers of the mock response.

args.name: times
args.doc: How many matching requests the rule answers before it ends. None (default) answers every matching request until the rule is removed. Must be 1 or more.

args.name: on
args.doc: Where the rule is added, see ContextOrPage. Context (default) for every page of the active context, also pages opened later, Page for the active page only: the rule stays on that page and does not follow Switch Page. Fails when no context or page is open.

keywords.name: Modify Responses
keywords.doc:
Adds a route rule that sends every request matching matcher to the server and changes the real response.

The request reaches the server, and only the parts given here change, in the request on its way out and in the response on its way back. Every change is None by default, which keeps the real value; give at least one.

Give at most one of body, json, path and json_patch. In headers and request_headers a given value wins, an empty string sends the header empty and None removes it.

A replaced body keeps the Content-Type of the real response or request when it is text or bytes, so body=<p>Sold out</p> on an HTML page stays HTML. Text is sent as UTF-8: when the real Content-Type names another charset, give the Content-Type with charset=utf-8 in headers or request_headers. A JSON value in body, json or request_body sets application/json, and path sets the type of the file as in Mock Responses. A Content-Type given or removed in headers or request_headers always wins.

When the real request fails, the page request fails too. The real request gets the browser timeout that is in effect when the rule is added.

Returns the rule id, to give to Remove Route Rule. Like the rules of Abort Requests, a rule ends with its context or page, when removed or when its times is used up. Header names are logged, never values or bodies; give tokens as Secret to keep them out of the keyword's arguments in the log.

Example, an order in an edge-case state, fetched with a token:

VAR    ${token: Secret} =    %{API_TOKEN}
VAR    &{auth} =    Authorization=${token}
VAR    &{patch} =    state=cancelled    note=${None}
Modify Responses    **/api/orders/1    json_patch=${patch}    request_headers=${auth}

See route rules for redirects, cookies on a changed URL, failures and more examples.
keywords.shortdoc: Adds a route rule that sends every request matching ``matcher`` to the server and changes the real response.

args.name: matcher
args.doc: Request URL matcher: a glob pattern, a JavaScript RegExp enclosed in /, or a JavaScript arrow function that receives the request URL and returns a boolean, such as url => url.searchParams.get('id') === '7'. Globs and RegExps match as in Wait For Response, see its matcher examples; unlike there, the function gets the URL, not the request. An invalid RegExp fails.

args.name: status
args.doc: The response status, from 100 to 599.

args.name: body
args.doc: Replaces the real body with text, a Robot Framework Secret, bytes or a JSON value, encoded as in Mock Responses.
args.repr: body: JsonSerializable | bytes | Secret | None = None

args.name: json
args.doc: Replaces the real body with a JSON-encoded value, as in Mock Responses.

args.name: path
args.doc: Replaces the real body with the bytes of a file, as in Mock Responses.

args.name: json_patch
args.doc: Changes fields of the real JSON body, as an RFC 7386 JSON Merge Patch: dictionaries merge, None deletes a key and a list replaces the whole list. Like json, it fails for NaN, Infinity and values JSON cannot hold.

args.name: headers
args.doc: HttpHeaderChanges (a dictionary) merged onto the real response headers: a value replaces the real header, None removes it.

args.name: request_url
args.doc: Sends the request to this URL instead, absolute or relative to the original one. The page keeps its original URL.

args.name: request_method
args.doc: Sends the request with this method.

args.name: request_headers
args.doc: HttpHeaderChanges (a dictionary) merged onto the real request headers, the same way as headers.

args.name: request_body
args.doc: Sends this text or Robot Framework Secret as UTF-8, these bytes unchanged, or a dictionary, a list, a number or a boolean as JSON, as the request body. A captured request body is ${request.postDataBuffer} from Wait For Request.
args.repr: request_body: JsonSerializable | bytes | Secret | None = None

args.name: times
args.doc: How many matching requests the rule changes before it ends. None (default) changes every matching request until the rule is removed.

args.name: on
args.doc: Where the rule is added, see ContextOrPage.

keywords.name: Mouse Button
keywords.doc:
