Clicks, presses or releases a mouse button.

Attention: Argument type int for 'delay' in milliseconds has been changed to timedelta in Browser 14.0.0. Use Robot Framework time format instead. For refactoring just add 'ms' after the delay number.

Delay Example:

Mouse Button    click    delay=100 ms
Mouse Button    click    delay=${dyn_delay} ms

Moving the mouse between holding down and releasing it is possible with Mouse Move.

Example:

Hover                     "Obstacle"           # Move mouse over the element
Mouse Button              down                 # Press mouse button down
Mouse Move Relative To    "Obstacle"    500    # Drag mouse
Mouse Button              up                   # Release mouse button

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Clicks, presses or releases a mouse button.

args.name: action
args.doc: Defines if it is a mouseclick (click), holding down a button (down) or releasing it (up).

args.name: x
args.doc: Coordinates to move to before the action is executed. Both must be given, otherwise the action happens at the current mouse position.

args.name: y
args.doc: Coordinates to move to before the action is executed. Both must be given, otherwise the action happens at the current mouse position.

args.name: button
args.doc: One of left, middle or right. Defaults to left.

args.name: clickCount
args.doc: Determines how often the button shall be clicked if action is equal to click. Defaults to 1.

args.name: delay
args.doc: Delay in Robot Framework time format between the mousedown and mouseup event. Can only be set if the action is click. Defaults to 0 s.

keywords.name: Mouse Move
keywords.doc:
Moves the virtual mouse to the given coordinates, instead of to an element found by a selector.

The virtual mouse is left on the specified coordinates.

Example:

Mouse Move    400    400

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Moves the virtual mouse to the given coordinates, instead of to an element found by a selector.

args.name: x
args.doc: Absolute coordinate starting at the left border of the page.

args.name: y
args.doc: Absolute coordinate down starting at the top border of the page.

args.name: steps
args.doc: Number of intermediate steps for the mouse event. Often it is necessary to send more than one intermediate event to get the desired result. Defaults to 1.

keywords.name: Mouse Move Relative To
keywords.doc:
Moves the mouse cursor relative to the selected element.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Example:

Mouse Move Relative To    id=indicator    -100

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Moves the mouse cursor relative to the selected element.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Identifies the element whose center is the start-point.

args.name: x
args.doc: Coordinates relative to the center of the element's bounding box.

args.name: y
args.doc: Coordinates relative to the center of the element's bounding box.

args.name: steps
args.doc: Number of intermediate steps for the mouse event. Often it is necessary to send more than one intermediate event to get the desired result. Defaults to 1.

keywords.name: Mouse Wheel
keywords.doc:
Simulates the user rotation of a mouse wheel.

Example:

# Before doing a mouse wheel interaction. A mouse needs to be positioned on the browser window.
Hover    body
Mouse Wheel    0    250

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Simulates the user rotation of a mouse wheel.

args.name: deltaX
args.doc: Pixels that are scrolled horizontally.

args.name: deltaY
args.doc: Pixels that are scrolled vertically.

keywords.name: New Browser
keywords.doc:
Create a new playwright Browser with specified options.

See Browser, Context and Page for more information about Browser and related concepts.

Returns a stable identifier for the created browser.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Create a new playwright Browser with specified options.

args.name: browser
args.doc: Opens the specified browser. Defaults to chromium.

args.name: headless
args.doc: Set to False if you want a GUI. Defaults to True.

args.name: args
args.doc: Additional arguments to pass to the browser instance. The list of Chromium flags can be found here. Defaults to None.

args.name: channel
args.doc: Allows operating against the stock Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge browsers. Can only be used together with the chromium browser, otherwise the keyword fails. For more details see: Playwright documentation.

args.name: chromiumSandbox
args.doc: Enable Chromium sandboxing. Defaults to False.

args.name: devtools
args.doc: Chromium-only. Whether to auto-open a Developer Tools panel for each tab. Defaults to False.

args.name: downloadsPath
args.doc: If specified, accepted downloads are downloaded into this folder. Otherwise, temporary folder is created and is deleted when browser is closed. Regarding file deletion, see the docs of Download and Promise To Wait For Download.

args.name: env
args.doc: Specifies environment variables that will be visible to the browser. Dictionary keys are variable names, values are the content. Defaults to None.

args.name: executablePath
args.doc: Path to a browser executable to run instead of the bundled one. If executablePath is a relative path, then it is resolved relative to current working directory. Note that Playwright only works with the bundled Chromium, Firefox or WebKit, use at your own risk. Defaults to None.

args.name: firefoxUserPrefs
args.doc: Firefox user preferences. Learn more about the Firefox user preferences at about:config.
args.repr: firefoxUserPrefs: dict[str, str | int | float | bool] | None = None

args.name: handleSIGHUP
args.doc: Close the browser process on SIGHUP. Defaults to True.

args.name: handleSIGINT
args.doc: Close the browser process on Ctrl-C. Defaults to True.

args.name: handleSIGTERM
args.doc: Close the browser process on SIGTERM. Defaults to True.

args.name: ignoreDefaultArgs
args.doc: If True, Playwright does not pass its own configuration args and only uses the ones from args. If a list is given, then the given default arguments are filtered out. Dangerous option; use with care. Defaults to None, which means Playwright's own default arguments are used.

args.name: proxy
args.doc: Network Proxy settings. Structure: {'server': <str>, 'bypass': <Optional[str]>, 'username': <Optional[str]>, 'password': <Optional[str]>}. Robot Framework 7.4 Secret type is supported.

args.name: reuse_existing
args.doc: If set to True, an existing browser instance that was created with the same arguments is reused. If no such browser exists, a new one is started. Defaults to True.

args.name: slowMo
args.doc: Slows down Playwright operations by the given time, in Robot Framework time format. Useful so that you can see what is going on. Defaults to no delay.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Maximum time in Robot Framework time format to wait for the browser instance to start. Defaults to 30 seconds. Pass 0 to disable timeout.

keywords.name: New Context
keywords.doc:
Create a new BrowserContext with specified options.

See Browser, Context and Page for more information about BrowserContext.

Returns a stable identifier for the created context that can be used in Switch Context.

Example:

Test an iPhone
    ${device}=    Get Device    iPhone X
    New Context    &{device}        # unpacking here with &
    New Page    http://example.com

A BrowserContext is the Playwright object that controls a single browser profile. Within a context caches and cookies are shared. See Playwright browser.newContext for a list of supported options.

If there's no open Browser this keyword will open one. Does not create pages. It is not possible to create a new context in a browser that was opened with New Persistent Context.

The httpCredentials and proxy arguments do support Robot Framework 7.4 Secret type. If Secret is used, the dictionary structure must be created before hand, example with Robot Framework's VAR syntax:

${user}   ${password} =    Get Secrets    # Returns username and password as Robot Framework Secret type
VAR    &{httpCredentials} =    username=${user}    password=${password}
New Context    httpCredentials=${httpCredentials}

Using dictionary literals with Robot Framework 7.4 Secret type is not supported, for example this will fail on variable conversion on Robot Framework side:

${user}   ${password} =    Get Secrets    # Returns username and password as Robot Framework Secret type
New Context    httpCredentials={'username': ${secret}, 'password': ${secret}}    # This will fail

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Create a new BrowserContext with specified options.

args.name: acceptDownloads
args.doc: Whether to automatically download all the attachments. Defaults to True where all the downloads are accepted.

args.name: baseURL
args.doc: When using Go To, Wait For Request, Wait For Response or Wait For Navigation it takes the base URL in consideration by using the URL() constructor for building the corresponding URL. Unset by default. Examples: baseURL=http://localhost:3000 and navigating to /bar.html results in http://localhost:3000/bar.html. baseURL=http://localhost:3000/foo/ and navigating to ./bar.html results in http://localhost:3000/foo/bar.html. baseURL=http://localhost:3000/foo (without trailing slash) and navigating to ./bar.html results in http://localhost:3000/bar.html.

args.name: bypassCSP
args.doc: Toggles bypassing page's Content-Security-Policy. Defaults to False.

args.name: clientCertificates
args.doc: Specifies a client certificate for mTLS authentication, for example clientCertificates=[{'origin': 'https://playwright.dev', 'pfxPath': 'certificate.p12', 'passphrase': 'password'}]. NOTE: The origin needs to be exact without any path.

args.name: colorScheme
args.doc: Emulates the prefers-color-scheme media feature, supported values are light, dark, no-preference and null. null disables the emulation.

args.name: defaultBrowserType
args.doc: If no browser is open and New Context opens a new browser with defaults, this setting defines which browser is opened. Very useful together with the Get Device keyword.

args.name: deviceScaleFactor
args.doc: Specify device scale factor (can be thought of as dpr). Defaults to 1.

args.name: extraHTTPHeaders
args.doc: HttpHeaders (a dictionary) sent with every request of the context. A value can be a Robot Framework Secret; the values are logged as XXX.

args.name: forcedColors
args.doc: Emulates the forced-colors media feature, supported values are active, none and null. Defaults to none.

args.name: geolocation
args.doc: A dictionary containing latitude and longitude and optionally accuracy to emulate. If latitude or longitude is not specified, the device geolocation won't be overridden.

args.name: hasTouch
args.doc: Specifies if viewport supports touch events. Defaults to False.

args.name: httpCredentials
args.doc: Credentials for HTTP authentication.

args.name: ignoreHTTPSErrors
args.doc: Whether to ignore HTTPS errors during navigation. Defaults to False.

args.name: isMobile
args.doc: Whether the meta viewport tag is taken into account and touch events are enabled. Defaults to False.

args.name: javaScriptEnabled
args.doc: Whether or not to enable JavaScript in the context. Defaults to True.

args.name: locale
args.doc: Specify user locale, for example en-GB, de-DE, etc.

args.name: offline
args.doc: Toggles browser's offline mode. Defaults to False.

args.name: permissions
args.doc: A list containing permissions to grant to all pages in this context. All permissions that are not listed here will be automatically denied.

args.name: proxy
args.doc: Network proxy settings to use with this context. Defaults to None. NOTE: For Chromium on Windows the browser needs to be launched with the global proxy for this option to work. If all contexts override the proxy, global proxy will be never used and can be any string, for example proxy={ server: 'http://per-context' }.

args.name: recordHar
args.doc: Enables HAR recording for all pages into a file. The path key must be a path to a file, for example recordHar={'path': '${OUTPUT_DIR}/har.file'}. A relative path is relative to the output directory. If not specified, the HAR is not recorded. Make sure to close the context for the HAR to be saved. See RecordHar for how to store the response bodies, record only what replaying needs, and record only the requests that match a URL filter.

args.name: recordVideo
args.doc: Enables video recording for all pages into a folder. If not specified videos are not recorded. Make sure to close the context for videos to be saved. Video is not supported in remote browsers. See RecordVideo for the folder, size, frame rate and action annotations.

args.name: reducedMotion
args.doc: Emulates the prefers-reduced-motion media feature, supported values are reduce and no-preference. Defaults to no-preference.

args.name: screen
args.doc: Emulates consistent window screen size available inside web page via window.screen. Is only used when the viewport is set. Example {'width': 414, 'height': 896}

args.name: serviceWorkers
args.doc: Whether to allow sites to register Service workers. Defaults to allow.

args.name: storageState
args.doc: Restores the storage state created by the Save Storage State keyword. Must be a path to an existing file, otherwise the keyword fails. Relative paths are resolved against the current working directory.

args.name: timezoneId
args.doc: Changes the timezone of the context. See ICU metaZones.txt for a list of supported timezone IDs.

args.name: tracing
args.doc: Boolean True (recommendation) or file path or directory where the tracing file is saved. The string {contextid} will be replaced with the context id. Path to *.zip files can be absolute or relative to ${OUTPUT_DIR}. Path to folders can be absolute or relative to ${OUTPUT_DIR}/browser/traces. If boolean True or a directory is given, the trace file will automatically be named trace_{contextid}.zip. Temporary trace files will be saved to ${OUTPUT_DIR}/browser/traces/temp. Tracing is automatically closed when context is closed. Temporary trace files will be automatically deleted at start of each test execution. Trace file can be opened after the test execution by running command from shell: rfbrowser show-trace /path/to/trace.zip. Tracing can also be enabled by setting a Robot Framework variable or environment variable ROBOT_FRAMEWORK_BROWSER_TRACING to True.

args.name: userAgent
args.doc: Specific user agent to use in this context.

args.name: viewport
args.doc: A dictionary containing width and height. Emulates consistent viewport for each page. Defaults to 1280x720. None disables the default viewport. If width and height are 0, the viewport will scale with the window.

keywords.name: New Page
keywords.doc:
Open a new Page.

A Page is the Playwright equivalent to a tab. See Browser, Context and Page for more information about Page concept.

Returns NewPageDetails as dictionary for created page. NewPageDetails (dict) contains the keys page_id and video_path. page_id is a stable identifier for the created page. video_path is path to the created video or empty if video is not created.

When a New Page is called without an open browser, New Browser and New Context are executed with default values first.

If navigating to url fails, the keyword fails and the newly created page is closed again. The page is closed only after the keyword set with Register Keyword To Run On Failure has run, so the failure screenshot shows the page that failed to load.

If the wait times out, the page's load report is logged: whether its navigation committed, how far the document got and which requests were still open.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Open a new Page.

args.name: url
args.doc: Optional URL to navigate the page to. The url should include the protocol, for example https://.

args.name: wait_until
args.doc: When to consider operation succeeded, defaults to load. Events can be either: domcontentloaded - consider operation to be finished when the DOMContentLoaded event is fired. load - consider operation to be finished when the load event is fired. networkidle - consider operation to be finished when there are no network connections for at least 500 ms. commit - consider operation to be finished when network response is received and the document started loading.

keywords.name: New Persistent Context
keywords.doc:
Opens a new persistent context.

New Persistent Context basically executes New Browser, New Context and New Page in one step and sets a profile at the same time. See persistent context in Playwright docs.

This keyword returns a tuple of browser id, context id and page details. (New in Browser 15.0.0)

other Arguments: Please see New Browser, New Context and New Page for more information about the other arguments.

If you want to use extensions you need to download the extension as a .zip, enable loading the extension, and load the extensions using chromium arguments like below. Extensions only work with chromium and with a headful browser.

${launch_args}=  Set Variable  ["--disable-extensions-except=./ublock/uBlock0.chromium", "--load-extension=./ublock/uBlock0.chromium"]
${browserId}  ${contextId}  ${pageDetails}=  New Persistent Context  browser=chromium  headless=False  url=https://robocon.io  args=${launch_args}

Check New Browser, New Context and New Page for the specific argument docs.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Opens a new persistent context.

args.name: userDataDir
args.doc: Path to a User Data Directory, which stores browser session data like cookies and local storage. Note that Chromium's user data directory is the parent directory of the "Profile Path" seen at chrome://version. Pass an empty string to use a temporary directory instead.

args.name: browser
args.doc: Browser type to use. Default is Chromium.

args.name: headless
args.doc: Whether to run browser in headless mode. Defaults to True.

keywords.name: Open Browser
keywords.doc:
DEPRECATED Opens a new browser instance. Use this keyword for quick experiments or debugging sessions.

Use New Page directly instead of Open Browser for production and automated execution. See Browser, Context and Page for more information about Browser and related concepts.

Creates a new browser, context and page with specified settings.

Browsers:

Value Name(s)
firefox Firefox
chromium Chromium
webkit webkit

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: *DEPRECATED* Opens a new browser instance. Use this keyword for quick experiments or debugging sessions.

args.name: url
args.doc: Navigates to URL if provided. Defaults to None.

args.name: browser
args.doc: Specifies which browser to use. The supported browsers are listed in the table below.

args.name: headless
args.doc: If set to False, a GUI is provided otherwise it is hidden. Defaults to False.

args.name: pause_on_failure
args.doc: Stop execution when failure detected and leave browser open. Defaults to True.

args.name: bypassCSP
args.doc: Defaults to bypassing CSP and enabling custom script attach to the page.

keywords.name: Pause At
keywords.doc:
Advances the clock by jumping forward in time and pauses it.

Fires due timers at most once. This is equivalent to a user closing the laptop lid for a while and reopening it at the specified time and then pausing. Pause can not move the clock backwards.

Example:

Set Time         2024-10-31 17:34:00    # Set the clock to a specific time
Do Something                            # Implement this in your keyword
Pause At         2024-10-31 18:34:00    # Pause the clock at a specific time
Check Something                         # Also this is implemented in your keyword
Resume Clock                            # Resume the clock
Do Something Else                       # Do something after clock runs normally
keywords.shortdoc: Advances the clock by jumping forward in time and pauses it.

args.name: time
args.doc: The time to pause the clock at.

keywords.name: Press Keys
keywords.doc:
Types the given key combination into element found by selector.

Supports values like a or b which will be automatically typed.

Also supports identifiers for keys like ArrowLeft or Backspace.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

See Playwright's documentation for a more comprehensive list of supported input keys. Playwright docs for press.

Example:

# Keyword         Selector                    *Keys
Press Keys      //*[@id="username_field"]    h    e   l   o   ArrowLeft   l

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Types the given key combination into element found by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector of the text field. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: keys
args.doc: Keys to be pressed one after the other. Combining modifiers with a single key press by chaining them with +, like Control+Shift+T, is supported.

args.name: press_duration
args.doc: Delay between keydown and keyup of each key. Can be given as seconds (float) or as Robot Framework time string. Defaults to 0 ms. Example: 50 ms

args.name: key_delay
args.doc: Delay between key presses. Can be given as seconds (float) or as Robot Framework time string. Defaults to 0 ms. Example: 50 ms

keywords.name: Promise To
keywords.doc:
Wrap a Browser library keyword and make it a promise.

The promised keyword is started in the background. Test execution continues without waiting for kw to finish.

Returns a reference to the promised keyword. Use Wait For or Wait For All Promises to wait for its result. Promises that are never waited for are waited for automatically at the end of the test, and a warning is logged.

Only Browser library keywords can be promised, any other keyword name fails the keyword.

Example:

${promise}=     Promise To            Wait For Response     matcher=     timeout=3
Click           \#delayed_request
${body}=        Wait For              ${promise}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Wrap a Browser library keyword and make it a promise.

args.name: kw
args.doc: Keyword that will run asynchronously in the background.

args.name: args
args.doc: Keyword arguments as normally used.

keywords.name: Promise To Upload File
keywords.doc:
Returns a promise that resolves when the file from path has been uploaded.

The file from path is uploaded into the next file chooser dialog on the page.

The keyword fails immediately if path does not point to an existing file. The promise fails if no file chooser dialog is opened within the timeout.

Example use:

${promise}=    Promise To Upload File    ${CURDIR}/test_upload_file.txt
Click          id=open_file_chooser_button
${upload_result}=    Wait For    ${promise}

Alternatively, you can use the Upload File By Selector keyword.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns a promise that resolves when the file from ``path`` has been uploaded.

args.name: path
args.doc: Path to file to be uploaded.

keywords.name: Promise To Wait For Download
keywords.doc:
Returns a promise that waits for the next download event on the page.

To enable downloads the context's acceptDownloads needs to be true.

With the default file path downloaded files are deleted when the context the download happened in is closed.

If browser is connected remotely with Connect To Browser then saveAs must be set to store it locally where the browser runs!

Keyword returns dictionary of type DownloadInfo which contains downloaded file path and suggested filename as well as state and downloadID. Example:

{
  "saveAs": "/tmp/robotframework-browser/downloads/2f1b3b7c-1b1b-4b1b-9b1b-1b1b1b1b1b1b",
  "suggestedFilename": "downloaded_file.txt",
  "state": "finished",
  "downloadID": None
}

If wait_for_finished is False, saveAs is an empty string, state is in_progress and downloadID contains an id which can be used with Get Download State to check the download later.

The keyword New Browser has a downloadsPath setting which can be used to set the default download directory. If saveAs is set to a relative path, the file will be saved relative to the browser's downloadsPath setting or if that is not set, relative to the Playwright's working directory. If saveAs is set to an absolute path, the file will be saved to that absolute path independent of downloadsPath.

Set download_timeout when the download can take longer than the browser timeout, for example when the server generates the file before sending it.

If the URL for the file to download shall be used, Download keyword may be a simpler alternative way to download the file.

The waited promise returns a dictionary which contains saveAs and suggestedFilename as keys. The saveAs contains the location where the file is downloaded and suggestedFilename contains the suggested name for the download. The suggestedFilename is typically computed by the browser from the Content-Disposition response header or the download attribute. See the spec on whatwg. Different browsers can use different logic for computing it.

Example usage:

New Context            acceptDownloads=True
New Page               ${LOGIN_URL}
${dl_promise}          Promise To Wait For Download    /path/to/download/file.name    download_timeout=30s
Click                  id=file_download
${file_obj}=           Wait For    ${dl_promise}
File Should Exist      ${file_obj}[saveAs]
Should Be True         ${file_obj.suggestedFilename}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns a promise that waits for the next download event on the page.

args.name: saveAs
args.doc: Defines path where the file is saved persistently. File will also temporarily be saved in playwright context's default download location. If empty, generated unique path (GUID) is used and file is deleted when the context is closed.

args.name: wait_for_finished
args.doc: If true, promise will wait for download to finish. If false, promise will resolve immediately after download has started.

args.name: download_timeout
args.doc: Maximum total time for the download to start and finish, counted from the moment the promise is created. If the download does not start within this time, the keyword fails. If it starts but does not finish, it is cancelled and the keyword fails. If wait_for_finished is False, only the start is limited. If not set, the download must start within the browser timeout, see Set Browser Timeout, and there is no limit for it to finish.

keywords.name: Record Keyword
keywords.doc:
Record browser interactions as one User Keyword named name.

Shows the Robot Framework Browser recorder toolbar on the pages of the current browser context and blocks until the recording ends. Every Action becomes a Keyword Call to a Browser keyword, is listed in the toolbar and is written to file immediately.

Toolbar buttons (each has a tooltip):

  • ✕ in the header: ends the session.
  • Minimize in the header (a dash): minimizes the toolbar.
  • Discard: drops the Keyword Calls recorded so far and starts the keyword again, empty.
  • Undo: removes the Keyword Calls of the last Action.
  • Pause (two bars): stops recording until Resume; Actions in between are not recorded.
  • Pick in the header: picks an element on the page, as Record Selector does, and adds its selector to the keyword as a comment row # Picked Selector <selector>. Playwright's own Pick locator button opens the same picker. While picking, nothing is recorded; Cancel returns to recording without a row.

The toolbar is in the recording state from the start. Click a value or a selector in the toolbar to turn the whole of it, or a marked part, into a Keyword Argument, named like email or ${email}. The same dialog asks whether the marked value becomes the argument's default. The toolbar also offers to use the new argument for the same value elsewhere in the keyword (replacing repeated values). A name that is already an argument of the keyword reuses that argument, so different recorded values can become the same argument; its default stays as it was.

The keyword is always created new: an existing keyword is never extended.

The recording ends with Save or ✕ in the toolbar, with Playwright's Record button, when idle_timeout passes without any Action or toolbar command, when all pages are closed or have crashed, or on an error. The keyword being recorded is saved unless it has no Keyword Calls.

Returns the text of the recorded keyword, including the *** Keywords *** header. If a recorded keyword cannot be written - the file became read-only, the disk is full - the keyword fails, and the recorded text is logged as a warning so nothing is lost.

Keyword Calls use the keyword names of this Browser library, so when Browser is imported with language, they are written in that language. A new keyword section header and the [Tags] and [Arguments] settings use the language of file: the first language declared in it with Language:, otherwise the first language the run was started with (--language or robot.toml), otherwise English. With file=${None} there is no file, so the language the run was started with is used. The language is determined when the recording starts; if file stops enabling it during the recording, saving fails until it is enabled again. An existing keyword section is used, whatever its language. The returned text starts with the English *** Keywords *** header, which Robot Framework accepts in every language, but its settings are in the language of file, so the text parses only where that language is enabled.

What is generated: every keyword gets the tag recorded. A popup or new tab becomes Switch Page NEW. An Action on another open page gets a Switch Page to it first, using the id the Switch Page that left that page returned (${page}= Switch Page NEW); a page closed by hand becomes Close Page, or Close Page ${page} when it is not the active one. A page the keyword has no id of, for example one open before the recording, cannot be switched to, and the toolbar says so. A dialog gets Handle Future Dialogs action=accept before the Action (Playwright does not report whether the dialog was accepted); a download is wrapped in Promise To Wait For Download and Wait For. A file chosen in a file chooser wraps the click that opened it in Promise To Upload File and Wait For; the page never reveals the file's folder, so the path reads <define_path_to_file>/<file name> and must be completed (or made an argument). Playwright's Assert snapshot becomes Get Aria Snapshot with an exact YAML comparison, and Assert visibility becomes Get Element States ... *= visible. Playwright folds a navigation that happens within 5 seconds after a click, fill or key press into that Action, so it is not recorded as a Go To of its own. Hovers are not recorded, because Playwright does not report them. Other Actions without a Browser keyword are only reported in the toolbar.

Needs a visible browser: fails if the active browser was opened headless, since nobody could use the toolbar there. A browser attached with Connect To Browser is assumed to be visible.

Limitations: only the current browser context is recorded; other contexts are ignored. Playwright's own recorder toolbar is shown at the top centre of the page during the recording and cannot be hidden, so it covers the page there. The toolbar does not appear on a page whose Content-Security-Policy allows only Trusted Types policies it names, nor in a document without a body, such as an SVG file. A modal <dialog> of the page covers the toolbar until it is closed, and a click there is recorded on the dialog.

Review a recorded keyword before you commit it. Its values come from the page under test, including anything typed into password fields. During the session the toolbar state, including the recorded values and typed text, is readable by scripts of every page in the context, and those scripts can send toolbar commands. Keystrokes typed into the toolbar do not reach the page, except to a window capture listener the page registered before the toolbar was injected.

Requires a Playwright version that offers the programmatic recorder. The context stays prepared for recording after the session ends.

Example:

${text} =    Record Keyword    Login As Admin
Record Keyword    Search Product    ${CURDIR}/shop.resource    idle_timeout=15 min
Record Keyword    Try Something    file=${None}

See Record Keywords to record several keywords in one session.
keywords.shortdoc: Record browser interactions as one User Keyword named ``name``.

args.name: name
args.doc: Name of the User Keyword to create. It must not exist in file and must not shadow any keyword the running suite can call.

args.name: file
args.doc: Target .robot or .resource file. Defaults to ${SUITE_SOURCE}, the file of the running suite; in a suite initialisation file that is its __init__.robot, and a keyword recorded there can only be used in that file. A relative path is resolved against the current working directory, not against the suite; use ${CURDIR} for a file next to the suite. The folder must exist and an existing file must be writable; both are checked before recording starts. With ${None} nothing is written; the keyword is logged to the console and to the log at INFO level instead.

args.name: idle_timeout
args.doc: Ends the recording after this long without an Action or toolbar command. Must be greater than zero. Default: 5 minutes, so a forgotten recording does not block the run for good. ${None} waits without limit.

keywords.name: Record Keywords
keywords.doc:
Record several User Keywords in one session.

Use Record keyword in the toolbar to name and start a keyword, record it, and Save it; then start the next one. Actions while no keyword is being recorded are not captured, so you can navigate freely between keywords. A name must not exist in file, must not have been recorded earlier in the session, and must not shadow any keyword the running suite can call - such names are rejected in the toolbar.

Shows the Robot Framework Browser recorder toolbar on the pages of the current browser context and blocks until the recording ends. Every Action becomes a Keyword Call to a Browser keyword, is listed in the toolbar and is written to file immediately.

Toolbar buttons (each has a tooltip):

  • ✕ in the header: ends the session.
  • Minimize in the header (a dash): minimizes the toolbar.
  • Record keyword: names and starts a keyword.
  • Discard: drops the keyword being recorded, also from file, and returns to idle.
  • Undo: removes the Keyword Calls of the last Action.
  • Pause (two bars): stops recording until Resume; Actions in between are not recorded.
  • Pick in the header: picks an element on the page, as Record Selector does, and adds its selector to the keyword as a comment row # Picked Selector <selector>. Playwright's own Pick locator button opens the same picker. While picking, nothing is recorded; Cancel returns to recording without a row.
  • Save: saves the keyword being recorded and returns to idle.

While the toolbar is minimized, its header offers Start (idle) or Save (recording).

The toolbar is idle until a keyword is started; Actions while idle are not recorded. While recording, click a value or a selector in the toolbar to turn the whole of it, or a marked part, into a Keyword Argument, named like email or ${email}. The same dialog asks whether the marked value becomes the argument's default. The toolbar also offers to use the new argument for the same value elsewhere in the keyword (replacing repeated values). A name that is already an argument of the keyword reuses that argument, so different recorded values can become the same argument; its default stays as it was.

Existing keywords are never extended.

The recording ends with ✕ in the toolbar header, with Playwright's Record button, when idle_timeout passes without any Action or toolbar command, when all pages are closed or have crashed, or on an error. The keyword being recorded is saved unless it has no Keyword Calls.

Returns the text of all keywords recorded in the session, under one *** Keywords *** header. If a recorded keyword cannot be written - the file became read-only, the disk is full - the keyword fails, and the recorded text is logged as a warning so nothing is lost.

Keyword names and languages are chosen as described in Record Keyword.

What is generated: every keyword gets the tag recorded. A popup or new tab becomes Switch Page NEW. An Action on another open page gets a Switch Page to it first, using the id the Switch Page that left that page returned (${page}= Switch Page NEW); a page closed by hand becomes Close Page, or Close Page ${page} when it is not the active one. A page the keyword has no id of, for example one open before the recording, cannot be switched to, and the toolbar says so. A dialog gets Handle Future Dialogs action=accept before the Action (Playwright does not report whether the dialog was accepted); a download is wrapped in Promise To Wait For Download and Wait For. A file chosen in a file chooser wraps the click that opened it in Promise To Upload File and Wait For; the page never reveals the file's folder, so the path reads <define_path_to_file>/<file name> and must be completed (or made an argument). Playwright's Assert snapshot becomes Get Aria Snapshot with an exact YAML comparison, and Assert visibility becomes Get Element States ... *= visible. Playwright folds a navigation that happens within 5 seconds after a click, fill or key press into that Action, so it is not recorded as a Go To of its own. Hovers are not recorded, because Playwright does not report them. Other Actions without a Browser keyword are only reported in the toolbar.

Needs a visible browser: fails if the active browser was opened headless, since nobody could use the toolbar there. A browser attached with Connect To Browser is assumed to be visible.

Limitations: only the current browser context is recorded; other contexts are ignored. Playwright's own recorder toolbar is shown at the top centre of the page during the recording and cannot be hidden, so it covers the page there. The toolbar does not appear on a page whose Content-Security-Policy allows only Trusted Types policies it names, nor in a document without a body, such as an SVG file. A modal <dialog> of the page covers the toolbar until it is closed, and a click there is recorded on the dialog.

Review recorded keywords before you commit them. Their values come from the page under test, including anything typed into password fields. During the session the toolbar state, including the recorded values and typed text, is readable by scripts of every page in the context, and those scripts can send toolbar commands. Keystrokes typed into the toolbar do not reach the page, except to a window capture listener the page registered before the toolbar was injected.

Requires a Playwright version that offers the programmatic recorder. The context stays prepared for recording after the session ends.

Example:

${text} =    Record Keywords
Record Keywords    ${CURDIR}/resources/shop.resource    idle_timeout=${None}

See Record Keyword to record exactly one keyword.
keywords.shortdoc: Record several User Keywords in one session.

args.name: file
args.doc: Target .robot or .resource file. Defaults to ${SUITE_SOURCE}, the file of the running suite; in a suite initialisation file that is its __init__.robot, and a keyword recorded there can only be used in that file. A relative path is resolved against the current working directory, not against the suite; use ${CURDIR} for a file next to the suite. The folder must exist and an existing file must be writable; both are checked before recording starts. With ${None} nothing is written; the keywords are logged to the console and to the log at INFO level instead.

args.name: idle_timeout
args.doc: Ends the recording after this long without an Action or toolbar command. Must be greater than zero. Default: 5 minutes, so a forgotten recording does not block the run for good. ${None} waits without limit.

keywords.name: Record Selector
keywords.doc:
Pick an element on the active page and return a selector for it.

Shows the Robot Framework Browser selector toolbar on the active page and blocks until a selector is chosen. Move the pointer over the page: Playwright highlights the element under it and names it in a tooltip. Click to pick it; the click does not reach the page. Elements inside frames and open shadow roots can be picked too.

The toolbar then shows the selector for the picked element:

  • Playwright / CSS: switches between the selector generators for the same element, see SelectorGenerator.
  • The selector itself can be edited. The elements it finds stay highlighted on the page, and the toolbar counts them; after an edit both follow once typing pauses for a second. One match is what most keywords need, several are shown as a warning, none as an error. The highlight ends with the keyword.
  • Highlight (a dashed square): switches the highlight off and on; it is on by default.
  • Reselect: picks another element.
  • Use: returns the selector, also when it does not find exactly one element.
  • ✕ in the header, or Escape in the toolbar: cancels, and the keyword fails.
  • Minimized, the header offers Reselect and Use once an element is picked.

Fails in a headless browser, while a Record Keyword or Record Keywords session runs in the browser context, when the page is closed or crashes, on cancel and when the idle_timeout passes.

The toolbar has the limits of the Record Keyword toolbar: it does not appear on a page whose Content-Security-Policy allows only Trusted Types policies it names, nor in a document without a body.

Like the recorder toolbar, the toolbar's commands are reachable by scripts of the page under test: use it on applications you trust, and check the selector you get.

Example:

${selector} =    Record Selector    Login button
Click    ${selector}
${heading} =    Record Selector    Page header    generator=css
Get Text    ${heading}    ==    Expected text

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Pick an element on the active page and return a selector for it.

args.name: label
args.doc: Shown in the toolbar header, to say which element to pick.

args.name: generator
args.doc: The generator the toolbar starts with; the toolbar can switch it. playwright (default) or css.

args.name: idle_timeout
args.doc: Fails the keyword after this long without a pick or toolbar command. Must be greater than zero. Default: 5 minutes. ${None} waits without limit.

keywords.name: Register Keyword To Run On Failure
keywords.doc:
Sets the keyword to execute, when a Browser keyword fails.

The initial keyword to use is set when importing the library, and the keyword that is used by default is Take Screenshot fail-screenshot-{index}. Taking a screenshot when something failed is a very useful feature, but notice that it can slow down the execution.

It is possible to use string NONE or any other robot falsy name, case-insensitively, as well as Python None to disable this feature altogether.

This keyword returns an object which contains the previously registered failure keyword. The return value can always be used to restore the original value later. The returned object contains the keyword name and the possible arguments used for the keyword.

If the Take Screenshot keyword is registered as run on failure keyword without positional arguments and without the filename argument, then the default value of the filename argument is not used as screenshot file name. Instead, ${TEST NAME}_FAILURE_SCREENSHOT_{index} in the output directory is used as file name. If there is a need to use the default value of the filename argument, use robotframework-browser-screenshot-{index} as the filename argument value.

Example:

Register Keyword To Run On Failure    Take Screenshot    # Uses ${TEST NAME}_FAILURE_SCREENSHOT_{index} as filename
Register Keyword To Run On Failure    Take Screenshot    robotframework-browser-screenshot-{index}    # Uses robotframework-browser-screenshot-{index} as filename
${previous kw}=    Register Keyword To Run On Failure    NONE    # Disables run on failure functionality.
Register Keyword To Run On Failure    ${previous kw}
Register Keyword To Run On Failure    Take Screenshot    fullPage=True
Register Keyword To Run On Failure    Take Screenshot    failure-{index}    fullPage=True

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Sets the keyword to execute, when a Browser keyword fails.

args.name: keyword
args.doc: The name of a keyword that will be executed if a Browser keyword fails. It is possible to use any available keyword, including user keywords or keywords from other libraries. A Browser keyword can be given by its English name even when a translation renames it.

args.name: args
args.doc: The arguments to the keyword if any.

args.name: scope
args.doc: Scope defines the lifetime of this setting. Available values are Global, Suite or Test / Task. See Scope Setting for more details.

keywords.name: Reload
keywords.doc:
Reloads current active page.

waitUntil events can be either: domcontentloaded - consider the operation to be finished when the DOMContentLoaded event is fired. load - consider the operation to be finished when the load event is fired. networkidle - consider the operation to be finished when there are no network connections for at least 500 ms. commit - consider the operation to be finished when the network response is received and the document started loading.

If the wait times out, the page's load report is logged: whether its navigation committed, how far the document got and which requests were still open.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Reloads current active page.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Maximum time for the reload to succeed. If not given, the library default timeout is used.

args.name: waitUntil
args.doc: When to consider the operation succeeded, defaults to load.

keywords.name: Remove All Route Rules
keywords.doc:
Removes the route rules of the active context and of every page in it.

Only rules added by this library are removed, routes that a plugin or a JavaScript keyword added with page.route stay. Like Remove Route Rule, the keyword waits for running handlers to finish. It logs how many Context and Page rules it removed, and how many times each rule ran. With no rules, or no open context, it logs and passes, so it is safe in a teardown.

Only the active context is covered. For several contexts, switch to each one:

FOR    ${context}    IN    @{contexts}
    Switch Context    ${context}
    Remove All Route Rules
END

Example:

[Teardown]    Remove All Route Rules
keywords.shortdoc: Removes the route rules of the active context and of every page in it.

keywords.name: Remove Locator Handler
keywords.doc:
Remove the locator handler indicated by locator.

The locator must be exactly the same string that was used as the selector argument when the handler was added. Handlers are tied to the page in which they were added, therefore this keyword removes the handler from the active page only. If no handler is found, the keyword does not fail, it only logs that no handler was found.
keywords.shortdoc: Remove the locator handler indicated by ``locator``.

keywords.name: Remove Route Rule
keywords.doc:
Removes the route rule with rule_id.

It logs how many times the rule ran. An unknown or already ended id, or no open context, is logged and the keyword passes. When the keyword returns, the rule affects no request: it waits for the rule's running handlers to finish.

Example:

${rule} =    Abort Requests    **/api/orders
Click    id=reload-orders    # request aborted
Remove Route Rule    ${rule}
Click    id=reload-orders    # reaches the server
keywords.shortdoc: Removes the route rule with ``rule_id``.

args.name: rule_id
args.doc: The id that Abort Requests, Mock Responses or Modify Responses returned. The rule is found in any context, so a Page rule can be removed while another page is active.

keywords.name: Resume Clock
keywords.doc:
Resumes the clock.

Once this keyword is called, time resumes flowing and timers are fired as usual.
keywords.shortdoc: Resumes the clock.

keywords.name: Save Page As Pdf
keywords.doc:
Saves page as PDF.

Saving a PDF is currently only supported in Chromium and only when the browser is running in headless mode.

headerTemplate and footerTemplate should be valid HTML markup. The following classes can be used to inject printing values into them:

  • date formatted print date
  • title document title
  • url document location
  • pageNumber current page number
  • totalPages total pages in the document

All possible units are:

  • px - pixel
  • in - inch
  • cm - centimeter
  • mm - millimeter

headerTemplate and footerTemplate markup have the following limitations:

  • Script tags inside the templates are not evaluated.
  • Page styles are not visible inside the templates.

Returns the path to the saved PDF file.

More details can be found in the Playwright pdf documentation.

Example:

New Browser        Chromium              headless=True
New Page           ${URL}
Emulate Media      media=screen
${pdf_path} =      Save Page As Pdf    page.pdf
Should Be Equal    ${pdf_path}           ${OUTPUT_DIR}${/}page.pdf
keywords.shortdoc: Saves page as PDF.

args.name: path
args.doc: Where the PDF is saved. If the path is not absolute, the file is saved relative to ${OUTPUT_DIR}.

args.name: displayHeaderFooter
args.doc: Display header and footer. Defaults to false.

args.name: footerTemplate
args.doc: HTML template for the print footer. Should use the same format as the headerTemplate.

args.name: format
args.doc: Paper format. If set, takes priority over the width and height arguments. Defaults to Letter.

args.name: headerTemplate
args.doc: HTML template for the print header. Both templates are only rendered when displayHeaderFooter is true. See the detailed explanation below.

args.name: height
args.doc: Paper height, accepts values labeled with units.

args.name: landscape
args.doc: Paper orientation. Defaults to false.

args.name: margin
args.doc: Defines the PDF margins, see PdfMarging for more details. Defaults to 0px on all sides.

args.name: outline
args.doc: Whether or not to embed the document outline into the PDF. Defaults to false.

args.name: pageRanges
args.doc: Paper ranges to print, e.g. 1-5, 8, 11-13. Defaults to the empty string, which means print all pages.

args.name: preferCSSPageSize
args.doc: Give any CSS @page size declared in the page priority over what is declared in the width and height or format arguments. Defaults to false, which will scale the content to fit the paper size.

args.name: printBackground
args.doc: Print background graphics. Defaults to false.

args.name: scale
args.doc: Scale of the webpage rendering. Defaults to 1. Scale amount must be between 0.1 and 2.

args.name: tagged
args.doc: Whether or not to generate a tagged (accessible) PDF. Defaults to false.

args.name: width
args.doc: Paper width, accepts values labeled with units.

keywords.name: Save Storage State
keywords.doc:
Saves the current active context storage state to a file.

Web apps use cookie-based or token-based authentication, where authenticated state is stored as cookies or in local storage. This keyword retrieves the storage state from authenticated contexts and saves it to disk. Then New Context can be created with prepopulated state.

Please note that the state file may contain secrets and should not be shared with people outside of your organisation.

Files in ${OUTPUTDIR}/browser/state are automatically deleted when new test execution starts. To keep a state file over several executions, save it with path to a location outside of that folder. File path is returned by the keyword.

Example:

Test Case
    New context
    New Page    https://login.page.html
    #  Perform login
    VAR    ${username: Secret}    %{USERNAME}    # Convert environment variable to secret
    VAR    ${password: Secret}    %{PASSWORD}    # Convert environment variable to secret
    Fill Secret    id=username    ${username}
    Fill Secret    id=password    ${password}
    Click    id=button
    Get Text    id=header    ==    Something
    #  Save storage to disk
    ${state_file} =    Save Storage State
    #  Create new context with saved state
    New context    storageState=${state_file}
    New Page    https://login.page.html
    #  Login is not needed because authentication is read from state file
    Get Text    id=header    ==    Something

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Saves the current active context storage state to a file.

args.name: path
args.doc: Where the state file is written. Relative paths are resolved against the current working directory and missing parent directories are created. If the file already exists, it is overwritten. If not given, a file with a generated name is created in ${OUTPUTDIR}/browser/state. The absolute path of the written file is returned.

args.name: indexedDB
args.doc: Also save IndexedDB. Needed by applications, like Firebase, which store authentication tokens in IndexedDB.

args.name: credentials
args.doc: Also save the context's virtual WebAuthn credentials, as created by Create Credential. This is not related to the httpCredentials argument of New Context, which is about HTTP authentication.

keywords.name: Scroll By
keywords.doc:
Scrolls an element or the page relative from current position by the given values.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Scrolls an element or the page relative from current position by the given values.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector of the element. If the selector is ${None} or ${Empty} the page itself is scrolled. To ensure an element is in view use Hover instead. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: vertical
args.doc: Defines how far and in which direction to scroll vertically. It can be a positive or negative number. Positive scrolls down, like 50, negative scrolls up, like -50. It can be a percentage value of the absolute scrollable size, like 9.95% or negative like -10%. It can be the string height to scroll exactly one visible height down, or -height to scroll one visible height up. Be aware that some pages do lazy loading and load more content once you scroll down. The percentage of the current scrollable height is used and may change. Defaults to height.

args.name: horizontal
args.doc: Defines how far and in which direction to scroll horizontally. Works the same way as vertical, but positive values scroll to the right and negative values to the left. width scrolls exactly one visible range to the right. Defaults to 0.

args.name: behavior
args.doc: Defines whether the scroll happens instantly or smoothly. Defaults to auto.

keywords.name: Scroll To
keywords.doc:
Scrolls an element or the page to an absolute position based on given coordinates.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Scrolls an element or the page to an absolute position based on given coordinates.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector of the element. If the selector is ${None} or ${Empty} the page itself is scrolled. To ensure an element is in view use Hover instead. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: vertical
args.doc: Defines where to scroll vertically. It can be a positive number, like 300. It can be a percentage value of the absolute scrollable size, like 50%. It can be a string defining the top or the bottom of the scroll area. < top | bottom > Be aware that some pages do lazy loading and load more content once you scroll down. Bottom defines the currently known bottom coordinate. Defaults to top.

args.name: horizontal
args.doc: Defines where to scroll horizontally. Works the same way as vertical, but defines < left | right > as start and end. Defaults to left.

args.name: behavior
args.doc: Defines whether the scroll happens instantly or smoothly. Defaults to auto.

keywords.name: Scroll To Element
keywords.doc:
This method waits for actionability checks, then tries to scroll element into view, unless it is completely visible.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Does nothing if the element is already completely visible.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: This method waits for actionability checks, then tries to scroll element into view, unless it is completely visible.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector of the element. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

keywords.name: Select Options By
keywords.doc:
Selects options from select element found by selector.

Returns a list of the options which the keyword was able to select. The type of the list items matches the attribute definition. For example, if attribute equals label, the returned list contains label values. Or in case of index, it contains the selected indexes.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

If no values to select are passed, all options of the element are deselected. The keyword fails if none of the given values matches an option.

Example:

${selected} =    Select Options By    select[name=preferred_channel]    label    Direct mail
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    Direct mail
${selected} =    Select Options By    select[name=interests]    value    males    females    others
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    males
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    females
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    others
Length Should Be    ${selected}    3
${selected} =    Select Options By    select[name=possible_channels]    index    0    2
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    0
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    2
${selected} =    Select Options By    select[name=interests]    text     Males    Females
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    Males
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    Females

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Selects options from select element found by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector of the <select> tag. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: attribute
args.doc: Attribute to select options by. Can be value, label, text or index. Where label and text are same.

args.name: values
args.doc: Values to select.

keywords.name: Send API Request
keywords.doc:
Sends an HTTP request through the active context, outside any page.

The keyword is Playwright's APIRequestContext.fetch of the active context. The request is an API request, not page traffic:

  • It uses the cookies of the context. A cookie that a page received is sent, and a cookie that the response sets is there for the pages of the context too.
  • It uses the context's baseURL, extraHTTPHeaders, httpCredentials, proxy, userAgent, ignoreHTTPSErrors and clientCertificates from New Context, as they are when the request is sent.
  • It needs an open context but no page, and fails when no context is open.
  • The browser's rules for a page do not apply: there is no CORS, and headers that a page cannot set, such as Origin or Cookie, are sent as given.
  • Route rules, such as those of Abort Requests, and Wait For Request and Wait For Response do not see it.

Use HTTP instead for a request that the page itself sends, with the page's rules.

The named-only arguments are the options of Playwright's fetch, with Playwright's names. An argument that is not given keeps Playwright's default.

The keyword fails on a network error, a timeout, too many redirects and, with failOnStatusCode, an error status.

Returns an APIResponse with the status, all headers, set-cookie included, the raw body as bytes and the views text and json. The response is logged without its headers and body, the headers at DEBUG level, as they can contain cookies, and the body at TRACE level.

Assigned with &{response} =, bytes holds base64 text. Assign with ${response} = to get the raw bytes.

New Context    baseURL=https://example.com
New Page    /login
# ... log in on the page ...
VAR    &{user} =    name=robot
${response} =    Send API Request    /api/users    POST    data=${user}    failOnStatusCode=True
Should Be Equal    ${response.status}    ${201}
Should Be Equal    ${response.json.name}    robot

VAR    &{params} =    q=robot    page=${2}
${response} =    Send API Request    /api/search    params=${params}

VAR    &{file} =    path=${CURDIR}/avatar.png
VAR    &{fields} =    description=Profile picture    file=${file}
${response} =    Send API Request    /api/avatar    POST    multipart=${fields}
keywords.shortdoc: Sends an HTTP request through the active context, outside any page.

args.name: url
args.doc: The request URL. A relative URL is resolved against the context's baseURL and fails without one.

args.name: method
args.doc: The HTTP method. Defaults to GET.

args.name: headers
args.doc: HttpHeaders (a dictionary) of the request. They override the context's extraHTTPHeaders with the same name.

args.name: params
args.doc: QueryParams (a dictionary or a string) added to the query of the url. Characters such as & in a string keep their meaning in a query, see QueryParams. The string None adds no parameters.

args.name: data
args.doc:
The request body, see JsonSerializable. Leave it out to send no body; the string None is sent as the text None. A Robot Framework Secret is sent as its text.

  • A dictionary, a list, a number or a boolean is sent as JSON, exactly as Python writes it, so large integers arrive unchanged. The Content-Type is application/json unless headers has one. A value that JSON cannot hold, such as NaN, a date or bytes inside a dictionary, fails before the request is sent.
  • bytes are sent as given, as application/octet-stream unless headers has a Content-Type.
  • A string is sent as given, but the Content-Type in headers decides how. Without one, it is application/octet-stream, also when the string is JSON. With application/json, parameters such as charset aside, a string that is valid JSON is sent as given, and any other string is encoded as a JSON string, so hello is sent as "hello". Any other Content-Type, also a JSON type such as application/problem+json, sends the string as given.
  • To send JSON written in the test data, give a dictionary, e.g. data=${{ {"name": "robot"} }}, or set the Content-Type in headers.
args.repr: data: JsonSerializable | bytes | Secret | None = None

args.name: form
args.doc: FormFields (a dictionary), sent URL-encoded as application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

args.name: multipart
args.doc: MultipartFields (a dictionary of text fields and files), sent as multipart/form-data, in the order given. data, form and multipart exclude each other, also when form or multipart is an empty dictionary. For now the data and the files given as buffer can be at most 4 MiB together; a file given as path does not count.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: How long to wait for the whole response, body included. Defaults to the library timeout; 0 waits without a limit.

args.name: failOnStatusCode
args.doc: When True, the keyword fails on a status that is not 2xx or 3xx. By default a response with an error status, such as 404, does not fail it.

args.name: maxRedirects
args.doc: How many redirects are followed. Playwright's default is 20, and it fails when there are more. 0 follows none and returns the redirect response.

args.name: maxRetries
args.doc: How often the request is retried when the connection is reset (ECONNRESET). Any other error fails at once, and an error status is never retried. Playwright's default is 0, no retry.

args.name: ignoreHTTPSErrors
args.doc: When True, errors of the server's HTTPS certificate are ignored. They are also ignored when the context was opened with ignoreHTTPSErrors=True; False cannot turn that off.

keywords.name: SessionStorage Clear
keywords.doc:
Remove all saved data from the session storage.

Example:

SessionStorage Set Item    mykey3    myvalue3
SessionStorage Clear
SessionStorage Get Item    mykey3    ==    ${None}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Remove all saved data from the session storage.

args.name: frame_selector
args.doc:
If this selector points to an element inside an iframe, the SessionStorage of that frame is used.

Example: iframe[name="test"] >>> body

keywords.name: SessionStorage Get Item
keywords.doc:
Get saved data from the session storage.

See Assertions for further details about the assertion arguments. They default to None.

If the key does not exist in the storage, ${None} is returned.

Example:

SessionStorage Set Item    key2    value2
${item} =    SessionStorage Get Item    key2
Should Be Equal    ${item}    value2

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Get saved data from the session storage.

args.name: key
args.doc: Named key of the item in the storage.

args.name: assertion_operator
args.doc: Assertion operator to use. See Assertions for more information.

args.name: assertion_expected
args.doc: Expected value to compare with.

args.name: message
args.doc: Custom error message to use.

args.name: frame_selector
args.doc: If this selector points to an element inside an iframe, the SessionStorage of that frame is used. Example: iframe[name="test"] >>> body

keywords.name: SessionStorage Remove Item
keywords.doc:
Remove saved data with key from the session storage.

Example:

SessionStorage Set Item       mykey2    myvalue2
SessionStorage Remove Item    mykey2
SessionStorage Get Item       mykey2    ==    ${None}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Remove saved data with key from the session storage.

args.name: key
args.doc: The name of the item which shall be deleted.

args.name: frame_selector
args.doc: If this selector points to an element inside an iframe, the SessionStorage of that frame is used. Example: iframe[name="test"] >>> body

keywords.name: SessionStorage Set Item
keywords.doc:
Save data to session storage.

Example:

SessionStorage Set Item    key2    value2

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Save data to session storage.

args.name: key
args.doc: The name of the key under which it should be saved.

args.name: value
args.doc: The value which shall be saved as a string.

args.name: frame_selector
args.doc: If this selector points to an element inside an iframe, the SessionStorage of that frame is used. Example: iframe[name="test"] >>> body

keywords.name: Set Assertion Formatters
keywords.doc:
Set keywords formatters for assertions.

Returns the formatters which were in use before this keyword was called. Formatters defined as lambda functions are not included in the returned value.

See type documentation of FormatterKeywords and FormatingRules for more information.

It is possible to define own formatters as lambda functions.

Example:

Set Assertion Formatters    {"Get Text": ["strip", "normalize spaces"]}  # This will convert all kinds of spaces to a single space and remove spaces from the start and end of the string.
Set Assertion Formatters    {"Get Title": ["apply to expected","lambda x: x.replace(' ', '')"]}  # This will remove all spaces from the string.
${value} =    Get Text    //div    ==    ${SPACE}Expected${SPACE * 2}Text
Should Be Equal    ${value}    Expected Text

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Set keywords formatters for assertions.

args.name: formatters
args.doc: Dictionary of keywords and formatters, where the key is the name of the keyword where the formatters are applied. The dictionary value is a list of formatters which are applied. Formatters for a defined keyword are always overwritten. An empty list will clear all formatters for the keyword. If formatters is an empty dictionary, then all formatters are cleared from all keywords, in the Global scope, regardless of the scope argument.

args.name: scope
args.doc: Defines the lifetime of the formatter, possible values are Global, Suite and Test.

keywords.name: Set Browser Timeout
keywords.doc:
Sets the timeout used by most input and getter keywords.

Returns the previous value of the timeout.

Example:

${old_timeout} =    Set Browser Timeout    1m 30 seconds
Click     //button
Set Browser Timeout    ${old_timeout}

Close Browser and Close Context are not shortened by this setting; they always get at least 20 seconds.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Sets the timeout used by most input and getter keywords.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: The timeout is set for the current Playwright context and for new contexts. Supports Robot Framework time format.

args.name: scope
args.doc: Scope defines the live time of that setting. Available values are Global, Suite or Test / Task. See Scope Setting for more details.

keywords.name: Set Default Run Before Unload
keywords.doc:
Set default runBeforeUnload value when Close Page is called indirectly.

Close Page is called indirectly when automatic page closing is done. The default value is false and this keyword can be used to change value. Returns the old runBeforeUnload value.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Set default runBeforeUnload value when `Close Page` is called indirectly.

keywords.name: Set Extra HTTP Headers
keywords.doc:
Sets the extra HTTP headers that every request of the active context or page sends.

The given headers replace all extra headers of the context or page, also those given as extraHTTPHeaders to New Context. To keep a header, pass it again. Page headers are sent on top of the context headers; for the same name the page header wins.

The keyword logs only the header names. A string value still shows in the keyword's arguments in the Robot Framework log; give a token as Secret to keep it out. The $variable syntax of Set HTTP Credentials is not resolved here: $token is sent as it is. With enable_playwright_debug in the library import, the values are visible as plain text in the Playwright debug log.

An Authorization header goes to every origin the page calls, third-party origins included. For HTTP Basic authentication Set HTTP Credentials with an origin is safer. In Playwright the headers also reach WebSocket handshakes in Chromium 151+ and WebKit; Firefox does not send them for a WebSocket opened inside a Worker.

Example:

New Context    extraHTTPHeaders={'X-Tenant': 'a'}
New Page    ${URL}/login
VAR    ${token: Secret} =    %{API_AUTHORIZATION}    # e.g. "Bearer abc123"
Set Extra HTTP Headers    X-Tenant=a    Authorization=${token}    # X-Tenant passed again to keep it
Set Extra HTTP Headers    X-Experiment=variant-b    on=Page
Set Extra HTTP Headers    # clears the context headers
keywords.shortdoc: Sets the extra HTTP headers that every request of the active context or page sends.

args.name: on
args.doc: Where the headers are set, see ContextOrPage. Context (default) for every page of the active context, also pages opened later, Page for the active page only. Fails when no context or page is open.

args.name: headers
args.doc: The headers, as free named arguments name=value. A value is a string or a Robot Framework Secret. An empty string is sent as an empty header. No headers clears them. A header named on cannot be set, because on= is the argument below.

keywords.name: Set Geolocation
keywords.doc:
Updates the current context's geolocation.

Latitude can be between -90 and 90 and longitude can be between -180 and 180. The accuracy of the location must be a non-negative number and defaults to 0. When creating the context, grant the geolocation permission so that pages can read the geolocation.

Example:

${permissions} =    Create List    geolocation
New Context    permissions=${permissions}
Set Geolocation    60.173708    24.982263    3    # Points to Korkeasaari in Helsinki.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Updates the current context's geolocation.

args.name: latitude
args.doc: Latitude between -90 and 90.

args.name: longitude
args.doc: Longitude between -180 and 180.

args.name: accuracy
args.doc: Non-negative accuracy value. Defaults to 0.

keywords.name: Set Highlight On Failure
keywords.doc:
Controls if the element is highlighted on failure.

Returns the previous value of the setting.

Example:

Set Highlight On Failure    True

Comment >> #TODO add real link
keywords.shortdoc: Controls if the element is highlighted on failure.

args.name: highlight
args.doc: If True, the element is highlighted when a screenshot is taken on failure. If False, the element is not highlighted in the screenshot.

args.name: scope
args.doc: Scope defines the live time of that setting. Available values are Global, Suite or Test / Task. See Scope Setting for more details.

keywords.name: Set HTTP Credentials
keywords.doc:
Sets the credentials the active context sends for HTTP authentication.

The given credentials replace all credentials of the active context, also those given as httpCredentials to New Context. To keep a credential, pass it again.

As in New Context, username and password are given as Robot Framework Secret or with the $variable syntax, so their values stay out of the log. The keyword logs only the origins. With enable_playwright_debug in the library import, the values are visible as plain text in the Playwright debug log.

Browsers may cache credentials per origin after a successful authentication, so changing the credentials of an origin that has already authenticated may have no effect. To switch users reliably, open a New Context.

Example:

VAR    &{admin} =    username=$admin_user    password=$admin_pwd    origin=https://admin.example.com
VAR    &{api} =    username=$api_user    password=$api_pwd    origin=https://api.example.com
New Context
Set HTTP Credentials    ${admin}    ${api}
New Page    https://admin.example.com
Set HTTP Credentials    # clears the credentials
keywords.shortdoc: Sets the credentials the active context sends for HTTP authentication.

args.name: credentials
args.doc: Zero or more HttpCredentials dictionaries with username, password and an optional origin (scheme://host:port). A credential with origin is sent only to that origin, one without to any origin that asks for authentication. For a request, the first credential whose origin matches, or that has none, is used. No credentials clears them.

keywords.name: Set Offline
keywords.doc:
Toggles the current context's offline emulation.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Toggles the current context's offline emulation.

args.name: offline
args.doc: Toggles the offline mode. Set to False to switch back to online mode. Defaults to True.

keywords.name: Set Presenter Mode
keywords.doc:
Sets presenter mode for element highlighting during test execution.

Presenter mode highlights elements found by keywords, which is useful for test debugging and demonstration. When enabled, the element is scrolled into view and highlighted with a border for a while to visually show what the keyword found.

The keyword returns the previous presenter mode value, allowing you to restore it later.

Example:

${old_mode} =    Set Presenter Mode    True
Click    //button                            # Element will be highlighted
Set Presenter Mode    ${old_mode}            # Restore previous mode

# With custom highlighting configuration
VAR    &{config}
...    duration=5 seconds
...    width=3px
...    style=dotted
...    color=red
Set Presenter Mode    ${config}
Get Text    //input                          # Will use custom highlight settings
Set Presenter Mode    False                  # Turn off highlighting
keywords.shortdoc: Sets presenter mode for element highlighting during test execution.

args.name: mode
args.doc: When set to True, enables presenter mode with default settings. When set to False, disables presenter mode. Can also be a dictionary containing the highlighting configuration options as defined in HighLightElement. Fields which are not given use their default values: duration 2 seconds, width 2px, style dotted and color blue.

keywords.name: Set Retry Assertions For
keywords.doc:
Sets the timeout used in retrying assertions when they fail.

The other keyword Set Browser Timeout controls how long Playwright will wait on the node side for elements to fulfill the requirements of the specific keyword.

Returns the previous value of the assertion retry timeout.

Example:

Set Browser Timeout    10 seconds
${old} =    Set Retry Assertions For    30s
Get Title    ==    Login Page
Set Retry Assertions For    ${old}

The example waits 10 seconds in Playwright to get the page title and the library will retry for 30 seconds to make sure that the title is correct.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Sets the timeout used in retrying assertions when they fail.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Assertion retry timeout will determine how long Browser library will retry an assertion to be true.

args.name: scope
args.doc: Scope defines the live time of that setting. Available values are Global, Suite or Test / Task. See Scope Setting for more details.

keywords.name: Set Selector Prefix
keywords.doc:
Sets the prefix for all selectors in the given scope.

Returns the previous value of the prefix.

Example:

${old} =    Set Selector Prefix    iframe#embedded_page >>>
Click    button#login_btn       # Clicks on button inside iframe with the selector iframe#embedded_page >>> button#login_btn
Set Selector Prefix    ${old}

Example will click on button with id login_btn inside iframe with id embedded_page. The resulting selector will be iframe#embedded_page >>> button#login_btn.

The effect of this prefix can be disabled by prefixing any selector with !prefix , with a trailing space, for single keyword calls, i.e. !prefix id=btn_outside_a_frame

Get Element, Get Elements, Get Element By and Get Element By Role automatically prefix the returned selector with !prefix so that it is possible to use them directly without setting the prefix to ${None} before usage.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Sets the prefix for all selectors in the given scope.

args.name: prefix
args.doc: Prefix for all selectors. Prefix and selector will be separated by a single space. Use ${None} or ${EMPTY} to disable the prefix.

args.name: scope
args.doc: Scope defines the live time of that setting. Available values are Global, Suite or Test / Task. See Scope Setting for more details.

keywords.name: Set Storage State
keywords.doc:
Restores a storage state file into the current active context.

Clears the cookies, local storage, IndexedDB and virtual WebAuthn credentials of the currently active context and replaces them with the ones from the path file, which must have been created by Save Storage State. Unlike creating a New Context with the storageState argument, the context and all of its pages stay open.

Pages that are already open keep the state they have loaded into memory. Reload them, with the Reload keyword, to make them see the restored state. Cookies and local storage are readable right away, without a reload, but the application has read them long ago.

Note that sessionStorage is not part of a storage state, neither when saving nor when restoring. It survives this keyword unchanged, so an application which keeps data of the previous user there still has it after the state was replaced.

Restoring a state which was saved with credentials=True installs the virtual WebAuthn authenticator into the context, the same way Install Credential does. Real authenticators do not work in that context afterwards.

Restoring IndexedDB

Restoring IndexedDB deletes the databases of the origin first, and that does not finish while any client of that origin holds an open connection to them. An application which keeps its connection open, which is the normal pattern when authentication tokens are stored in IndexedDB, therefore blocks the restore indefinitely. Playwright does not time out on its own, see playwright#42258.
