This keyword works around that by navigating the pages of the affected origins to about:blank, restoring the state, and navigating them back to the url they had before. Use reload_pages to control which pages that applies to. A reload is needed in any case, because deleting the databases closes the connection of the application as well.

A service worker of the origin can hold a connection open too, and no value of reload_pages helps against that, because a service worker outlives the pages. The keyword then fails when timeout expires.

reload_pages=none detects a blocking connection up front and fails immediately instead of waiting for the timeout. That detection needs indexedDB.databases(), which older browsers, Firefox before 126 among them, do not have. There the keyword cannot tell whether a connection blocks and falls back to waiting for timeout.

Example:

New Context
New Page    https://login.page.html
    #  Perform login as first user
${user_a} =    Save Storage State    indexedDB=True
    #  Perform login as second user
${user_b} =    Save Storage State    indexedDB=True
    #  Switch back to the first user without creating a new context
Set Storage State    ${user_a}
Reload
Get Text    id=current-user    ==    userA
keywords.shortdoc: Restores a storage state file into the current active context.

args.name: path
args.doc: Path to a state file created by Save Storage State. Relative paths are resolved against the current working directory. The keyword fails if the file does not exist.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Time to wait for the state to be restored. If not defined, the library default timeout is used. Pass 0 to disable the timeout.

args.name: reload_pages
args.doc: Which pages are reloaded while the state is restored, see ReloadPages. Only relevant when the state file contains IndexedDB.

keywords.name: Set Strict Mode
keywords.doc:
Controls library strict mode.

The keyword returns the strict mode value which was in use before this keyword was called.

Strict mode is enabled by default. The initial value can also be set with the strict argument in the library importing. Strict mode is applied only to those keywords which state in their documentation that they use strict mode, see Finding elements for more details.

Example:

${old_mode} =      Set Strict Mode    False
Get Text           //input            # Does not fail even if the selector matches multiple elements
Set Strict Mode    ${old_mode}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Controls library strict mode.

args.name: mode
args.doc: When set to True, keywords that search elements will use Playwright strict mode and fail if the selector matches more than one element. When set to False, such keywords do not fail but operate on the first matching element.

args.name: scope
args.doc: Scope defines the live time of that setting. Available values are Global, Suite or Test / Task. See Scope Setting for more details.

keywords.name: Set Time
keywords.doc:
Sets the time of the browser's internal clock.

fixed makes Date.now and new Date() always return the same fake time, while all timers keep running.

system sets the current system time but does not trigger any timers.

install installs fake timers, which are used to manually control the flow of time in tests. They allow you to advance time, fire timers, and control the behavior of time-dependent functions.

How to use clock related keywords, see Playwright clock documentation. Also reviewing the Playwright Clock API is recommended.
keywords.shortdoc: Sets the time of the browser's internal clock.

args.name: time
args.doc: The time to set. Supports Robot Framework date and time format

args.name: clock_type
args.doc: The clock type to set. Default is install.

keywords.name: Set Viewport Size
keywords.doc:
Sets the current page's viewport size to the specified dimensions.

In the case of multiple pages in a single browser, each page can have its own viewport size. However, New Context allows setting the viewport size (and more) for all later opened pages in the context at once.

Set Viewport Size will resize the page. A lot of websites don't expect phones to change size, so you should set the viewport size with New Context before opening the page itself.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Sets the current page's viewport size to the specified dimensions.

args.name: width
args.doc: Sets the width in pixels.

args.name: height
args.doc: Sets the height in pixels.

keywords.name: Show Keyword Banner
keywords.doc:
Controls if the keyword banner is shown on page or not.

The keyword call banner is a CSS overlay that shows the currently executed keyword directly on the page, centered at its bottom. This is useful for debugging and for showing the test execution on video recordings. By default, the banner is not shown on the page except when running in presenter mode.

The banner can also be controlled by an import setting of the Browser library. (see Importing section)

Returns the previous settings as a dictionary with the keys show and style.

Example:

Show Keyword Banner     True    top: 5px; bottom: auto; left: 5px; right: auto; background-color: #00909077; font-size: 9px; color: black;   # Show banner on top left corner with custom styles
Show Keyword Banner     False   # Hide banner

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Controls if the keyword banner is shown on page or not.

args.name: show
args.doc: If True, the banner is shown on the page. If False, the banner is not shown on the page. If ${None}, the banner is shown on the page only when running in presenter mode.

args.name: style
args.doc: Additional CSS styles to be applied to the banner. These styles may override the existing ones for the banner.

args.name: scope
args.doc: Scope defines the live time of that setting. Available values are Global, Suite or Test / Task. See Scope Setting for more details.

keywords.name: Start Coverage
keywords.doc:
Starts the coverage for the current page.

The coverage_type can be one of the following:

  • all: Both CSS and JS.
  • css: CSS.
  • js: JS.

Coverage must be started when the page is open and before any action is performed on the page. Coverage will be stored when calling the Stop Coverage keyword or when the page or context is closed. This is done automatically when using the auto closing.

The raw argument saves the raw coverage data in the coverage folder. The raw data is needed to combine multiple coverage reports into a single report. A single report can be created with the rfbrowser coverage /path/to/basefolder/ /path/to/outputfolder/ command. Please note that the raw argument is ignored if the config_file is defined. In that case the user is responsible for also setting the raw reporter in the config file. To see more details about combining coverage data, run the rfbrowser coverage --help command.

Example:

New Page
Start Coverage
Go To    ${LOGIN_URL}
Do Something In The Page
Stop Coverage
keywords.shortdoc: Starts the coverage for the current page.

args.name: config_file
args.doc: Optional path to options file. If the file does not exist, it is ignored.

args.name: coverage_type
args.doc: Type of coverage to start. Default is all.

args.name: path
args.doc: Absolute or relative directory path (relative to ${OUTPUT_DIR}/browser/coverage/) where the coverage is stored in a directory with the page id name.

args.name: raw
args.doc: Whether to save raw coverage data. Default is False.

args.name: reportAnonymousScripts
args.doc: Whether to report anonymous scripts. Default is False. Only valid for JS coverage.

args.name: resetOnNavigation
args.doc: Whether to reset coverage on navigation. Default is True.

keywords.name: Start Tracing
keywords.doc:
Starts recording a Playwright trace of the active context.

Use it to record a small trace of one part of a test, without tracing everything the context does. The trace holds what happens between this keyword and Stop Tracing. One context can record several traces one after another, for example one per test. To trace a context for its whole life, use the tracing argument of New Context instead. Open traces with rfbrowser show-trace or at https://trace.playwright.dev.

A context runs only one trace at a time. Starting a trace on a context that already records one fails, also when the trace was started by the tracing argument of New Context or by the ROBOT_FRAMEWORK_BROWSER_TRACING variable. Stop it first with Stop Tracing.

If the trace is not stopped with Stop Tracing, it is saved under ${OUTPUT_DIR}/browser/traces when its scope ends, or when its context closes, whichever comes first. When the library is imported with auto_delete_passed_tracing=True, a trace that ends with a passed test or suite in this way is not saved, the same as a context trace closed by automatic closing.

Keyword groups that are open when tracing starts are added to the trace, so the trace shows which keyword started it.

Example:

New Context
New Page         ${LOGIN_URL}
Start Tracing    title=Login    scope=Test
Fill Text        id=username_field    demo
Click            id=login_button
${trace} =    Stop Tracing    path=login.zip

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Starts recording a Playwright trace of the active context.

args.name: screenshots
args.doc: Records a screenshot after each action, for the film strip of the trace viewer.

args.name: snapshots
args.doc: Records a DOM snapshot of the page around each action.

args.name: sources
args.doc: Embeds the source files of the actions in the trace.

args.name: title
args.doc: Name of the trace shown in the trace viewer.

args.name: scope
args.doc: When the trace is saved if it is not stopped before. Test saves it when the running test ends, and fails outside a test. Suite saves it when the running suite ends. Global saves it only when its context closes. See Scope. Without a running suite, as when the library is used from Python, every scope behaves like Global.

keywords.name: Stop Coverage
keywords.doc:
Stops the coverage for the current page.

Creates a coverage report by using monocart-coverage-reports To see the default and all possible options, see options.js file for more details.

If coverage was not started, the keyword returns None. Otherwise it returns the path to the generated HTML report file, or the path to the coverage folder if no HTML file is found from the folder. The latter can happen when the report format or output folder has been changed with the config_file argument of the Start Coverage keyword.
keywords.shortdoc: Stops the coverage for the current page.

keywords.name: Stop Tracing
keywords.doc:
Stops the trace of the active context, saves it and returns the path of the file.

Stops any trace of the active context: one started with Start Tracing, or one started by the tracing argument of New Context. Fails when the active context records no trace. A context can start a new trace after this.

A trace saved by this keyword is always kept, also with auto_delete_passed_tracing=True.

Example:

Start Tracing
Click    id=login_button
${trace} =    Stop Tracing    path=login.zip
Log    Trace of the login is in ${trace}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Stops the trace of the active context, saves it and returns the path of the file.

args.name: path
args.doc: Where the trace is saved. A path ending with .zip is the file, relative to ${OUTPUT_DIR}. Any other path is a directory under ${OUTPUT_DIR}/browser/traces, where the trace gets a file of its own. Without path, a trace of Start Tracing gets a file of its own in ${OUTPUT_DIR}/browser/traces, and a trace of New Context is saved where its tracing argument said.

keywords.name: Switch Browser
keywords.doc:
Switches the currently active Browser to another open Browser.

Returns a stable identifier for the previous browser. See Browser, Context and Page for more information about Browser and related concepts.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Switches the currently active Browser to another open Browser.

args.name: id
args.doc: The id of the browser to switch to. Example: browser=96207191-8147-44e7-b9ac-5e04f2709c1d. A browser id is returned by New Browser when it is started or can be fetched from the browser catalog when returned by Get Browser Catalog.

keywords.name: Switch Context
keywords.doc:
Switches the active BrowserContext to another open context.

Returns a stable identifier for the previous context. See Browser, Context and Page for more information about Context and related concepts.

Example:

${first_context} =     New Context
New Page             ${URL1}
${second_context} =    New Context
New Page             ${URL2}
Switch Context       ${first_context}    # Switches back to first context and page.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Switches the active BrowserContext to another open context.

args.name: id
args.doc: The id of the context to switch to. Example: context=525d8e5b-3c4e-4baa-bfd4-dfdbc6e86089. A context id is returned by New Context when it is started or can be fetched from the browser catalog when returned by Get Browser Catalog.

args.name: browser
args.doc: The browser in which to search for that context. CURRENT for the currently active browser, ALL to search in all open browsers or the id of the browser where to switch context.

keywords.name: Switch Page
keywords.doc:
Switches the active browser page to another open page by id or NEW.

Returns a stable identifier id for the previous page. See Browser, Context and Page for more information about Page and related concepts.

If a page id is given, the context and browser arguments are ignored and the page is searched from all open browsers.

NEW may time out if no new page is opened before the library timeout expires.

Example:

Click           button#pops_up    # Open new page
${previous} =    Switch Page      NEW

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Switches the active browser page to another open page by ``id`` or ``NEW``.

args.name: id
args.doc: The id or alias of the page to switch to. Example: page=8baf2991-5eaf-444d-a318-8045f914e96a or NEW. Can be a string or a dictionary returned by New Page Keyword. A page id can be fetched from the browser catalog when returned by Get Browser Catalog. NEW can be used to switch to a pop-up that just has been opened by the webpage, CURRENT can be used to switch to the active page of a different context or browser, identified by their id.

args.name: context
args.doc: The context in which to search for that page. CURRENT for the currently active context, ALL to search in all open contexts or the id of the context where to switch page.

args.name: browser
args.doc: The browser in which to search for that page. CURRENT for the currently active browser, ALL to search in all open browsers or the id of the browser where to switch page.

keywords.name: Take Screenshot
keywords.doc:
Takes a screenshot of the current window or element and saves it to disk.

Keyword uses strict mode if selector is defined. See Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Example

Take Screenshot                                 # Takes screenshot from page with default filename
Take Screenshot   selector=id=username_field    # Captures element in image
# Takes screenshot with jpeg extension, defines image quality and timeout how long taking screenshot should last
Take Screenshot   fullPage=True    fileType=jpeg    quality=50    timeout=10s
Take Screenshot   EMBED                         # Screenshot is embedded as Base64 image to the log.html.
Take Screenshot   UUID                          # Takes screenshot from page with filename generated by: https://docs.python.org/3/library/uuid.html.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Takes a screenshot of the current window or element and saves it to disk.

args.name: filename
args.doc: Filename into which to save. The file will be saved into the Robot Framework ${OUTPUTDIR}/browser/screenshot directory by default, but it can be overwritten by providing a custom path or filename. String {index} in the filename will be replaced with a rolling number. Use this to not overwrite filenames. If filename equals to UUID (case insensitive), then the filename is created by Python uuid; https://docs.python.org/3/library/uuid.html. If filename equals to EMBED (case insensitive) or ${NONE}, then the screenshot is embedded as a Base64 image into the log.html. The image is saved temporarily to the disk and a warning is displayed if removing the temporary file fails. The ${OUTPUTDIR}/browser/screenshot directory is removed at the first suite startup.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Take a screenshot of the element matched by selector. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors. If not provided, take a screenshot of the current viewport.

args.name: crop
args.doc: Crops the taken screenshot to the given box. It takes the same dictionary as returned from Get BoundingBox. Cropping only works on a page screenshot, so when no selector is given.

args.name: disableAnimations
args.doc: When set to True, stops CSS animations, CSS transitions and Web Animations. Animations get different treatment depending on their duration: - finite animations are fast-forwarded to completion, so they'll fire the transitionend event. - infinite animations are cancelled to initial state, and then played over after the screenshot.

args.name: fileType
args.doc: png or jpeg. Specifies the screenshot type, defaults to png.

args.name: fullPage
args.doc: When True, takes a screenshot of the full scrollable page, instead of the currently visible viewport. Defaults to False.

args.name: highlight_selector
args.doc: Highlights elements while taking the screenshot. Highlight method is playwright. This highlighting also automatically happens if the Robot Framework variable ${ROBOT_FRAMEWORK_BROWSER_FAILING_SELECTOR} is set to a selector string and is available on page. This is the case if highlight_on_failure has been set to True when importing Browser library.

args.name: log_screenshot
args.doc: When set to False the screenshot is taken but not logged into log.html.

args.name: mask
args.doc: Specify selectors that should be masked when the screenshot is taken. Masked elements will be overlaid with a pink box #FF00FF that completely covers their bounding box. The argument can take a single selector string or a list of selector strings if multiple different elements should be masked.

args.name: maskColor
args.doc: Specify the color of the overlay box for masked elements, in CSS color format. Default color is pink #FF00FF.

args.name: omitBackground
args.doc: Hides the default white background and allows capturing screenshots with transparency. Not applicable to jpeg images.

args.name: quality
args.doc: The quality of the image, between 0-100. Not applicable to png images.

args.name: scale
args.doc: css or device. css will reduce the image size and device keeps the image in its original size. Defaults to device.

args.name: return_as
args.doc: Defines what this keyword returns. Possible values are documented in ScreenshotReturnType. It can be either a path to the screenshot file as string or Path object, or the image data as bytes or base64 encoded string. When the screenshot is embedded into the log, path_string returns the string EMBED.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Maximum time how long taking the screenshot can last, defaults to the library timeout. Supports Robot Framework time format, like 10s or 1 min, pass 0 to disable the timeout. The default value can be changed by using the Set Browser Timeout keyword.

keywords.name: Tap
keywords.doc:
Simulates tap on the element found by selector.

Requires that the hasTouch option of New Context is set to true. This method taps the element by performing the following steps:

  • Wait for actionability checks on the element, unless the force option is set.
  • Scroll the element into view if needed.
  • Use page.touchscreen to tap the center of the element, or the specified position.
  • Wait for initiated navigations to either succeed or fail.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Example:

New Context    hasTouch=${True}
New Page    ${URL}
Tap    css=input#login_button

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Simulates tap on the element found by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector element to tap. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: modifiers
args.doc: Modifier keys to press. Ensures that only these modifiers are pressed during the tap, and then restores current modifiers back. If not specified, currently pressed modifiers are used. Modifiers can be specified in any order, and multiple modifiers can be specified. Valid modifier keys are Alt, Control, ControlOrMeta, Meta and Shift.

args.name: force
args.doc: Whether to bypass the actionability checks. Defaults to False.

args.name: noWaitAfter
args.doc: Deprecated. This option has no effect. Defaults to False.

args.name: position_x
args.doc: A point to tap relative to the top-left corner of element bounding-box. Only positive values within the bounding-box are allowed. Both values must be given, otherwise the position is ignored. If not specified, taps some visible point of the element.

args.name: position_y
args.doc: A point to tap relative to the top-left corner of element bounding-box. Only positive values within the bounding-box are allowed. Both values must be given, otherwise the position is ignored. If not specified, taps some visible point of the element.

args.name: trial
args.doc: When set, this method only performs the actionability checks and skips the action. Defaults to False.

keywords.name: Type Secret
keywords.doc:
Types the given secret into the text field found by selector.

This keyword does not log the secret in Robot Framework logs, but if Playwright debug logs are enabled, the secret will be visible as plain text in the Playwright debug logs, regardless of the Robot Framework log level or how secret is resolved.

This keyword supports Robot Framework 7.4 Secret variable type, which is the recommended way if you are using Robot Framework 7.4 or newer.

For older Robot Framework versions the keyword supports resolving secrets from environment variables and Robot Framework variables in the following ways. The keyword resolves the secret from a Robot Framework variable internally, when the secret variable is prefixed with $, without the curly braces. Example: $Password will resolve to the ${Password} Robot Framework variable.

If the secret variable is prefixed with %, the library will resolve the corresponding environment variable. Example: %ENV_PWD will resolve to the %{ENV_PWD} environment variable.

Using normal Robot Framework variables like ${password}, which are not Secret type variables, will not work!

Normal plain text will not work. If you want to use plain text, use the Type Text keyword instead.

This keyword also works with a cryptographic cipher text that has been encrypted by CryptoLibrary. See CryptoLibrary for more details.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

See Type Text for details.

Example

Type Secret    input#username_field    ${username}    # Keyword resolves ${username} variable value from Robot Framework Secret type variable
Type Secret    input#username_field    $username      # Keyword resolves ${username} variable value from Robot Framework variables
Type Secret    input#username_field    %username      # Keyword resolves $USERNAME/%USERNAME% variable value from environment variables

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Types the given ``secret`` into the text field found by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector of the text field. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: secret
args.doc: Supports Robot Framework 7.4 Secret type as normal variable (with curly braces). Also environment variable name with % prefix or a local variable with $ prefix that has the secret text value (without curly braces).

args.name: delay
args.doc: Delay between the single key strokes. It may be either a number or a Robot Framework time string. Time strings are fully explained in an appendix of Robot Framework User Guide. Defaults to 0 ms. Example: 50 ms

args.name: clear
args.doc: Set to False if the field should not be cleared before typing. Defaults to True.

keywords.name: Type Text
keywords.doc:
Types the given txt into the text field found by selector.

Sends a keydown, keypress/input, and keyup event for each character in the text.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

See Fill Text for filling the full text at once.

Example

Type Text    input#username_field    user
Type Text    input#username_field    user    delay=10 ms    clear=No

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Types the given ``txt`` into the text field found by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector of the text field. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: txt
args.doc: Text for the text field.

args.name: delay
args.doc: Delay between the single key strokes. It may be either a number or a Robot Framework time string. Time strings are fully explained in an appendix of Robot Framework User Guide. Defaults to 0 ms. Example: 50 ms

args.name: clear
args.doc: Set to False if the field should not be cleared before typing. Defaults to True.

keywords.name: Uncheck Checkbox
keywords.doc:
Unchecks the checkbox found by selector.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Does nothing if the element is not checked/selected.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Unchecks the checkbox found by ``selector``.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector of the checkbox. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: force
args.doc: Set to True to skip Playwright's Actionability checks.

keywords.name: Upload File By Selector
keywords.doc:
Uploads file from path to file input element matched by selector.

Fails if the upload is not done before the library timeout. Therefore it may be necessary to increase the timeout with Set Browser Timeout. It is possible to upload multiple files or folders by defining additional files or folders in extra_paths.

If a path is a directory, all files from the directory are uploaded. Subdirectories are not included. It is possible to upload files and directories with the same keyword. The keyword fails if a given path does not exist.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

If path is a FileUploadBuffer dictionary, then the structure should be:

{
  'name': str,
  'mimeType': str,
  'buffer': str
}

If path argument is FileUploadBuffer, then extra_paths argument is not supported and using it will raise an error.

Upload single file example:

Upload File By Selector    //input[@type='file']    big_file.zip

Upload many files example:

Upload File By Selector    //input[@type='file']    file1.zip    file2.zip    file3.zip

Upload folder example:

Upload File By Selector    //input[@type='file']    /path/to/folder

Upload as buffer example:

${text} =    Get File    /path/to/file    # Read file from disk
VAR    &{buffer}    name=not_here.txt    mimeType=text/plain    buffer=${text}    # Create buffer dictionary
Upload File By Selector    id=file_chooser    ${buffer}    # Upload buffer

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Uploads file from ``path`` to file input element matched by selector.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Identifies the file input element.

args.name: path
args.doc: Path to the file or folder to be uploaded. Can also be a FileUploadBuffer dictionary.

args.name: extra_paths
args.doc: Additional paths to files or folders to be uploaded.

keywords.name: Wait For
keywords.doc:
Waits for promises to finish and returns results from them.

Returns a single result if only one promise is waited for. Otherwise it returns a list of results in the same order as the promises were given. If one of the promises fails, then this keyword will fail.

See Promise To for more information about promises.

For general waiting of elements please see Implicit waiting.

Example:

${promise}=    Promise To            Wait For Response     matcher=     timeout=3
Click         \#delayed_request
${body}=       Wait For              ${promise}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Waits for promises to finish and returns results from them.

args.name: promises
args.doc: Promises to wait for.

keywords.name: Wait For Alert
keywords.doc:
Returns a promise to wait for next dialog on page, handles it with action and optionally verifies the dialogs text.

Dialog/alert can be any of alert, beforeunload, confirm or prompt.

The main difference between this keyword and Handle Future Dialogs is that the Handle Future Dialogs keyword is automatically set as a promise, but this keyword must be called as an argument to the Promise To keyword. Also this keyword can optionally verify the dialog text and returns it. If the text argument is None or is not set, the dialog text is not verified.

Example with returning text:

${promise} =         Promise To    Wait For Alert    action=accept
Click               id=alerts
${text} =            Wait For      ${promise}
Should Be Equal      ${text}         Am an alert

Example with text verification:

${promise} =       Promise To    Wait For Alert    action=accept    text=Am an alert
Click              id=alerts
${text} =          Wait For      ${promise}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns a promise to wait for next dialog on page, handles it with ``action`` and optionally verifies the dialogs text.

args.name: action
args.doc: How to handle the alert. Can be accept or dismiss.

args.name: prompt_input
args.doc: The value to enter into the prompt. Only valid if the action argument equals accept. Defaults to an empty string.

args.name: text
args.doc: Optional text to verify the dialog text with.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Optional timeout in Robot Framework time format. Defaults to the library timeout.

keywords.name: Wait For Alerts
keywords.doc:
Returns a promise to wait for multiple dialogs on a page.

Handles each alert/dialog with actions and optionally verifies the dialog texts. Dialog/alert can be any of alert, beforeunload, confirm or prompt.

There must be an equal amount of items in the actions, prompt_inputs and texts lists. Use None if texts and/or prompt inputs are not needed.

This keyword works in the same way as Wait For Alert, but it can handle multiple alerts with one promise. Like the Wait For Alert keyword, this keyword must be called as an argument to the Promise To keyword.

Example to handle two alerts, first one is accepted and second one is dismissed:

${promise} =    Promise To
...    Wait For Alerts
...    ["accept", "dismiss"]
...    [None, None]
...    [None, None]
Click    id=alerts
${texts} =    Wait For    ${promise}

Example to handle confirm and prompt alert. Example assumes that the first is a confirm and second one is prompt:

${promise} =    Promise To
...    Wait For Alerts
...    ["dismiss", "accept"]
...    [None, "I am a prompt"]
...    ["First alert accepted?", None]
Click    id=confirmAndPrompt
${texts} =    Wait For    ${promise}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Returns a promise to wait for multiple dialogs on a page.

args.name: actions
args.doc: List of how to handle the alerts. Can be accept or dismiss.

args.name: prompt_inputs
args.doc: List of the values to enter into the prompts. Only valid if the corresponding action equals accept. Use None if no input is needed.

args.name: texts
args.doc: List of optional texts to verify the dialog texts with. Use None if text verification should be disabled.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Optional timeout in Robot Framework time format. Defaults to the library timeout. The timeout is applied to each alert separately.

keywords.name: Wait For All Promises
keywords.doc:
Waits for all promises to finish.

Waits for all promises which have been created but not yet waited for with Wait For. If one of the promises fails, then this keyword will fail.

Example:

Promise To               Wait For Response     matcher=     timeout=3
Click                    \#delayed_request
Wait For All Promises

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Waits for all promises to finish.

keywords.name: Wait For Condition
keywords.doc:
Waits for a condition, defined with Browser getter keywords, to become True.

This keyword is basically just a wrapper around our assertion keywords, but with a timeout. It can be used to wait for anything that also can be asserted with our keywords.

In comparison to Robot Framework's Wait Until Keyword Succeeds this keyword is more readable and easier to use, but is limited to Browser library's assertion keywords.

The easiest way to use this keyword is first starting with an assertion keyword with assertion like: Get Text

Start:

Get Text    id=status_bar   contains    Done

Then you replace the word Get with Wait For Condition and if necessary add the timeout argument.

End:

Wait For Condition    Text    id=status_bar   contains    Done

Example usage:

Wait For Condition    Element States    id=cdk-overlay-0    ==    detached
Wait For Condition    Element States     //h1    contains    visible    editable    enabled    timeout=2 s
Wait For Condition    Title    should start with    Robot
Wait For Condition    Url    should end with    robotframework.org

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Waits for a condition, defined with Browser getter keywords, to become True.

args.name: condition
args.doc: A condition, defined with Browser getter keywords, without the word Get.

args.name: args
args.doc: Arguments to pass to the condition keyword.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Timeout to wait for the condition to become True. Uses default timeout of the library if not set. As the other assertion keywords this timeout only influences the time the assertion is retried. The browser timeout is used to wait for the element to be found.

args.name: message
args.doc: Overrides the default error message.

keywords.name: Wait For Elements State
keywords.doc:
Waits for the element found by selector to satisfy state option.

Note that Browser library has Implicit waiting mechanisms. Depending on the situation you might not need to use Wait for Elements State.

If users experience reliability issues with this keyword, consider using Wait for Condition with Get Element States keyword instead. Wait For Elements State uses features of Playwright to wait for element states. However, in some situations these features might not work as expected. Wait for Condition with Get Element States is more robust as it uses Browser library's own waiting mechanisms that actively poll the state of an element.

State options are appearing in or disappearing from the DOM, becoming visible or hidden, and the other states listed in ElementState. If at the moment of calling the keyword, the selector already satisfies the condition, the keyword will return immediately.

If the selector doesn't satisfy the condition within the timeout the keyword will FAIL.

The states focused and defocused are not supported with iframe selectors, which contain >>>. In that case the keyword raises an error and suggests to use Wait For Condition with Get Element States instead.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Example:

Wait For Elements State    //h1    visible    timeout=2 s
Wait For Elements State    //h1    focused    1s

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Waits for the element found by ``selector`` to satisfy state option.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector of the corresponding object. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: state
args.doc: See ElementState for explanation.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: uses default timeout from library if not set.

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message. The message argument accepts {selector}, {function}, and {timeout} format options. The {function} formatter is the state argument value for the states which are waited for by Playwright, that are attached, detached, visible, hidden, stable, enabled, disabled and editable. For all other states, it is the JavaScript expression which is evaluated for the element.

keywords.name: Wait For Function
keywords.doc:
Polls JavaScript expression or function in browser until it returns a (JavaScript) truthy value.

Keyword uses strict mode, see Finding elements for more details about strict mode.

Example usage:

${promise}      Promise To      Wait For Function    element => element.style.width=="100%"    selector=\#progress_bar    timeout=4s
Click         \#progress_bar
Wait For      ${promise}

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Polls JavaScript expression or function in browser until it returns a (JavaScript) truthy value.

args.name: function
args.doc: A valid javascript function or a javascript function body. For example () => true and true will behave similarly.

args.name: selector
args.doc: Selector to resolve and pass to the JavaScript function. This will be the first argument the function receives. If a selector is given, function must be a function with an argument which receives the element handle. For example (element) => document.activeElement === element. See the Finding elements section for details about the selectors.

args.name: polling
args.doc: Default polling value of raf polls in a callback for requestAnimationFrame. Any other value for polling will be parsed as a Robot Framework time for the interval between polls.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Uses default timeout of the library if not set.

args.name: message
args.doc: overrides the default error message. The message argument accepts {selector}, {function}, and {timeout} format options.

keywords.name: Wait For Load State
keywords.doc:
Waits until the page reaches the required load state.

This resolves when the page reaches a required load state, load by default. The navigation must have been committed when this method is called. If current document has already reached the required state, resolves immediately.

If the state has been already reached while loading current document, the underlying Playwright will resolve immediately. Can be one of:

load - wait for the load event to be fired.
domcontentloaded - wait for the DOMContentLoaded event to be fired.
networkidle - DISCOURAGED wait until there are no network connections for at least 500 ms.
commit - not supported by this keyword, the keyword returns immediately without waiting.

If the wait times out, the page's load report is logged: whether its navigation committed, how far the document got and which requests were still open.

Example:

Go To                         ${URL}
Wait For Load State    domcontentloaded    timeout=3s
keywords.shortdoc: Waits until the page reaches the required load state.

args.name: state
args.doc: State to wait for, defaults to load. Possible values are load, domcontentloaded, networkidle and commit.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Timeout supports Robot Framework time format. Uses browser timeout if not set.

keywords.name: Wait For Navigation
keywords.doc:
Waits until the page has navigated to the given url.

The keyword works only when the page is loaded and it does not work if only the URL fragment changes. Example: if https://marketsquare.github.io/robotframework-browser/Browser.html changes to https://marketsquare.github.io/robotframework-browser/Browser.html#Wait%20For%20Navigation the keyword will fail.

Example:

Go To                  ${ROOT_URL}/redirector.html
Wait for navigation    ${ROOT_URL}/posted.html    wait_until=${wait_until}

If the wait times out, the page's load report is logged: whether its navigation committed, how far the document got and which requests were still open.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Waits until the page has navigated to the given ``url``.

args.name: url
args.doc: Expected navigation target address, either a Glob-Pattern (a plain string without wildcards matches exactly) or a JavaScript-like regex wrapped in / symbols, as in Wait For Response. An invalid RegExp fails at once.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Timeout supports Robot Framework time format. Uses default timeout if not set.

args.name: wait_until
args.doc: When to consider the operation succeeded, defaults to load. Events can be either: domcontentloaded - consider operation to be finished when the DOMContentLoaded event is fired. load - consider operation to be finished when the load event is fired. networkidle - consider operation to be finished when there are no network connections for at least 500 ms. commit - consider operation to be finished when network response is received and the document started loading.

keywords.name: Wait For Request
keywords.doc:
Waits for a request matching matcher to be made and returns it as a CapturedRequest.

By default only the request is awaited, not its response. The keyword returns as soon as the request is sent, so redirectedTo is always None here. See Wait For Response if the response is needed.

The returned CapturedRequest mirrors Playwright's Request: the URL, method, headers (allHeaders includes cookie), the raw body as postDataBuffer, the parsed body as postDataJSON, the resource type and more. Its documentation lists every key and the parsing rules of the legacy postData key.

The request is logged without its body. allHeaders and headersArray can contain cookies, so they are logged only at DEBUG level. The body is logged at TRACE level: as formatted JSON when it is JSON, as text when it is UTF-8, otherwise as base64.

Example:

${promise} =    Promise To    Wait For Request    **/api/login    wait_for_all_fields=True
Click    id=login_button
${request} =    Wait For    ${promise}
Should Contain    ${request.allHeaders}[cookie]    consent=

See Wait For Response for more details about the matcher.

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Waits for a request matching ``matcher`` to be made and returns it as a `CapturedRequest`.

args.name: matcher
args.doc: Request URL matcher. Can be a string (Glob-Pattern), a JavaScript RegExp (enclosed in / with optional trailing flags) or a JavaScript arrow-function that receives the Request object and returns a boolean. By default (with an empty string) the first request is matched. The matcher syntax is the same as in Wait For Response, see its matcher examples. An invalid RegExp fails at once. For additional information, see the Playwright waitForRequest documentation.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Timeout supports Robot Framework time format. Uses default timeout if not set.

args.name: wait_for_all_fields
args.doc: Some fields are known only later than the request itself: Chromium and WebKit report allHeaders and headersArray only when the response headers arrive. With the default False the keyword returns at once and those fields are None. With True it also waits for them, within timeout, and fails if they do not arrive in time or the browser cannot report them, for example because the page closed.

keywords.name: Wait For Response
keywords.doc:
Waits for a response matching matcher and returns it as a CapturedResponse.

The keyword waits until the response headers are received and then reads the response body.

The returned CapturedResponse mirrors Playwright's Response: the status, headers (allHeaders includes set-cookie), the body as bytes, text and json, the HTTP version, server address, TLS details and the CapturedRequest it answers. Its documentation lists every key and the parsing rules of the legacy body key.

The response is logged without its body. allHeaders and headersArray can contain cookies, so they are logged only at DEBUG level. The body is logged at TRACE level: as formatted JSON when it is JSON, as text when it is UTF-8, otherwise as base64.

Binary data: bytes and request.postDataBuffer hold real bytes when read by key, as ${response.bytes} or ${response}[bytes]. Everything that reads the dictionary through items() gets them as base64 text instead, so that the dictionary can be serialized with json.dumps:

  • &{response} = assignment copies the outer dictionary through items(), so after it bytes is base64 text, while request.postDataBuffer stays bytes. Assign with ${response} = to keep the real bytes everywhere.
  • FOR ... IN &{response}, Get Dictionary Items and json.dumps return base64 text.
  • The variables view of the RobotCode debugger shows base64 text.

Matcher Examples:

Glob-Pattern:

Glob-Patterns are strings that can contain wildcards. Possible wildcards/patterns are:

  • * matches any number of characters, except /
  • ** matches any number of characters, including /
  • {foo,bar,baz} matches one of the strings in the braces (in this example foo, bar or baz)

?, [ and ] match literally. To match exactly one character or a character class, use a RegExp (/.../, see below).

Example:

Wait For Response    **/api/get/text    # matches any response with url ending with /api/get/text. example: https://browser.fi/api/get/text

RegExp:

Regular Expressions are JavaScript regular expressions enclosed in / with optional trailing flags. Any matcher that starts with / and ends with /, or with / and only the flag letters gimsuy, is read as a RegExp. So a relative glob such as /api/users/ or /api/items/my is a RegExp, api/users and api/items with the flags my. Write it as **/api/users/ to match it as a glob. Be aware that backslashes need to be escaped in Robot Framework, e.g. \\w instead of \w. See regex101 for more information on Regular Expressions.

Example:

Wait For Response    /http://\\w+:\\d+/api/get/text/i    # matches any response with url ending with /api/get/text and containing http:// followed by any word and port. example: http://localhost:8080/api/get/text

JavaScript Arrow-Function:

JavaScript Arrow-Functions are anonymous JavaScript functions that receive the Response object and return a boolean.

Example:

Wait For Response    response => response.url() === 'http://localhost/api/post' && response.status() === 200    # matches any response with url http://localhost/api/post and status code 200

Robot Examples:

Synchronous Example:

Click                \#delayed_request    # Creates response which should be waited before next actions
Wait For Response    matcher=/http://\\w+:\\d+/api/get/text/i
Click                \#save

Asynchronous Example:

${promise} =    Promise To    Wait For Response    timeout=60s
Click           \#delayed_request    # Creates response which should be waited before pressing save.
Click           \#next
Wait For        ${promise}            # Waits for the response
Click           \#save

JavaScript Function Example:

Click               \#delayed_request    # Creates response which should be waited before pressing save.
Wait For Response   response => response.url().endsWith('json') && response.request().method() === 'GET'

Asserting the JSON body, a cookie and saving a binary body:

${promise} =       Promise To    Wait For Response    matcher=**/api/login
Click            id=login-button
${response} =      Wait For      ${promise}
Should Be Equal    ${response.json.user}    demo
Should Contain     ${response.allHeaders}[set-cookie]    sessionid=

${logo} =          Promise To    Wait For Response    matcher=**/logo.png
Go To            ${URL}
${response} =      Wait For      ${logo}
Create Binary File    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/logo.png    ${response.bytes}

Waiting only for the status of a large download:

${response} =      Wait For Response    **/export.zip    include_body=False
Should Be Equal As Integers    ${response.status}    200

Comment >>
keywords.shortdoc: Waits for a response matching ``matcher`` and returns it as a `CapturedResponse`.

args.name: matcher
args.doc: Response URL matcher. Can be a string (Glob-Pattern), a JavaScript RegExp (enclosed in / with optional trailing flags) or a JavaScript arrow-function that receives the Response object and returns a boolean. By default (with an empty string) the first response is matched. An invalid RegExp fails at once. For additional information, see the Playwright page.waitForResponse documentation.

args.name: timeout
args.doc: Timeout supports Robot Framework time format. Uses default timeout if not set. It covers both the wait for the response and reading its body and other fields; the keyword fails if they do not arrive in time.

args.name: include_body
args.doc: If False, the response body is not read and not transferred, and body, bytes, text and json are None. Use it when only the status or headers matter and the body is large or never ends. httpVersion, serverAddr and securityDetails are then None too, because some browsers report them only after the whole body has arrived: httpVersion in Firefox and WebKit, the other two in WebKit.

typedocs.name: AbortErrorCode
typedocs.doc:
The network error that Abort Requests makes an aborted request fail with.

The members are Playwright's error codes. The page sees the request fail with that network error, for example net::ERR_TIMED_OUT in Chromium for timedout. Firefox and WebKit report most codes as one generic failure.

  • aborted: The operation was aborted, by the user or by the page.
  • accessdenied: Permission to access a resource, other than the network, was denied.
  • addressunreachable: The IP address is unreachable.
  • blockedbyclient: The client chose to block the request.
  • blockedbyresponse: The request failed because the response came with requirements that were not met, for example X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy.
  • connectionaborted: The connection timed out because no ACK was received for data sent.
  • connectionclosed: The connection was closed.
  • connectionfailed: The connection attempt failed.
  • connectionrefused: The connection attempt was refused.
  • connectionreset: The connection was reset.
  • internetdisconnected: The Internet connection was lost.
  • namenotresolved: The host name could not be resolved.
  • timedout: The operation timed out.
  • failed: A generic failure. The default.

typedocs.name: APIResponse
typedocs.doc:
The response of Send API Request.

The keys mirror Playwright's APIResponse. The value is a Robot Framework dictionary, so keys can be accessed as ${response.status} or ${response}[status].

Key Description
status The HTTP status code, e.g. 200.
statusText The status text, e.g. OK.
ok True if status is in the range 200-299.
url The final URL of the response, after redirects.
headers Dictionary of all response headers, set-cookie included, with lower-case names. Repeated headers are joined: set-cookie with a new line, the others with , .
headersArray List of all response headers as name and value dictionaries, with the names as the server sent them and one entry for each repeated header.
bytes The raw response body as bytes. Use it for binary content such as images.
text The response body decoded as UTF-8. Invalid bytes become the replacement character U+FFFD.
json The response body parsed as JSON regardless of the content-type. None if the body is not valid JSON. A body of null is also None; text tells the two apart.

bytes, text and json follow the same rules as in HttpResponse and CapturedResponse. There is no legacy body key.

Assigned with &{response} =, bytes holds base64 text. Assign with ${response} = to get the raw bytes.

Example

{
  "status": 201,
  "statusText": "Created",
  "ok": true,
  "url": "https://example.com/api/users",
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
    "set-cookie": "session=abc; Path=/"
  },
  "headersArray": [
    {"name": "Content-Type", "value": "application/json; charset=utf-8"},
    {"name": "Set-Cookie", "value": "session=abc; Path=/"}
  ],
  "bytes": "eyJuYW1lIjoicm9ib3QifQ==",
  "text": "{\"name\":\"robot\"}",
  "json": {
    "name": "robot"
  }
}

typedocs.name: AssertionOperator
typedocs.doc:
Currently supported assertion operators are:

Operator Alternative Operators Description Validate Equivalent
== equal, equals, should be Checks if returned value is equal to expected value. value == expected
!= inequal, should not be Checks if returned value is not equal to expected value. value != expected
> greater than Checks if returned value is greater than expected value. value > expected
>= Checks if returned value is greater than or equal to expected value. value >= expected
< less than Checks if returned value is less than expected value. value < expected
<= Checks if returned value is less than or equal to expected value. value <= expected
*= contains Checks if returned value contains expected value as substring. expected in value
not contains Checks if returned value does not contain expected value as substring. expected in value
^= should start with, starts Checks if returned value starts with expected value. re.search(f"^{expected}", value)
$= should end with, ends Checks if returned value ends with expected value. re.search(f"{expected}$", value)
matches Checks if given RegEx matches minimum once in returned value. re.search(expected, value)
validate Checks if given Python expression evaluates to True.
evaluate then When using this operator, the keyword does return the evaluated Python expression.

There are three different possibilities what keyword returns when matches operator is used: string, tuple or dictionary. What keyword returns depends on how the RegEx is formed. If RegEx does not contain group(s), then keyword will return the string without modifications. If RegEx contains groups, meaning (...), then keyword will return a tuple. Each tuple item contains the text which is matched by the group. If there is group and group has a name, (?P<name>...) syntax, then keyword returns a dictionary. In this case dictionary key is the group name and value contains the matched text. If there mix of groups and groups with names, then tuple is returned.

Currently supported formatters for assertions are:

Formatter Description
normalize spaces Substitutes multiple spaces to single space from the value
strip Removes spaces from the beginning and end of the value
case insensitive Converts value to lower case before comparing
apply to expected Applies rules also for the expected value

Formatters are applied to the value before assertion is performed and keywords returns a value where rule is applied. Formatter is only applied to the value which keyword returns and not all rules are valid for all assertion operators. If apply to expected formatter is defined, then formatters are then formatter are also applied to expected value.

typedocs.name: AutoClosingLevel
typedocs.doc:
Controls when contexts and pages are closed during the test execution.

If automatic closing level is TEST, contexts and pages that are created during a single test are automatically closed when the test ends. Contexts and pages that are created during suite setup are closed when the suite teardown ends.

If automatic closing level is SUITE, all contexts and pages that are created during the test suite are closed when the suite teardown ends.

If automatic closing level is MANUAL, nothing is closed automatically while the test execution is ongoing. All browsers, context and pages are automatically closed when test execution ends.

If automatic closing level is KEEP, nothing is closed automatically while the test execution is ongoing. Also, nothing is closed when test execution ends, including the node process. Therefore, it is users responsibility to close all browsers, context and pages and ensure that all process that are left running after the test execution end are closed. This level is only intended for test case development and must not be used when running tests in CI or similar environments.

Automatic closing can be configured or switched off with the auto_closing_level library import parameter.

See: Importing

typedocs.doc:

Other strings and all other values are passed as-is, allowing keywords to handle them specially if needed. All string comparisons are case-insensitive.

Examples: TRUE (converted to True), off (converted to False), example (used as-is)

typedocs.name: bytes
typedocs.doc:
Strings are converted to bytes so that each Unicode code point below 256 is directly mapped to a matching byte. Higher code points are not allowed. Robot Framework's \xHH escape syntax is convenient with bytes having non-printable values.

Examples: good, hyvä (same as hyv\xE4), \x00 (the null byte)

Integers and sequences of integers are converted to matching bytes directly. They must be in range 0-255.

Examples: 0 (converted to the null byte), [82, 70] (converted to RF)

Support for integers and sequences of integers is new in Robot Framework 7.4.

typedocs.name: CapturedRequest
typedocs.doc:
A request captured by Wait For Request, and the request of a CapturedResponse.

The keys mirror Playwright's Request. The value is a Robot Framework dictionary, so keys can be accessed as ${request.method} or ${request}[method].

Key Description
url The URL of the request.
method The HTTP method, e.g. GET or POST.
headers Dictionary of request headers with lower-case names. Like Playwright's headers() it leaves out security-related headers such as cookie.
allHeaders Dictionary of all request headers, including cookie and the headers the browser adds. None in Wait For Request unless wait_for_all_fields is True, and in Wait For Response if the browser could not report them, for example because the page closed.
headersArray List of dictionaries with name and value. Unlike the dictionaries it keeps headers that occur several times, and names keep their original case. None like allHeaders.
postData Legacy. The request body, parsed as described in Parsing rules below. Prefer postDataBuffer or postDataJSON.
postDataBuffer The raw request body as bytes, or None if the request has no body.
postDataJSON The request body parsed like Playwright's postDataJSON(): a dictionary for a application/x-www-form-urlencoded body, the parsed value for a JSON body, otherwise None.
resourceType The resource type as the browser sees it, e.g. document, xhr, fetch or image.
isNavigationRequest True if the request drives a frame navigation.
redirectedFrom The URL of the request that was redirected to this one, or None.
redirectedTo The URL this request was redirected to, or None. It is None in Wait For Request, because the redirect is not known when the request is sent.
frame Dictionary with the url and name of the frame that issued the request, or None if Playwright cannot tell, e.g. for Service Worker requests.

Example

A login request sent with fetch, as Wait For Request returns it with wait_for_all_fields=True, with made-up values, as JSON. postDataBuffer is shown as base64 text, the way json.dumps writes it.

{
  "url": "https://example.com/api/login",
  "method": "POST",
  "headers": {
    "accept": "application/json",
    "content-type": "application/json",
    "referer": "https://example.com/login",
    "user-agent": "Mozilla/5.0 Chrome/141.0"
  },
  "allHeaders": {
    "accept": "application/json",
    "content-type": "application/json",
    "referer": "https://example.com/login",
    "user-agent": "Mozilla/5.0 Chrome/141.0",
    "cookie": "consent=yes"
  },
  "headersArray": [
    {
      "name": "Accept",
      "value": "application/json"
    },
    {
      "name": "Content-Type",
      "value": "application/json"
    },
    {
      "name": "Cookie",
      "value": "consent=yes"
    },
    {
      "name": "Referer",
      "value": "https://example.com/login"
    },
    {
      "name": "User-Agent",
      "value": "Mozilla/5.0 Chrome/141.0"
    }
  ],
  "postData": {
    "user": "demo",
    "password": "secret"
  },
  "postDataBuffer": "eyJ1c2VyIjoiZGVtbyIsInBhc3N3b3JkIjoic2VjcmV0In0=",
  "postDataJSON": {
    "user": "demo",
    "password": "secret"
  },
  "resourceType": "fetch",
  "isNavigationRequest": false,
  "redirectedFrom": null,
  "redirectedTo": null,
  "frame": {
    "url": "https://example.com/login",
    "name": ""
  }
}

Parsing rules

postData is kept as it always was, and its parsing depends on where it is returned:

  • In Wait For Request the body is parsed as JSON regardless of the content-type. A body that is not valid JSON is returned as a string, and a request without a body returns None. JSON is not limited to objects: 42 becomes a number and true a boolean.
  • As request.postData of Wait For Response the body is parsed as JSON only when the request's content-type contains application/json. Otherwise it is the raw string.

postDataBuffer and postDataJSON are the same in both places.

Binary data and JSON

postDataBuffer holds real bytes. The dictionary can still be serialized with json.dumps, which writes bytes as base64 text. Robot Framework's &{request} = assignment copies the dictionary the same way, so after it postDataBuffer is base64 text. Assign it with ${request} = to keep the real bytes. The variables view of the RobotCode debugger reads the dictionary the same way, so it shows postDataBuffer as base64 text, while ${request.postDataBuffer} still returns the real bytes.

typedocs.name: CapturedResponse
typedocs.doc:
A response captured by Wait For Response.

The keys mirror Playwright's Response. The value is a Robot Framework dictionary, so keys can be accessed as ${response.status} or ${response}[status].

Key Description
status The HTTP status code, e.g. 200.
statusText The status text, e.g. OK. Not all browsers report it.
ok True if status is in the range 200-299.
url The URL of the response.
headers Dictionary of response headers with lower-case names. Like Playwright's headers() it leaves out security-related headers such as set-cookie.
allHeaders Dictionary of all response headers, including set-cookie. Several set-cookie headers are joined with a line break. None if the browser could not report them, for example because the page closed.
headersArray List of dictionaries with name and value. Unlike the dictionaries it keeps headers that occur several times, and names keep their original case. None like allHeaders.
body Legacy. The response body, parsed as described in Parsing rules below. Prefer json, text or bytes.
bytes The raw response body as bytes. Use it for binary content such as images.
text The response body decoded as UTF-8, like Playwright's text(). Invalid bytes become the replacement character U+FFFD.
json The response body parsed as JSON regardless of the content-type, like Playwright's json(). None if the body is not valid JSON. A body of null is also None; text tells the two apart.
httpVersion The HTTP version, e.g. HTTP/1.1 or h2. None if Playwright cannot read it, or with include_body=False.
serverAddr Dictionary with the ipAddress and port of the server. None if Playwright cannot read it, or with include_body=False.
securityDetails ( SecurityDetails ) TLS details of a HTTPS response: a dictionary with the optional keys issuer and subjectName (certificate Common Names), protocol (e.g. TLS 1.3), and validFrom and validTo (Unix timestamps in seconds). Without TLS it is None or an empty dictionary, depending on the browser. None with include_body=False.
fromServiceWorker True if a Service Worker answered the request.
request The CapturedRequest that this response answers.

body, bytes, text and json are None when the body cannot be read, for example for a redirect response, or when Wait For Response was called with include_body=False.

      "content-type": "application/json",
      "referer": "https://example.com/login",
      "user-agent": "Mozilla/5.0 Chrome/141.0"
    },
    "allHeaders": {
      "accept": "application/json",
      "content-type": "application/json",
      "referer": "https://example.com/login",
      "user-agent": "Mozilla/5.0 Chrome/141.0",
      "cookie": "consent=yes"
    },
    "headersArray": [
      {
        "name": "Accept",
        "value": "application/json"
      },
      {
        "name": "Content-Type",
        "value": "application/json"
      },
      {
        "name": "Cookie",
        "value": "consent=yes"
      },
      {
        "name": "Referer",
        "value": "https://example.com/login"
      },
      {
        "name": "User-Agent",
        "value": "Mozilla/5.0 Chrome/141.0"
      }
    ],
    "postData": {
      "user": "demo",
      "password": "secret"
    },
    "postDataBuffer": "eyJ1c2VyIjoiZGVtbyIsInBhc3N3b3JkIjoic2VjcmV0In0=",
    "postDataJSON": {
      "user": "demo",
      "password": "secret"
    },
    "resourceType": "fetch",
    "isNavigationRequest": false,
    "redirectedFrom": null,
    "redirectedTo": null,
    "frame": {
      "url": "https://example.com/login",
      "name": ""
    }
  }
}

Parsing rules

body is kept as it always was: it is parsed as JSON regardless of the content-type, and a body that is not valid JSON is returned as the decoded text. So {"a": 1} becomes a dictionary, [1, 2] a list, 42 a number and true a boolean, even when the server sends them as text/plain. An empty body is an empty string. That holds even when the browser keeps no body at all, as WebKit does for a 204, 205 or 304 response or one with content-length: 0. NaN and Infinity are not valid JSON and stay text.

json follows the same parsing but is None where body falls back to text. It is a string only when the body is a valid JSON string such as "abc".

Binary data and JSON

bytes and request.postDataBuffer hold real bytes. The dictionary can still be serialized with json.dumps, which writes bytes as base64 text. Robot Framework's &{response} = assignment copies only the outer dictionary the same way, so after it bytes is base64 text while request.postDataBuffer keeps its real bytes. Assign it with ${response} = to keep the real bytes everywhere:

${response} =    Wait For Response    **/logo.png
Create Binary File    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/logo.png    ${response.bytes}

The variables view of the RobotCode debugger reads the dictionary the same way, so it shows bytes and request.postDataBuffer as base64 text. ${response.bytes} still returns the real bytes.

typedocs.name: ClientCertificate
typedocs.doc:
Defines client certificate.

  • origin Exact origin that the certificate is valid for. Origin includes https protocol, a hostname and optionally a port.
  • certPath Optional Path to the file with the certificate in PEM format.
  • keyPath Optional Path to the file with the private key in PEM format.
  • pfxPath Optional Path to the PFX or PKCS12 encoded private key and certificate chain.

typedocs.name: CLockAdvanceType
typedocs.doc:
Defines how time is advanced.

fast_forward: Advance the clock by jumping forward in time. run_for: Advance the clock, firing all the time-related callbacks.

fast_forward will Only fires due timers at most once. This is equivalent to user closing the laptop lid for a while and reopening it later, after given time.

typedocs.name: ClockType
typedocs.doc:
Defines how time is set.

The recommended approach is to use fixed to set the time to a specific value.

fixed: Sets the fixed time for Date.now() and new Date(). system: Is only recommended for advanced use cases. install: initializes the clock and allows you to: pause_at: Pauses the time at a specific time. fast_forward: Fast forwards the time. run_for: Runs the time for a specific duration. resume: Resumes the time.

  • Page: The active page only.

typedocs.name: CookieSameSite
typedocs.doc:
Enum that defines the Cookie SameSite type.

It controls whether or not a cookie is sent with cross-site requests, providing some protection against cross-site request forgery attacks (CSRF).

The possible attribute values are:

Value Description
Strict Means that the browser sends the cookie only for same-site requests, that is, requests originating from the same site that set the cookie. If a request originates from a different domain or scheme (even with the same domain), no cookies with the SameSite=Strict attribute are sent.
Lax Means that the cookie is not sent on cross-site requests, such as on requests to load images or frames, but is sent when a user is navigating to the origin site from an external site (for example, when following a link). This is the default behavior if the SameSite attribute is not specified.
None means that the browser sends the cookie with both cross-site and same-site requests. The Secure attribute must also be set when setting this value.

See MDN Set-Cookie for more information.

typedocs.doc: Enum that defines the Cookie type.

typedocs.doc:

typedocs.name: datetime
typedocs.doc:
String timestamps are expected to be in ISO 8601 like format YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.mmmmmm, where any non-digit character can be used as a separator or separators can be omitted altogether. Additionally, only the date part is mandatory, all possibly missing time components are considered to be zeros.

A special values NOW and TODAY (case-insensitive) can be used to get the current local datetime. This is new in Robot Framework 7.3.

Integers and floats are considered to represent seconds since the Unix epoch.

Examples: 2022-02-09T16:39:43.632269, 20220209 16:39, now, ${1644417583.632269} (Epoch time)

typedocs.doc:
Strings must be Python dictionary literals. They are converted to actual dictionaries using the ast.literal_eval function. They can contain any values ast.literal_eval supports, including dictionaries and other collections.

Any mapping is accepted and converted to a dict.

If the type has nested types like dict[str, int], items are converted to those types automatically. This in new in Robot Framework 6.0.

typedocs.doc:
Downloaded file information.

Key Description

suggestedFilename is the suggested filename that was computed from the Content-Disposition response header.
state is the state of the download. i.e. in_progress, finished or canceled.

typedocs.name: ElementRole
typedocs.doc:
Role selector does not replace accessibility audits and conformance tests, but rather gives early feedback about the ARIA guidelines.

Many html elements have an implicitly defined role that is recognized by the role selector. You can find all the supported roles here. ARIA guidelines do not recommend duplicating implicit roles and attributes by setting role and/or aria-* attributes to default values.

typedocs.name: ElementState
typedocs.doc:
Enum that defines the state an element can have.

The following states are possible:

State Description
attached to be present in DOM.
detached to not be present in DOM.
visible to have non or empty bounding box and no visibility:hidden.
hidden to be detached from DOM, or have an empty bounding box or visibility:hidden.
enabled to not be disabled.
disabled to be disabled. Can be used on <button>, <fieldset>, <input>, <optgroup>, <option>, <select> and <textarea>.
editable to not be readOnly.
readonly to be readOnly. Can be used on <input> and <textarea>.
selected to be selected. Can be used on <option>.
deselected to not be selected.
focused to be the activeElement.
defocused to not be the activeElement.
checked to be checked. Can be used on <input>.
unchecked to not be checked.
stable to be both visible and stable.

typedocs.name: FetchCache
typedocs.doc:
How HTTP uses the browser's HTTP cache, the fetch cache option.

Value Description
default Uses the cache by the normal HTTP rules. The browser's default.
no-store Ignores the cache and does not store the response.
reload Ignores the cache but stores the response.
no-cache Asks the server to revalidate a cached response.
force-cache Uses any cached response, even a stale one.
only-if-cached Uses only a cached response and fails without one. Requires mode=same-origin.

See MDN RequestInit cache.

typedocs.name: FetchCredentials
typedocs.doc:
Whether HTTP sends cookies and HTTP authentication, the fetch credentials option.

Value Description
omit Never sends them.
same-origin Sends them only to the page's own origin. The browser's default.
include Sends them to every origin, also cross-origin. The server must allow credentials with CORS.

See MDN RequestInit credentials.

typedocs.name: FetchMode
typedocs.doc:
Which cross-origin requests HTTP allows, the fetch mode option.

Value Description
cors Allows cross-origin requests under the CORS rules. The browser's default.
no-cors Sends a cross-origin request without CORS. The response is of type opaque: status 0, no headers and an empty body. Only GET, HEAD and POST with simple headers are allowed.
same-origin Fails on a cross-origin request.

See MDN RequestInit mode.

typedocs.name: FetchPriority
typedocs.doc:
The priority of an HTTP request relative to the page's other requests, the fetch priority option.

Value Description
high Higher than other requests of the same kind.
low Lower than other requests of the same kind.
auto The browser decides. The default.

Browsers that do not support it ignore it. See MDN RequestInit priority.

typedocs.name: FetchRedirect
typedocs.doc:
How HTTP handles a redirect response, the fetch redirect option.

Value Description
follow Follows the redirect. The browser's default.
error Fails on a redirect.
manual Returns the redirect itself as a response of type opaqueredirect with status 0; its headers and body cannot be read.

See MDN RequestInit redirect.

typedocs.doc:
Dictionary that contains information about a file upload buffer.

{

typedocs.doc:

typedocs.name: FormFields
typedocs.doc:
Form fields: a dictionary of field names and values, used by HTTP and Send API Request.

A value is a string, a number or a boolean. Numbers are sent as their text and a boolean as true or false, the way JavaScript writes them. Any other value, such as a nested dictionary or a list, fails before the request is sent.

Names and values are encoded completely, so they can hold any character: a space, &, =, + or % arrives at the server as written.

VAR    &{fields} =    username=demo    password=a&b=c    remember=${True}
${response} =    HTTP    /login    POST    form=${fields}
# sent as: username=demo&password=a%26b%3Dc&remember=true

typedocs.name: GeoLocation
typedocs.doc:
Defines the geolocation.

  • latitude Latitude between -90 and 90.
  • longitude Longitude between -180 and 180.
  • accuracy Optional Non-negative accuracy value. Defaults to 0.

Example usage: {'latitude': 59.95, 'longitude': 30.31667}
