typedocs.doc:
Presenter mode configuration options.

duration Sets for how long the selector shall be highlighted. Defaults to 5s => 5 seconds.

width Sets the width of the higlight border. Defaults to 2px.

style Sets the style of the border. Defaults to dotted.

color Sets the color of the border, default is blue. Valid colors i.e. are: red, blue, yellow, pink, black

typedocs.name: HighlightMode
typedocs.doc:
Highlight mode for the element.

border: Highlights the element with a border outside of the selected element. This is the classic way to highlight an element of Browser librarary.

playwright: Highlights the element with Playwrights built in function.

both: Highlights the element with both methods.

typedocs.name: HttpCredentials
typedocs.doc:
Sets the credentials for http basic-auth.

origin: Restrain sending http credentials on specific origin (scheme://host:port). Credentials for HTTP authentication. If no origin is specified, the username and password are sent to any servers upon unauthorized responses.

Can be defined as robot dictionary or as string literal. Does not reveal secrets in Robot Framework logs. Instead, username and password values are resolved internally. Please note that if enable_playwright_debug is enabled in the library import, secret will be always visible as plain text in the playwright debug logs, regardless of the Robot Framework log level.

Example as literal:

${pwd} =    Set Variable    1234
${username} =    Set Variable    admin
New Context
...    httpCredentials={'username': '$username', 'password': '$pwd'}

Example as robot variable

*** Variables ***
${username}=       admin
${pwd}=            1234
&{credentials}=    username=$username    password=$pwd

*** Keywords ***
Open Context
   New Context    httpCredentials=${credentials}

typedocs.name: HttpHeaderChanges
typedocs.doc:
Changes to real HTTP headers: a dictionary of header names and new values.

Used by Modify Responses. A value is the same as in HttpHeaders: a string, a Robot Framework Secret, a number or a boolean. In addition, None removes the header. A given value replaces the real one, whatever its case, and an empty string sends the header empty.

VAR    &{changes} =    X-Cache=${None}    X-Debug=${True}
Modify Responses    **/api/orders    headers=${changes}    # removes X-Cache

typedocs.name: HttpHeaders
typedocs.doc:
HTTP headers: a dictionary of header names and values.

Used by HTTP, Send API Request, Mock Responses and the extraHTTPHeaders of New Context and New Persistent Context. Header names are case-insensitive. The dictionary can also be written as text, such as {"X-Tenant": "a"}.

A value is a string, a Robot Framework Secret, a number or a boolean. Numbers are sent as their text and a boolean as true or false, the way JavaScript writes them. An empty string sends an empty header. None, a dictionary or a list fails before the request is sent. A Secret is revealed only when it is sent, and header values are never logged above DEBUG level.

VAR    ${token: Secret} =    %{API_TOKEN}
VAR    &{headers} =    Authorization=${token}    X-Retry=${2}
Send API Request    /api/orders    headers=${headers}    # X-Retry: 2

typedocs.name: HttpResponse
typedocs.doc:
The response of HTTP, read from the response the page's fetch received.

The keys mirror the browser's fetch Response. The value is a Robot Framework dictionary, so keys can be accessed as ${response.status} or ${response}[status].

Key Description
status The HTTP status code, e.g. 200. 0 for a response of type opaque or opaqueredirect.
statusText The status text, e.g. OK. Empty over HTTP/2.
ok True if status is in the range 200-299.
url The final URL of the response, after redirects.
headers Dictionary of the response headers the page can read, with lower-case names. The browser leaves out set-cookie, joins repeated headers with , and, for a cross-origin response, shows only the headers CORS exposes.
redirected True if the response is the result of a redirect.
type basic for a same-origin response, cors for a cross-origin one, opaque for mode=no-cors and opaqueredirect for redirect=manual.
body Legacy. Parsed as JSON when the content-type is JSON, otherwise text. Prefer json, text or bytes.
bytes The raw response body as bytes. Use it for binary content such as images.
text The response body decoded as UTF-8, like fetch's text(). Invalid bytes become the replacement character U+FFFD.
json The response body parsed as JSON regardless of the content-type. None if the body is not valid JSON. A body of null is also None; text tells the two apart.

The keys status, statusText, ok, url, bytes, text and json mean the same as in CapturedResponse, so a response of HTTP can be compared with the one Wait For Response captures for the same request. Two keys differ: headers holds only what the page can read, while CapturedResponse sees every header but security-related ones such as set-cookie; and the legacy body of HTTP is parsed as JSON only with a JSON content-type, while that of CapturedResponse is parsed whenever it is valid JSON.

Example

{
  "status": 200,
  "statusText": "OK",
  "ok": true,
  "url": "https://example.com/api/user",
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
    "content-length": "33"
  },
  "redirected": false,
  "type": "basic",
  "body": {
    "user": "demo",
    "roles": [
      "admin"
    ]
  },
  "bytes": "eyJ1c2VyIjoiZGVtbyIsInJvbGVzIjpbImFkbWluIl19",
  "text": "{\"user\":\"demo\",\"roles\":[\"admin\"]}",
  "json": {
    "user": "demo",
    "roles": [
      "admin"
    ]
  }
}

bytes is shown as base64 text, the way json.dumps writes it.

typedocs.name: integer
typedocs.doc:
Conversion is done using Python's int built-in function. Floating point numbers are accepted only if they can be represented as integers exactly. For example, 1.0 is accepted and 1.1 is not.

It is possible to use hexadecimal, octal and binary numbers by prefixing values with 0x, 0o and 0b, respectively. Spaces and underscores can be used as visual separators for digit grouping purposes.

Examples: 42, -1, 0b1010, 10 000 000, 0xBAD_C0FFEE

typedocs.name: JsonSerializable
typedocs.doc:
A value that the keyword sends as JSON: a dictionary, a list, a string, a number, a boolean or None.

The value is sent as compact JSON, the way JavaScript's JSON.stringify writes it: {"id":7,"tags":["new"]}. A dictionary or a list holds only such values. NaN, Infinity and values JSON cannot hold, such as a set or a date, fail before the request is sent.

Where an argument also takes text, such as body of HTTP or data of Send API Request, a string is sent as the text it is, and only the other values are sent as JSON. Where the argument is JSON only, such as json of Mock Responses, a string is sent as a JSON string, in quotes.

VAR    &{order} =    id=${7}    tags=${{ ["new"] }}
HTTP    /api/orders    POST    ${order}    # sends {"id":7,"tags":["new"]}
Mock Responses    **/api/orders    json=${{ [] }}    # answers []

typedocs.name: KeyAction
typedocs.doc: Enum that defines which Keyboard Key action to perform.

typedocs.name: KeyboardInputAction
typedocs.doc:
Enum that defines how Keyboard Input adds the text into the page.

insertText is mostly similar to pasting of text.

type is similar to typing by pressing keys on the keyboard.

typedocs.name: KeyboardModifier
typedocs.doc:
Modifier keys to press while doing other actions.

Modifiers that are pressed during the Hover or Click.

typedocs.name: LambdaFunction
typedocs.doc:
Python lambda function.

The string must start with lambda and the function must accept one argument.

Example: lambda value: value.lower().replace(' ', '')

typedocs.name: list
typedocs.doc:
Strings must be Python list or tuple literals. They are converted using the ast.literal_eval function and possible tuples converted further to lists. They can contain any values ast.literal_eval supports, including lists and other collections.

If the argument is a list, it is used without conversion. Tuples and other sequences are converted to lists.

If the type has nested types like list[int], items are converted to those types automatically.

Examples: ['one', 'two'], [('one', 1), ('two', 2)]

Support to convert nested types is new in Robot Framework 6.0. Support for tuple literals is new in Robot Framework 7.4.

typedocs.name: Mapping
typedocs.doc:
Strings must be Python dictionary literals. They are converted to actual dictionaries using the ast.literal_eval function. They can contain any values ast.literal_eval supports, including dictionaries and other collections.

Any mapping is accepted without conversion. An exception is that if the type is MutableMapping, immutable values are converted to dict.

If the type has nested types like Mapping[str, int], items are converted to those types automatically. This in new in Robot Framework 6.0.

Examples: {'a': 1, 'b': 2}, {'key': 1, 'nested': {'key': 2}}

typedocs.name: Media
typedocs.doc:
Changes the CSS media type of the page.

The only allowed values are 'screen', 'print' and null. Passing null disables CSS media emulation. Using False will not define media argument.

typedocs.name: MouseButton
typedocs.doc: Enum that defines which mouse button to use.

typedocs.name: MouseButtonAction
typedocs.doc: Enum that defines which Mouse Button action to perform.

typedocs.name: MultipartFields
typedocs.doc:
Fields of a multipart/form-data body, used by HTTP and Send API Request.

A dictionary of field names and values. A value is a text field or a file:

  • A string, a number or a boolean is a text field, sent like in FormFields.
  • A dictionary is a file, with either path or buffer:
Key Description
path Path of the file to send. A relative path is relative to the working directory of the Robot Framework process. The file name and mime type default to the file's name and the type its extension suggests.
buffer The file content as bytes. A string is sent encoded as UTF-8.
name The file name the server receives. Required with buffer.
mimeType The mime type of the file, e.g. image/png. Defaults to application/octet-stream with buffer.

These four keys are the only ones, spelled as here. Any other value, a dictionary with another key such as mimetype, or a file with both or none of path and buffer, fails before the request is sent. So does a string that only looks like a dictionary given for the whole argument; create the dictionaries with VAR or ${{ {...} }}.

A file from disk, a file made from text and a text field:

VAR    &{avatar} =    path=${CURDIR}/avatar.png
VAR    &{notes} =    name=notes.txt    mimeType=text/plain    buffer=Hello
VAR    &{fields} =    description=Profile picture    avatar=${avatar}    notes=${notes}
${response} =    Send API Request    /api/profile    POST    multipart=${fields}

The same with inline Python dictionaries:

${response} =    HTTP    /api/profile    POST
...    multipart=${{ {'description': 'Profile picture', 'avatar': {'path': 'avatar.png'}} }}

typedocs.name: NewPageDetails
typedocs.doc:
Return value of New Page keyword.

page_id is the UUID of the opened page. video_path path to the video or empty string if video is not created.

typedocs.name: None
typedocs.doc:
String NONE (case-insensitive) and the empty string are converted to the Python None object. Other values cause an error.

Converting the empty string is new in Robot Framework 7.4.
usages: Register Keyword To Run On Failure

typedocs.name: NotSet
typedocs.doc:
Defines a value that is not set.

This is used to differentiate between a value that is set to None and a value that is not set at all. Example ForcedColors has an options active, none and null. If user does not not want to give any of the ForcedColors options, user can use not_set value. Then keyword will not define ForcedColors option at all when underlying Playwright method(s) is called.

typedocs.name: PageLoadStates
typedocs.doc: Enum that defines available page load states.

typedocs.name: Path
typedocs.doc:

Examples: /tmp/absolute/path, relative/path/to/file.ext, name.txt

typedocs.doc:

Margins of the pdf.

typedocs.name: Permission
typedocs.doc:
Enum that defines the permission to grant to a context.

See grantPermissions(permissions) for more details.

typedocs.name: PlaywrightLogTypes
typedocs.doc:
Enable low level debug information from the playwright to playwright-log.txt file.

It is possible to disable the creation of playwright-log.txt totally. Mainly useful for the library developers and for debugging purposes. Will log everything as plain text, also including secrets. If playwright-log.txt file can not be deleted, time.time_ns() is added at the end of file name. Example playwright-log-12345.txt

disabled: playwright-log.txt is not created at all. All node side logging is lost. library: Default, only logging from Browser library node side is written to the playwright-log.txt file. playwright: Also includes Playwright log messages to the playwright-log.txt file. false: Same as library and for backwards compatability. true: Same as playwright and for backwards compatibility.

typedocs.name: Proxy
typedocs.doc:
Network proxy settings.

server Proxy to be used for all requests. HTTP and SOCKS proxies are supported, for example http://myproxy.com:3128 or socks5://myproxy.com:3128. Short form myproxy.com:3128 is considered an HTTP proxy.

bypass Optional coma-separated domains to bypass proxy, for example ".com, chromium.org, .domain.com".

username Optional username to use if HTTP proxy requires authentication.

password Optional password to use if HTTP proxy requires authentication.

typedocs.name: QueryParams
typedocs.doc:
Query parameters added to the URL of Send API Request: a dictionary or a string.

The parameters are appended to the query that the URL already has.

A dictionary of parameter names and values is checked like FormFields: a value is a string, a number or a boolean. Names and values are encoded completely, so they can hold any character, also &, =, + and %. Prefer a dictionary unless the query is already at hand as text.

VAR    &{params} =    q=rock & roll    page=${2}    exact=${True}
${response} =    Send API Request    /api/search?lang=en    params=${params}
# sends /api/search?lang=en&q=rock+%26+roll&page=2&exact=true

A string is appended as written; the string None adds no parameters. Characters that a URL cannot hold, such as a space, an umlaut or #, are encoded on the way. The characters that structure a query keep that meaning: & separates parameters, = separates a name from its value, + stands for a space and % starts an encoded character. Write them as %26, %3D, %2B and %25 to send them as text.

${response} =    Send API Request    /api/search    params=q=rock roll&page=2
# the server reads q = "rock roll" and page = "2"
${response} =    Send API Request    /api/search    params=q=rock %26 roll
# the server reads q = "rock & roll"; with a plain & it would read q = "rock " and " roll" = ""

typedocs.name: RecordHar
typedocs.doc:
Enables HAR recording for all pages into to a file.

If not specified, the HAR is not recorded. Make sure to await context to close for the HAR to be saved.

Key Description
path Path on the filesystem to write the HAR file to. A relative path is relative to the output directory.
content How response bodies are stored: embed stores them in the HAR, attach writes them as separate files next to the HAR, or into the archive when path ends with .zip, and omit leaves them out. Defaults to attach when path ends with .zip, otherwise to embed.
mode full (default) records everything. minimal records only what is needed to replay the HAR and leaves out sizes, timings, pages, cookies and security information.
urlFilter Records only the requests whose URL matches. A glob pattern, for example **/api/**, or a JavaScript RegExp enclosed in / with optional trailing flags, for example /api/v\d+/i. Such a value is always a RegExp, and an invalid one fails.
omitContent Leaves the response bodies out of the HAR. Default is False. Use content=omit instead.

mode=minimal with a urlFilter keeps the HAR small, for example to keep it in the repository as a test fixture.

Example:

${har} =    Create Dictionary     path=/path/to/har.file    omitContent=True
New Context    recordHar=${har}
New Context    recordHar={'path': 'login-api.har', 'mode': 'minimal', 'urlFilter': '**/api/**'}

typedocs.name: RecordVideo
typedocs.doc:
Enables Video recording

Key Description
dir Folder of the videos.
size ViewportDimensions of the videos.
fps Frame rate of the videos. Defaults to 25. Firefox and WebKit record at most 25 frames per second.
showActions Annotates the interacted elements in the videos, with the keys below.

Keys of showActions:

Key Description
duration How long each annotation is shown, in milliseconds. Defaults to 500.
position Position of the action title: top-left, top, top-right (default), bottom-left, bottom or bottom-right.
cursor pointer (default) shows a mouse pointer that moves from one action point to the next, none shows no cursor.
style CSS declarations of the annotations: point for the marker on the action point and highlight for the box over the element, both shown only when given, and title for the action title.

Examples:

 New Context  recordVideo={'dir':'videos', 'size':{'width':400, 'height':200}}
 New Context  recordVideo={'dir': 'd:/automation/video'}
 New Context  recordVideo={'showActions': {'position': 'bottom', 'style': {'title': 'font-size: 32px'}}}

typedocs.name: ReducedMotion
typedocs.doc:
Emulates 'prefers-reduced-motion' media feature.

Supported values are 'reduce', 'no-preference' and null. Passing null disables reduced motion emulation.

typedocs.name: ReduceMotion
typedocs.doc: Emulates prefers-reduced-motion media feature, supported values are reduce, no-preference.

typedocs.name: ReferrerPolicy
typedocs.doc:
How much of the referrer HTTP sends in the Referer header, the fetch referrerPolicy option.

The browser's default is strict-origin-when-cross-origin. See MDN Referrer-Policy for what each value sends.

typedocs.name: RegExp
typedocs.doc:
Create a (JavaScript) RegExp object from a string.

The matcher must start with a slash and end with a slash and can be followed by flags.

Example: /hello world/gi Which is equivalent to new RegExp("hello world", "gi") in JavaScript.

Following flags are supported:

Flag Description
g Global search.
i Case-insensitive search.
m Allows ^ and $ to match newline characters.
s Allows . to match newline characters.
u "unicode"; treat a pattern as a sequence of unicode code points.
y Perform a "sticky" search that matches starting at the current position in the target string.

See RegExp Object and RegExp Guide for more information.

typedocs.name: ReloadPages
typedocs.doc:
Defines which pages Set Storage State reloads while it restores the state.

Restoring a state file that contains IndexedDB does not finish while a page of the context holds an open connection to a database of that origin. To get around that, the pages are navigated to about:blank, the state is restored, and they are navigated back to the url they had before.

affected: Reloads the pages whose origin has IndexedDB in the state file. none: Reloads nothing. The keyword fails immediately when it detects an open connection which would block the restore. all: Reloads every page of the context.

typedocs.name: RequestMethod
typedocs.doc: Enum that defines the request type.

typedocs.name: Scale
typedocs.doc:
Enum that defines the scale of the screenshot.

When set to "css", screenshot will have a single pixel per each css pixel on the page. For high-dpi devices, this will keep screenshots small. Using "device" option will produce a single pixel per each device pixel, so screenshots of high-dpi devices will be twice as large or even larger.

typedocs.name: Scope
typedocs.doc:
Some keywords which manipulates library settings have a scope argument. With that scope argument one can set the "live time" of that setting. Available Scopes are: Global, Suite and Test / Task. Is a scope finished, this scoped setting, like timeout, will no longer be used and the previous higher scope setting applies again.

Live Times:

  • A Global scope will live forever until it is overwritten by another Global scope. Or locally temporarily overridden by a more narrow scope.
  • A Suite scope will locally override the Global scope and live until the end of the Suite within it is set, or if it is overwritten by a later setting with Global or same scope. Children suite does inherit the setting from the parent suite but also may have its own local Suite setting that then will be inherited to its children suites.
  • A Test or Task scope will be inherited from its parent suite but when set, lives until the end of that particular test or task.

A new set higher order scope will always remove the lower order scope which may be in charge. So the setting of a Suite scope from a test, will set that scope to the robot file suite where that test is and removes the Test scope that may have been in place.
usages: Register Keyword To Run On Failure

typedocs.name: ScreenshotFileTypes
typedocs.doc: Enum that defines available file types for screenshots.

typedocs.name: ScreenshotReturnType
typedocs.doc:
Enum that defines what Take Screenshot keyword returns.

  • path returns the path to the screenshot file as pathlib.Path object.
  • path_string returns the path to the screenshot file as string.
  • bytes returns the screenshot itself as bytes.
  • base64 returns the screenshot itself as base64 encoded string.

typedocs.name: ScrollBehavior
typedocs.doc:
Enum that controls the behavior of scrolling.

smooth

typedocs.name: ScrollPosition
typedocs.doc:
Scroll position of an element.

Key Description
top The amount of pixel between the top border of the page and the top border of visible area.
left The amount of pixel between the left border of the page and the left border of visible area.
bottom The amount of pixel between the top border of the page and the bottom border of visible area.
right The amount of pixel between the left border of the page and the right border of visible area.

typedocs.name: Secret
typedocs.doc:
Encapsulates secret values to avoid them being shown in Robot Framework logs.

The value is required to be robot.api.types.Secret object. These objects encapsulate confidential values so that they are not exposed in log files. How to create them is explained in the User Guide.

New in Robot Framework 7.4.

typedocs.name: SelectAttribute
typedocs.doc:
Enum that defines the attribute of an <option> element in a <select>-list.

This defines by what attribute an option is selected/chosen.

<select class="my_drop_down">
  <option value="0: Object">None</option>
  <option value="1: Object">Some</option>
  <option value="2: Object">Other</option>
</select>

value of the first option would be 0: Object.

label / text both defines the innerText which would be None for first element.

index 0 indexed number of an option. Would be 0 for the first element.

typedocs.name: SelectionStrategy
typedocs.doc:
SelectionStrategy to be used. Refers to Playwrights page.getBy*** functions. See Playwright Locators

AltText

All images should have an alt attribute that describes the image. You can locate an image based on the text alternative using page.getByAltText().

For example, consider the following DOM structure.

<img alt="playwright logo" src="/img/playwright-logo.svg" width="100" />

Label

Allows locating input elements by the text of the associated <label> or aria-labelledby element, or by the aria-label attribute.

For example, this method will find inputs by label "Username" and "Password" in the following DOM:

<input aria-label="Username">
<label for="password-input">Password:</label>
<input id="password-input">

Placeholder

Allows locating input elements by the placeholder text.

Example:

<input type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" />

TestId

Locate element by the test id.

Currently only the exact attribute data-testid is supported.

Example:

<button data-testid="directions">Itinéraire</button>

Text

Allows locating elements that contain given text.

Matching by text always normalizes whitespace, even with exact match. For example, it turns multiple spaces into one, turns line breaks into spaces and ignores leading and trailing whitespace. Input elements of the type button and submit are matched by their value instead of the text content. For example, locating by text "Log in" matches <input type=button value="Log in">.

Title

Allows locating elements by their title attribute.

Example:

<img alt="playwright logo" src="/img/playwright-logo.svg" title="Playwright" width="100" />

typedocs.name: SelectionType
typedocs.doc:
Enum that defines if the current id or all ids shall be returned.

ACTIVE / CURRENT defines to return only the id of the currently active instance of a Browser/Context/Page.

ALL / ANY defines to return ids of all instances.

typedocs.name: SelectOptions
typedocs.doc:
Dictionary with the following keys and their values "index", "value", "label" and "selected".

Keys Description
index 0 based index of the option.
value Value attribute of the option.
label Label/Text of the option.
selected Boolean if the option is selected.

typedocs.name: SelectorGenerator
typedocs.doc:
How Record Selector writes the selector of the picked element.

playwright: Playwright's own selector, the one its codegen and Record Keyword use: role, text, label, placeholder or test id where they identify the element, written in Browser selector syntax, for example role=button[name="Save"s].

css: A CSS selector built from ids, classes, attributes and the element's position, for example #login > div.form > button:nth-child(2). Frames are joined with >>> and open shadow roots with >>.

typedocs.name: ServiceWorkersPermissions
typedocs.doc:
Whether to allow sites to register Service workers.

allow: Service Workers can be registered.

block: Playwright will block all registration of Service Workers.

typedocs.name: SizeFields
typedocs.doc:
Enum that defines how the returned size is filtered.

ALL defines that the size is returned as a dictionary. {'width': <float>, 'height': <float>}.

width / height will return a single float value of the chosen dimension.

typedocs.name: string
typedocs.doc:
All arguments are converted to Unicode strings.

Most values are converted simply by using str(value). An exception is that bytes are mapped directly to Unicode code points with same ordinals. This means that, for example, b"hyv\xe4" becomes "hyvä".

Converting bytes specially is new Robot Framework 7.4.
usages: Register Keyword To Run On Failure

typedocs.name: SupportedBrowsers
typedocs.doc:
Defines which browser shall be started.

Browser Browser with this engine
chromium Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge (since 2020), Opera
firefox Mozilla Firefox
webkit Apple Safari, Mail, AppStore on MacOS and iOS

Since Playwright comes with a pack of builtin binaries for all browsers, no additional drivers e.g. geckodriver are needed.

All these browsers that cover more than 85% of the world wide used browsers, can be tested on Windows, Linux and MacOS. Theres is not need for dedicated machines anymore.

typedocs.name: TextType
typedocs.doc:
Defines which Playwright method is used to get the text of an element.

allInnerTexts: Returns a list of node.innerText values for all matching nodes.

allTextContents: Returns a list of node.textContent values for all matching nodes.

innerText: Returns the element node.innerText value, which represents the rendered text content of a node and its descendants.

inputValue: Returns the value for the matching <input> or <textarea> or <select> element.

innerHTML: Returns the element node.innerHTML value, which is the HTML markup contained within the element, omitting any shadow roots.

typedocs.name: timedelta
typedocs.doc:
Strings are expected to represent a time interval in one of the time formats Robot Framework supports:

  • a number representing seconds like 42 or 10.5
  • a time string like 1 hour 2 seconds or 1h 2s
  • a "timer" string like 01:02 (1 minute 2 seconds) or 01:00:03 (1 hour 3 seconds)

Integers and floats are considered to be seconds.

See the Robot Framework User Guide for more details about the supported time formats.

typedocs.name: TracingGroupMode
typedocs.doc:
Defines in what detail level keywords are written to Playwright trace.

Playwrright trace is a full log of all playwright actions and events that happen in the browser during the test run. This includes all API calls, events, logs, network requests, and responses as well as the DOM at every moment during execution. This trace can be activated with the tracing parameter of New Context keyword.

  • Full All keyword calls that run are written to trace as groups even if they do not call Browser keywords. Keywords in IF, TRY or other branches that do not run get no group.
  • Browser Just Browser library keywords are written to the logs as groups.
  • Playwright No additional keywords are logged, just the Playwright API calls.

A keyword goes only to the traces of the contexts it acts on, and a keyword that acts on no context, like Log, goes to the trace of the context active when it ends. See Traces.

A group is named after the keyword call with the values of its arguments, so Get Text id=a == ${tag} shows the value of ${tag}. A value longer than 200 characters is cut, as in the Robot Framework log. Inline Python, like ${{ $x + 1 }}, and extended variable syntax, like ${x.upper()}, stay as written, because showing their value would run them a second time. The secret arguments of keywords like Fill Secret show as ***, and the other arguments of those keywords stay as written. A Secret variable shows as <secret>.

typedocs.name: tuple
typedocs.doc:
Strings must be Python tuple or list literals. They are converted using the ast.literal_eval function and possible lists converted further to tuples. They can contain any values ast.literal_eval supports, including tuples and other collections.

If the argument is a tuple, it is used without conversion. Lists and other sequences are converted to tuples.

If the type has nested types like tuple[str, int, int], items are converted to those types automatically.

Examples: ('one', 'two'), (('one', 1), ('two', 2))

Support to convert nested types is new in Robot Framework 6.0. Support for list literals is new in Robot Framework 7.4.

typedocs.name: ViewportDimensions
typedocs.doc:
Viewport dimensions.

Viewport is the browsers inner window size that is used to display the page.

Key Description
width page width in pixels.
height page height in pixels.
